=== NOTES 1:79 | Eastern Chalukya Administration, Society and Religious Conditions
## SUB 0 | Court Artists and Scholars – Chellavva and Ugradityacharya
[79:0:0] # Chellavva – the most-asked person of this row
[79:0:1] - **Who:** **Chellavva (Challavva / Chellava)** – court **singer and dancer** of **Chalukya Bhima I** (G2 2011 ×2; APPSC PYQ).
[79:0:2] - **Titles:** **Gandharva-Vidya-Visarada** (G2 Mains 2019 ×2; APPSC PYQ ×2) and **Samasta Gandharva Vidya Kovida**.
[79:0:3] - **Reward:** Bhima I gave her the village **Attili** (Attili inscription) and two kandikas of land.
[79:0:4] - **Father:** **Mallappa**, a renowned musician, compared to **Tumburu** in the Attili inscription.
[79:0:5] - **⚠ Trap:** patron = **Chalukya Bhima I**, not Gunaga Vijayaditya, Rajaraja Narendra or the Rashtrakuta Amoghavarsha.
[79:0:6] - **⚠ Trap:** in the "who got the title" options, **Mallappa** (her father), **Chamekamba** (courtesan of Ammaraja II's time) and **Bhattadeva** (court poet) are distractors.
[79:0:7] # Other scholars and their works
[79:0:8] TABLE head: Person | Work / title | Patron or place
  [79:0:8.0] Ugradityacharya | Kalyanakaraka – a Jain medical (Ayurveda) treatise on diagnosis and treatment | Jain scholar of Ramatirtha
  [79:0:8.1] Bhattavamana | Kavyalankara Sutras; title Kavi Vrishabha | Chalukya Bhima I
  [79:0:8.2] Bhattudeva | Title Kavichakravarti | Ammaraja II
  [79:0:8.3] Pavuluri Mallana | Ganitasara Sangraham (Telugu mathematics); got Navakhandavada | Rajaraja Narendra
[79:0:9] - **Kalyanakaraka = Ugradityacharya** (G2 2012, 2019; APPSC PYQ ×3); Somadeva Suri, Padmaprabha Maladhari Deva and Revana Siddha are distractors.
[79:0:10] # Royal patrons → literary title
[79:0:11] TABLE head: Ruler | Title
  [79:0:11.0] Vishnuvardhana III | Kavi Pandita Kamadhenu
  [79:0:11.1] Ammaraja II | Kavigayaka Kalpataru
  [79:0:11.2] Rajaraja Narendra | Kavyageetha Priyudu
[79:0:12] # Music and dance
[79:0:13] - **Hallisaka = Kolatam:** the popular dance of the period; music and dance were held in courts and temples.
[79:0:14] - **Bhairavakona** (Nallamala hills, **Prakasam**): **eight rock-cut Shiva cave temples** (7th–8th c.), a central seat of Shaivism; sculptures of musical instruments.
[79:0:15] - **Panchadarla** (Dharapalem, **Anakapalli**): **Uma Dharmalingeswara** temple with Eastern Chalukya and 15th-century inscriptions; ASI recorded **17** in 1899 (in news Aug 2026).
[79:0:16] ~~ Sources: NextGen Eastern Chalukyas p.15, p.17, p.27, p.30; NextGen AP History Previous Papers p.13; Rocket AP History sheet #44; app notes 1:79 (sub 6, 7)
## SUB 1 | Religion – Sects, Agamas and the Chalukya Mother Goddess
[79:1:0] # Family goddess
[79:1:1] - **Mother goddess of the early Chalukyas:** **Hariti** – the Chalukyas called themselves **Hariti-putras** of the **Manavya gotra**, nourished by the **Seven Mothers** (Saptamatrikas) (G2 2019).
[79:1:2]   - **⚠ Settled:** the printed key "Cushmandini" is wrong – **Kushmandini** is a **Jain yakshi**; Rocket and the Chalukya prasastis give **Hariti**.
[79:1:3] - **Same goddess, other dynasty:** Hariti was also the tutelary deity of the **Ikshvakus**; the metronymic "Hariti-putra" suggests a southern origin of the Eastern Chalukyas.
[79:1:4] # Shaivism and Vaishnavism
[79:1:5] - **Shaivism dominant:** sects **Pasupata** (founder **Lakulisha**, oldest, peaceful), **Kalamukha** (extremist) and **Kapalika** (Bhairava worship).
[79:1:6] - **Trilinga desa:** Draksharama, Kaleshwaram and Srisailam; Srisailam was called a Kapalika kshetra by Bhavabhuti.
[79:1:7] - **Vaishnava kings:** **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** (Kunti Madhava temple, Pithapuram) and **Danarnava** (Mandavya Narayana temple, Samalkot).
[79:1:8] - **Jayasimha I** performed the **Ashvamedha**; royal prasastis boast of many Ashvamedhas.
[79:1:9] - **Jayasimha II** brought the **Koya Kottalu** (Boya Kottas) into the Brahmanical fold.
[79:1:10] # Agamas and saint traditions
[79:1:11] TABLE head: Tradition | Faith | Point
  [79:1:11.0] Pancharatra | Vaishnava | Common to Ramanuja and Madhva (APPSC Endowment 2022)
  [79:1:11.1] Vaikhanasa | Vaishnava | Founded by Vikhanasa; followed at Srivari temple, Tirumala (APPSC Endowment 2022)
  [79:1:11.2] Nayanars | Saiva | 63 Tamil Shiva saints (Alvars = Vaishnava) (APPSC Endowment 2022)
[79:1:12] - **⚠ Trap:** Pancharatra and Vaikhanasa are **Vaishnava**, not Shaiva or Shakta.
[79:1:13] # Buddhism
[79:1:14] - **Declining:** Buddharamas became Shaiva temples (Dhanyakataka → Amareswara); Hiuen Tsang (639) found Buddhist sites decaying; survived at **Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda**.
[79:1:15] ~~ Sources: Rocket AP History sheet #7; NextGen Eastern Chalukyas p.7, p.27-29; NextGen Post-Kakatiyas p.13; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalukya_dynasty; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaikhanasa; app notes 1:79 (sub 3)
## SUB 2 | Administration – Offices, Nadus and Taxes
[79:2:0] # Structure
[79:2:1] - **State theory:** the **Saptanga** idea (seven limbs); king autocratic, succession to the eldest son; official language **Sanskrit**.
[79:2:2] - **Ashtadasa Tirthas** = **eighteen administrative offices**.
[79:2:3] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [79:2:3.0] Tirthulu | Council of ministers; Samaharta = its chief
  [79:2:3.1] Vishaya / Mandala | Province under a Vishayapati / Mandaleswara
  [79:2:3.2] Kottam | Another territorial subdivision
  [79:2:3.3] Grameyaka / Gramani / Urgavunda | Village head
  [79:2:3.4] Rattodi (Rattadi) | Chief village officer
  [79:2:3.5] Vanneyus (Manneyus) | Toll collectors
  [79:2:3.6] Sthanadhipati | Officer managing temples and their endowments
  [79:2:3.7] Pradvivaka | King's adviser on judicial matters; verdicts = jayapatras with the royal seal
  [79:2:3.8] Talari | Village watchman; paid the value of goods if the thief was not caught
[79:2:4] # Nadus → region
[79:2:5] TABLE head: Nadu | Region
  [79:2:5.0] Pakanadu | Nellore (asked 2002)
  [79:2:5.1] Palnadu | Macharla, Gurajala
  [79:2:5.2] Kammanadu | Bapatla, Ongole, Narasaraopet
  [79:2:5.3] Venginadu | Krishna and Godavari
[79:2:6] - **Capitals:** Pithapuram → **Vengi** (Jayasimha I) → **Rajamahendravaram** (Ammaraja I).
[79:2:7] # Taxes
[79:2:8] - **Land tax:** **1/6** of the produce, called **Koru / Aripannu / Siddhaya**; tax-free land = **Sarva Kara Pariharam**.
[79:2:9] - **Udranga:** in epigraphy the **fixed or principal land tax** (tax on permanent tenants), paired with **uparikara** (minor taxes) – D.C. Sircar.
[79:2:10]   - **⚠ Settled:** "Udranga = tax on water" (old app key) has no source support; a PYQ offering only tolls / salt / water / shop tax has no correct option.
[79:2:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen Eastern Chalukyas p.4-5, p.22-24; D.C. Sircar, Indian Epigraphical Glossary p.349 (https://sanskrit-lexicon.uni-koeln.de/scans/IEGScan/IEGScanpdf/pg_349.pdf); app notes 1:79 (sub 0)
## SUB 3 | Society, Economy and Guilds
[79:3:0] # Society
[79:3:1] - **Varna order** with Brahmin privilege; Brahmins split into **Vaidikas** and **Niyogis** (administration and army).
[79:3:2] - **Agraharas:** tax-free villages for Brahmins, who performed **Hiranyagarbha** and **Bahusuvarna** rituals.
[79:3:3] - **Vaisyas = Komatis**; their guilds = **Nakarams**; Reddy, Kamma and Kapu communities grew strong.
[79:3:4] - **Panchanamvaru:** five artisan groups (blacksmith, goldsmith, brazier, carpenter, sculptor) appear as an organised body.
[79:3:5] - **Panduranga** (general of Gunaga Vijayaditya) **subdued the Boyas**, built Pandurangapuram on Pulicat lake and issued the Addanki verse inscription.
[79:3:6] # Guilds and trade
[79:3:7] - **Penugonda (West Godavari)** = **headquarters of the merchant guilds** of medieval Andhra and main seat of goddess **Vasavi** (APPSC PYQ).
[79:3:8]   - Bejawada was a trade centre but not the guild headquarters.
[79:3:9] - **Kakumanu inscription** (Chalukya Bhima I) names a **Setti Shreshthi** (chief merchant).
[79:3:10] TABLE head: Fact | Ruler
  [79:3:10.0] Gold coins found in Arakan (Burma) | Saktivarma I (Chalukya Chandra)
  [79:3:10.1] Trade with the eastern islands | Rajaraja Narendra
  [79:3:10.2] 72 merchants sent to China | Kulottunga I
[79:3:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen Eastern Chalukyas p.5, p.25-26; NextGen AP History Previous Papers p.13, p.27; app notes 1:79 (sub 1, 2)
## SUB 4 | Jainism – Basadis and Grants
[79:4:0] TABLE head: Site / grant | Donor
  [79:4:0.0] Nedumba Vasati, Vijayawada; Mushinikonda village for it | Queen Ayyana Mahadevi, wife of Kubja Vishnuvardhana
  [79:4:0.1] Mushikonda village to the Jains | Vishnuvardhana III
  [79:4:0.2] Kaluchumbarru grant to Arhanandi | Ammaraja II, at the request of Chamekamba
  [79:4:0.3] Maliyapundi grant to the Jinalaya at Dharmavaram | Ammaraja II, at the request of vassal Durgaraja
  [79:4:0.4] Ramakonda cave, Ramatirtham (Vizianagaram) | Vimaladitya, for his guru Trikala Yogi Siddhanta Deva
[79:4:1] - **Only Jain king** of the dynasty: **Vimaladitya**.
[79:4:2] - **Potlacheruvu** = the leading **Jain** centre (G2 2017 key); its persecution by Kalamukhas and Virashaivas came later, in the **Kakatiya age**.
[79:4:3] - **Migration:** under Brahmanical pressure Jains moved to **Karnataka**, among them the family of **Basaveshwara**.
[79:4:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen Eastern Chalukyas p.19, p.27, p.30; NextGen Kakatiyas (Brahmaya destroyed Jain residences at Potlacheru); app notes 1:79 (sub 3, 4)
## SUB 5 | Education – Ghatikas
[79:5:0] - **Ghatikas** = advanced **Sanskrit schools** attached to **agraharas or temples**.
[79:5:1] - **Heads:** **Ghatika Samanyulu**, e.g. **Mandasharma** of the **Asanapura Ghatika**, Kammanadu.
[79:5:2] - **Subjects:** Vedas, Vedangas, Dharmashastras, Tarka, Vyakarana, Arthashastra, **Dhanurveda**, **Ayurveda**.
[79:5:3] - **⚠ Trap:** **Hallisaka** (a dance) was **not** a Ghatika subject.
[79:5:4] - **Jain pupils** began their studies with **"Om Namah Siddham"**.
[79:5:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen Eastern Chalukyas p.10, p.30; app notes 1:79 (sub 5)

=== NOTES 1:80 | Eastern Chalukya Art and Architecture – Biccavolu, Draksharama and Samalkot Temples
## SUB 0 | Chalukya Bhima I – Pancharamas and the Twin Bhimeswara Temples
[80:0:0] # The builder
[80:0:1] - **Chalukya Bhima I** (892-922): fought **360 battles** (Pithapuram inscription of Mallapadeva) and is said to have built **360 temples**; "the Vengi ruler who built many temples" (APPSC PYQ).
[80:0:2] - **Pancharamas built by:** **Chalukya Bhima I**, i.e. under the **Vengi (Eastern) Chalukyas** (APPSC PYQ ×2) – not Kubja Vishnuvardhana, Pulakesin II, Rajaraja Narendra, Kakatiyas or Vijayanagara.
[80:0:3] - **Draksharama founder:** **Chalukya Bhima I** built the **Bhimeswara** temple (G2 1993); an **Eastern Chalukya** monument, not Pallava or Satavahana.
[80:0:4] - **Twin temples:** **Draksharama Bhimeswara** and **Kumararama Bhimeswara at Samalkot**, the latter in memory of his **son**.
[80:0:5] # The five Pancharamas
[80:0:6] TABLE head: Rama | Place | District (old) | District (after 2022)
  [80:0:6.0] Draksharama (Bhimeswara) | Draksharama | East Godavari | Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema
  [80:0:6.1] Kumararama | Samalkot = Chalukya Bhimavaram | East Godavari | Kakinada
  [80:0:6.2] Somarama | Gunupudi, Bhimavaram | West Godavari | West Godavari
  [80:0:6.3] Ksheerarama | Palakollu | West Godavari | West Godavari
  [80:0:6.4] Amararama | Amaravati | Guntur | Palnadu
[80:0:7] - **Amaravati is a Pancharama** (G1 1991), not a Shakti Peetha.
[80:0:8] - **Not a Pancharama:** **Simhachalam** (a Narasimha shrine) (MPDO 1997); Chalukya Bhimavaram is one.
[80:0:9] - **Chalukya Bhimavaram = Samalkot (Samarlakota)** (Welfare Officers 2017) – not Pithapuram, Draksharama or Gudipudi.
[80:0:10] - **All are two-storeyed except Ksheerarama**; four lie in the Godavari delta, **Amararama** on the **Krishna**.
[80:0:11] - **Literary sources:** **Skanda Purana** and **Srinatha's Bhimeswara Puranam**.
[80:0:12] # Draksharama vs Samalkot
[80:0:13] TABLE head: Feature | Draksharama | Samalkot
  [80:0:13.0] Name | Bhimeswara | Kumararama / Kumara Bhimeswara
  [80:0:13.1] Plan | Two-storeyed shrine, massive lingam | Two-storeyed, closely similar; black-granite lingam
  [80:0:13.2] Extras | Huge Nandi mandapa; one of the Trilinga kshetras | Towering gopuram added later
  [80:0:13.3] Later work | Renovated by the Reddis | Renovated by the Reddis
[80:0:14] - **Sapta Godavari:** the sacred tank (**pushkarini**) of the **Draksharama Bhimeswara** temple; legend says the Seven Sages brought its water, used for the abhisheka (Welfare Officers PYQ).
[80:0:15] - **Jananathapura:** Draksharama was also the provincial capital and coronation seat of the Chalukya-Chola viceroys of Vengi.
[80:0:16] ~~ Sources: NextGen Eastern Chalukyas p.3, p.14, p.28, p.31; Rocket AP History sheet #18; app notes 1:80 (sub 3, 5)
## SUB 1 | Other Temple Builders – Vijayaditya II, Bikkavolu and Rajahmundry
[80:1:0] # Vijayaditya II – 108 temples
[80:1:1] - **Vijayaditya II (Narendra Mrigaraja):** fought **108 battles in 12 years** against the Rashtrakutas (**Govinda III, Amoghavarsha I**) and their Gangavadi allies.
[80:1:2] - **108 Shiva temples** (**Narendreswara / Narendra Mrigeswara**) at the battle sites – recorded in the **Sataluru** inscription (G2 2008, 2012, 2019; statement a of G2 2025 ✓).
[80:1:3] - **⚠ Trap:** the source is **Sataluru**, not Kopparam (a Pulakesin II record).
[80:1:4] # Bikkavolu (Biccavolu) group
[80:1:5] - **Old name:** **Birudankaprolu = Bikkavolu** (East Godavari), after Gunaga Vijayaditya's title **Birudankabhima** (Welfare Officers 2017; APPSC PYQ).
[80:1:6] - **Builder:** **Gunaga Vijayaditya III** (848-892) – **Golingeswara, Rajarajeswara (Raja Raja), Chandrasekhara, Mukteswara, Vijayeswara**.
[80:1:7] - **Golingeswara** = the only one still standing; **Vijayeswara** has carved **Ganga and Yamuna** figures.
[80:1:8] - **⚠ Settled:** "**Rajaraja Narendra** built the Rajarajeswara temple at Biccavole" is the **incorrect** statement (G2 Mains 2025 key: "b only").
[80:1:9]   - NextGen p.20 credits Rajaraja Narendra with a temple at Bikkavolu; the ASI attributes the whole group to Gunaga Vijayaditya III.
[80:1:10] # Temples → builder
[80:1:11] TABLE head: Temple | Place | Builder
  [80:1:11.0] Kunti Madhava | Pithapuram | Kubja Vishnuvardhana
  [80:1:11.1] Kumaraswamy | Chebrolu | Chalukya Bhima I
  [80:1:11.2] Parvateswara, Indrakeeladri | Bezawada | Bhattupu, commander of Bhima I
  [80:1:11.3] Mandavya Narayana (Raja Narayana) | Samalkot | Danarnava
  [80:1:11.4] Kotilingala, Markandeya, Vishnu | Rajahmundry | Rajaraja Narendra
[80:1:12] - **Pedda Masjid:** the Rajahmundry **Vishnu temple** became a mosque under the **Tughlaqs**.
[80:1:13] - **Rajahmundry:** built as capital by **Ammaraja I (Rajamahendra)**; "cultural capital of the Andhras".
[80:1:14] ~~ Sources: NextGen Eastern Chalukyas p.12-13, p.20, p.31; ASI, Gollingeswara Group of Temples, Biccavolu (https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/education/archaeological-survey-of-india/gollingeswara-group-of-temples,-east-godavari,-andhra-pradesh); Rocket AP History sheet #18, #36; app notes 1:80 (sub 1, 2, 4)
## SUB 2 | Vengi School and the Chalukya-Chola Style
[80:2:0] - **Vengi School:** mainly **Dravida** temples – **Pallava (Kanchi) + Badami Chalukya** influences with **local Andhra** features; local laterite and limestone; concentrated in the **Krishna-Godavari delta**.
[80:2:1] - **Vesara (Chalukya) style:** NextGen defines it as **Dravidian vimana + Buddhist** art; it belongs to the **Badami Chalukyas** and was brought into Andhra by the Vengi Chalukyas.
[80:2:2] - **Navabrahma temples (nine), Alampur:** **Badami Chalukyas**, 7th–8th c. – not Eastern Chalukyas.
[80:2:3] - **Chalukya-Chola model:** the **Draksharama Bhimeswara** temple blends **Pallava + early Chalukya** features into an independent style (G2 Mains 2025).
[80:2:4] TABLE head: Temple | Style
  [80:2:4.0] Draksharama Bhimeswara | Chalukya-Chola (Eastern Chalukya)
  [80:2:4.1] Brihadeeswara, Thanjavur | Imperial Chola
  [80:2:4.2] Padmakshi, Hanamkonda | Kakatiya
  [80:2:4.3] Lepakshi | Vijayanagara
[80:2:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen Eastern Chalukyas p.6, p.30; NextGen AP History Previous Papers p.17; app notes 1:80 (sub 0)
## SUB 3 | Jain Foundations of the Period
[80:3:0] TABLE head: Site | Foundation | Royal patron
  [80:3:0.0] Vijayawada | Nedumba Vasati | Queen Ayyana Mahadevi
  [80:3:0.1] Ramatirtham | Ramakonda cave for guru Trikala Yogi Siddhanta Deva | Vimaladitya
  [80:3:0.2] Mushikonda | Village granted to the Jains | Vishnuvardhana III
  [80:3:0.3] Kaluchumbarru | Grant at the request of Chamekamba | Ammaraja II
[80:3:1] - **Leading Jain centre:** **Potlacheruvu**.
[80:3:2] ~~ Sources: NextGen Eastern Chalukyas p.19, p.27; app notes 1:80 (sub 6)

=== NOTES 1:83 | Minor Dynasties of Andhradesa – Chalukya-cholas, Kona Haihayas, Matsyas, Pusapati and Others
## SUB 0 | Palnadu War (Palnati Yuddham), 1182
[83:0:0] - **Where and when:** **Karempudi, 1182 CE** (Rocket); epic **Palnati Veera Charitra** by **Srinatha**; also the folk **Palnati Veerula Katha**.
[83:0:1] - **Rivals:** all sons of the Palnadu Haihaya **Alugaraju (Anugaraju)** – Nalagamaraju's faction vs the Malideva faction.
[83:0:2] TABLE head: Person | Role
  [83:0:2.0] Nalagamaraju | Son of Mailama Devi, daughter of Velanati Gonka II
  [83:0:2.1] Malideva and brothers | Half-brothers – rival faction, led by Brahmanaidu
  [83:0:2.2] Nayakuralu Nagamma | Nalagama's minister; Shaivite; built the Veerabhadra temple, Gurajala; her intrigue exiled Malideva and Brahmanaidu
  [83:0:2.3] Brahmanaidu | Minister of Malideva; Vira Vaishnava reformer
  [83:0:2.4] Balachandra | Brahmanaidu's son; hero killed in the war
[83:0:3] - **Cause of the war:** **Nagamma** – the rivalry of Nayakuralu Nagamma and Brahmanaidu (APPSC PYQ); Balachandra was a hero, not the cause.
[83:0:4] - **Brahmanaidu's faith:** follower of **Ramanujacharya** (Vira Vaishnavism) (APPSC PYQ).
[83:0:5] - **Dalit temple entry:** **Brahma Naidu** opened the **Chennakesava temple, Macherla** to all castes, including Dalits (APPSC PYQ).
[83:0:6] - **Chapa Koodu / Dasa Samaj:** his inter-caste dining; his followers became the **Maladasari** (dasa) community.
[83:0:7] - **Karempudi angle (G2 PYQ):** the **Velamas**, "intruders" into the Reddi-dominated economic life of Palnadu, were driven out in the **Battle of Karempudi**.
[83:0:8] - **Allies:** **Kota Bhimaraju II** joined Kakatiya **Rudradeva** to back Nalagamaraju.
[83:0:9] ~~ Sources: Rocket AP History sheet #12, #19; NextGen Kakatiyas (Rudradeva backed Nalagamaraju); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Palnadu; app notes 1:83 (sub 4)
## SUB 1 | Velanati Chodas
[83:1:0] - **Seat:** **Velanadu** (Bapatla, Tenali, Repalle, Guntur); capital **Chandavolu (Dhanadapuram)**.
[83:1:1] - **Line:** progenitor **Mallavarma**; founder **Gonka I** (Samasta Senadhipati of Vengi under the Chalukya-Cholas); greatest **Gonka II** (1132-1161).
[83:1:2] - **Origin:** not Telugu Chodas – ancestors were the **Kirtipura lords of Madhyadesha**; they named sons after their Chalukya-Chola overlords (first: **Rajendra Choda**).
[83:1:3] - **Pithapuram inscription** of Velanati **Prithvisvara** names **Kolleru Lake** (G2 Mains 2017; G2 PYQ) – not Chilka, Pulicat or Pakala.
[83:1:4] - **End:** Kakatiya **Ganapatideva** (1201 campaign) killed **Prithvisvara**, with Nellore Choda Tikkana's help, and later the last member **Mummadi Rajendra Choda**.
[83:1:5] # Marriage alliances
[83:1:6] - **Mailama (Mailamba)**, daughter of **Gonka II**, was married to the Palnadu Haihaya **Anugaraju**, who ruled Palnadu from **Gurajala** with Velanati support.
[83:1:7] - The **Kondapadumatis** were also tied to Velanadu by marriage.
[83:1:8] > Statement angle (NTR Univ. JA): "Rajendra Choda, son of Gonka II, married Mailamba, daughter of Gonkaraja" ✗ (Mailamba was his sister, married to Anugaraju); "Anama, sister of Buddharaja, married the Haihaya chief of Palnadu" – not in the sources → key "neither A nor B".
[83:1:9] ~~ Sources: NextGen Kakatiyas (Ganapati's Velanati campaign, Prithvisvara); NextGen AP History Previous Papers p.8; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Palnadu; app notes 1:83 (sub 1, 2)
## SUB 2 | Kulottunga I and the Chalukya-Chola Viceroys of Vengi
[83:2:0] - **Kulottunga I (Rajendra Chalukya)**, son of Rajaraja Narendra and Ammanga Devi, = **first Chalukya-Chola king**: Chola throne **1070**, Vengi **1075** after the death of **Vijayaditya VII**, the last Eastern Chalukya → he **united the Chola and Eastern Chalukya crowns** (G1 1983-84).
[83:2:1] - **Married** **Madhurantaki**, daughter of the Chola **Rajendra**.
[83:2:2] - **Deeds:** sent **72 merchants to China**; built **Kulottunga Cholapuram** (Visakhapatnam); conquered **Kalinga by sea** → **Kalingattuparani** by **Jayangondar**.
[83:2:3] # Viceroys
[83:2:4] - **Titles taken:** the Eastern Chalukya **Sarvalokasraya, Sri Vishnuvardhana**; coronation at **Jananathapura (Draksharama)**, the provincial capital of Vengi.
[83:2:5] - **Viceroy crowned at Draksharama:** **Rajaraja Chodaganga** (G2 Mains 2025 key).
[83:2:6]   - The Chellur plates show Kulottunga's son **Vira Choda** also styled Vishnuvardhana; he is not an option.
[83:2:7] - **Vikrama Chola** served after Rajaraja Chodaganga and was recalled in **1118** as his father's **co-regent**; the line ended with **Parantaka Chola**.
[83:2:8] - **After Kulottunga:** Andhra became a web of **nadus** under vassals who accepted **Velanadu**, later **Kakatiya**, overlordship; he raised Velanati, Nellore, Konidena and Pottapi Chodas, Chagis and Kona Haihayas as Mandaleswaras.
[83:2:9] ~~ Sources: NextGen Eastern Chalukyas p.21-22; NextGen AP History Previous Papers p.46; Rocket AP History sheet #1; SII Vol 1, Chellur plates of Vira Choda (https://www.whatisindia.com/inscriptions/south_indian_inscriptions/volume_1/vira_choda.html); app notes 1:83 (sub 0)
## SUB 3 | Minor Dynasties – Region and Seat
[83:3:0] TABLE head: Dynasty | Region | Seat | Key point
  [83:3:0.0] Kona Haihayas | Konaseema | Rakuduru | Progenitor Kirti Varma
  [83:3:0.1] Palnadu Haihayas | Palnadu | Gurajala | Claimed descent from Kartavirya Arjuna; founder Betaraju I (Satrasala inscription)
  [83:3:0.2] Gona Haihayas | South Telangana | Vardhamanapuram | –
  [83:3:0.3] Kota kings | Kammanadu (Amaravati to Tripurantakam) | Dhanyakatakam | Founder Betaraju I; Bhimaraju I (1108-27) Kalinga campaigns
  [83:3:0.4] Chagis | Natavadi and Vijayavati vishayas | Gudimetta (also Vinukonda) | Overlords: Chalukya-Cholas → Kakatiyas → Gajapatis
  [83:3:0.5] Matsyas of Oddadi | Upland Srikakulam–Vizianagaram | Oddadi | Claimed descent from a fish; emblem double fish; founder Satyamartanda married Prabhavati, daughter of Jayatsena of Utkala
  [83:3:0.6] Bana kings | Rayalaseema | Parivipuram (Hindupur) | Descent from Bali
  [83:3:0.7] Vatsavayis | Peddapuram | Peddapuram | Ruled Peddapuram for about three centuries (APPSC PYQ)
  [83:3:0.8] Pusapatis | Vizianagaram | Vizianagaram | Gajapati Vijayarama
[83:3:1] - **Kota overlords:** **Chalukya-Cholas → Velanati Chodas → Kakatiyas**; a Kota chief married **Ganapamba**, daughter of Ganapatideva.
[83:3:2] - **Melambika**, Ganapatideva's sister, married into the **Chagi** family.
[83:3:3] - **Matsyas:** ruled c. 1200–1470; replaced by the **Pusapati** and **Madgole** zamindaris (Madgole claim Matsya descent).
[83:3:4] - **Pusapatis:** Raja **Vijayarama Raju** was killed fighting the East India Company at **Padmanabham (10 July 1794)**; Vizianagaram became a zamindari under the **Permanent Settlement (1802)**.
[83:3:5] - **Taruvariyur inscription** praises Nellore Choda **Manumasiddhi I** as a thunderbolt to his enemies.
[83:3:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen Andhra Cholas p.8; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peddapuram; app notes 1:83 (sub 1, 3, 5, 6)

=== NOTES 1:86 | Chola Local Self-government – Uttaramerur Inscriptions, Ur, Sabha, Nagaram, Variyams
## SUB 0 | Village Autonomy – the Chola Hallmark
[86:0:0] - **Special feature of Chola polity:** **autonomy of village administration** / autonomous village panchayats (UPPSC 1995; CDS 2000) – not mandalam divisions, monarchy, ministers or tax methods.
[86:0:1] - **Famous for:** **village assemblies** (RAS 1993); **excellent village administration** (UPPSC 1991); **elaborate local self-government** (State PSC) – the **Cholas**, not the Chalukyas, Cheras, Solankis or Parmars.
[86:0:2] - **Early Panchayati Raj:** "Chola village administration was an early example of the Panchayati Raj system" – autonomous elected village bodies evolved by the **Dravidians (Cholas)** (RAS 1997).
[86:0:3] - **Real powers:** the sabha, ur and nagaram were **elected bodies with real powers** over revenue, irrigation, temples and justice – not symbolic councils.
[86:0:4] - **Nature of the gram sabhas (Degree Lecturers 2011):** fully **autonomous**, **helped the public** (tanks, roads, justice) and acted as **bankers and trustees** (raised loans, held endowments) → **all of the above**.
[86:0:5] - **Historians:** K.A. **Nilakanta Sastri** – a remarkable "grassroots democracy"; **Burton Stein** – a **segmentary state**.
[86:0:6] TABLE head: Dynasty | Local government
  [86:0:6.0] Cholas | Culmination: elected assemblies, committees, lottery
  [86:0:6.1] Pallavas | Sabha and ur already appear – the base the Cholas built on
  [86:0:6.2] Badami Chalukyas | Highly centralised
  [86:0:6.3] Rashtrakutas | Village assemblies active in disputes
[86:0:7] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval India p.407, p.413; NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 3 p.204; app notes 1:86 (sub 0)
## SUB 1 | Uttaramerur Inscriptions
[86:1:0] - **What:** two inscriptions on the temple walls at **Uttaramerur**, a **brahmadeya** village in **Kanchipuram district**, Tamil Nadu.
[86:1:1] - **Date and king:** **919 and 921 CE** (c. 920), reign of **Parantaka I** – not Rajaraja I.
[86:1:2] - **Source of Chola local government:** Uttaramerur (APPSC G2 2000, 2003; APPSC PYQ ×3; IAS 1993; APPSC G1) – not Kudumiyanmalai, Gangaikondacholapuram, Kanchipuram, Thanjavur, Uraiyur, Silappadikaram, Tolkappiyam or Periya Puranam.
[86:1:3] - **Contents:** constitution of the sabha, **qualifications**, **disqualifications**, mode of election (**kudavolai**), committees, functions and the **right to recall**.
[86:1:4] - **⚠ Trap:** the **Thanjavur** inscription of Rajaraja I records military feats (Chera navy at Kandalur), not village government.
[86:1:5] # Qualifications and disqualifications
[86:1:6] TABLE head: Qualifications | Disqualifications
  [86:1:6.0] Own at least 1/4 veli of tax-paying land | Failed to submit accounts
  [86:1:6.1] Own a house (residence) on own site | Committed sins / crimes, alcoholism
  [86:1:6.2] Age 35–70 | Debt defaulters; close relatives of members
  [86:1:6.3] Knowledge of the Vedas or administration | Served on a committee in the past three years
[86:1:7] - **Aug 2025:** the PM cited the Uttaramerur **"ballot pot"** as proof of India's early democratic traditions.
[86:1:8] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval India p.408-409; Rocket Indian History #1; app notes 1:86 (sub 3)
## SUB 2 | Kudavolai, Terms and Variyams
[86:2:0] # Kudavolai (pot-ballot)
[86:2:1] - 1. Village divided into **30 wards (kudumbus)**; 2. names of eligible persons written on **palm leaves**; 3. put in a **pot (kudam)**; 4. a **young boy** drew the lots in public.
[86:2:2] - **Term:** **360 days** (one year); removed at once for an offence; a person who served in the last three years was barred.
[86:2:3] - **⚠ Sources differ:** NextGen says committee members "served three-year terms" – the inscription fixes a **one-year** term and a **three-year bar** on re-selection (PMF).
[86:2:4] # Terms → meaning (APPSC G1 match)
[86:2:5] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [86:2:5.0] Variyam | Committee (system)
  [86:2:5.1] Kudumbu | Ward
  [86:2:5.2] Kudavolai | Lottery (palm-leaf ballots in a pot)
  [86:2:5.3] Perumakkal | Member of the village assembly
  [86:2:5.4] Variyapperumakkal | Elected committee members
[86:2:6] > Match key: a-IV, b-I, c-II, d-III.
[86:2:7] # Variyams → function
[86:2:8] TABLE head: Variyam | Function
  [86:2:8.0] Samvatsara variyam | Annual committee; also justice
  [86:2:8.1] Eri variyam | Tanks and water distribution
  [86:2:8.2] Pon variyam | Gold – finance, currency checking
  [86:2:8.3] Thotta variyam | Gardens / orchards (UPRO 2013 ×2)
  [86:2:8.4] Panchavara variyam | Standing committee
[86:2:9] - Uttaramerur committees covered **irrigation, gardens, justice and finance**.
[86:2:10] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval India p.408; NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 3 p.204; app notes 1:86 (sub 4, 5, 6)
## SUB 3 | Assemblies – Ur, Sabha, Nagaram, Nattar
[86:3:0] TABLE head: Assembly | Where | Members
  [86:3:0.0] Ur | Non-brahmadeya (vellanvagai) villages | Landholders (urar); land sale, gifts, tax exemptions
  [86:3:0.1] Sabha / Mahasabha | Brahmadeya (agrahara) villages | Brahmins with property, family, learning (Vedic) and good conduct
  [86:3:0.2] Nagaram | Merchant (market) towns | Merchants (nagarattar)
  [86:3:0.3] Nattar | The nadu (group of villages) | Leading vellala landholders
[86:3:1] - **Nadu** = a group of villages; the **nattar** handled **revenue collection and disputes above the village** (a Chola body, not created by the 73rd Amendment).
[86:3:2] - **Powers:** absolute proprietor of village lands; collected royal dues in **cash, kind or both**; levied taxes; **raised loans**; **auctioned defaulters' land**.
[86:3:3] - **Temples:** Rajaraja I directed the **Cholamandalam sabhas** to serve the **Brihadeshvara** temple.
[86:3:4] - **AP parallel:** village **mahajana** assemblies in **Kakatiya and Velanati** inscriptions – a weaker parallel.
[86:3:5] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval India p.407-408; NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 3 p.204; app notes 1:86 (sub 1, 2, 7)
## SUB 4 | Chola Assembly vs 73rd Amendment
[86:4:0] TABLE head: Point | Chola village assembly | 73rd Amendment
  [86:4:0.0] Selection | Lottery among the qualified | Direct election
  [86:4:0.1] Eligibility | Property, age 35–70, Vedic learning | Adult franchise
  [86:4:0.2] Term | 360 days | 5 years (Art. 243E)
  [86:4:0.3] Women | No quota (women, labourers, landless excluded) | At least 1/3 seats (Art. 243D)
[86:4:1] - **Gram Sabha:** **Art. 243A**; the intermediate tier may be omitted in a State with population **not above 20 lakh** (Art. 243B).
[86:4:2] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval India p.408; app notes 1:86 (sub 8)

=== NOTES 1:87 | Chola Central and Provincial Administration, Land Classification, Revenue and Irrigation
## SUB 0 | Army and Navy
[87:0:0] - **Army:** **elephants, cavalry, infantry** (the three limbs) **and a navy** – **chariots were not part of it** (Police Constable 2016).
[87:0:1] - **Naval power:** the **Cholas** were the South Indian state famous for naval power (UPPSC 2004 ×2); **Rajaraja I** built the navy.
[87:0:2] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [87:0:2.0] Kaikkolar | Royal infantry regiments
  [87:0:2.1] Velaikkarar | Bodyguards sworn to die with the king
  [87:0:2.2] Kadagams | Military cantonments
[87:0:3] - Rajaraja I's navy destroyed the Chera fleet at **Trivandrum (Kandalur)**; Rajendra I's 1025 fleet took **Kadaram = Kedah**; the Bay of Bengal became a **"Chola Lake"**.

## SUB 1 | Kingship and Chola Records
[87:1:0] - **Successor named in the king's lifetime:** the **Cholas** – the yuvaraja was made **co-regent** (UPPSC 2001); Rajendra I co-regent **1012**, king 1014.
[87:1:1] - **⚠ Trap:** "the successor was named only after the king's death" is false.
[87:1:2] - **King's image:** titles *ko*, *perumal*, *rajarajadhiraja*; praised as warrior, patron of arts and protector of **varnashrama dharma**; Rajaraja I = **Ulakalanda Perumal** – measured the earth like **Vishnu's three strides**.
[87:1:3] - **Royal orders:** a **Sanskrit preamble** (genealogy, conquests) + a **Tamil operative part**.
[87:1:4] - **Temple-wall records:** Rajaraja I and Rajendra I had their victories inscribed on **temple walls** – the main reason we know far more about the Cholas than their predecessors.
[87:1:5] > A-R (UPPSC 2020): A "more information about the Cholas" ✓; R "inscriptions on temple walls narrating victories" ✓ and **explains A**.
[87:1:6] TABLE head: Record | Point
  [87:1:6.0] Anbil plates | Sundara Chola; Sanskrit genealogy
  [87:1:6.1] Tiruvalangadu plates | Rajendra I – genealogy and conquests
  [87:1:6.2] Larger Leiden (Anaimangalam) | Rajaraja I's grant to the Chulamanivarma-vihara of the Srivijaya king at Nagapattinam
  [87:1:6.3] Smaller Leiden | 3 sheets; Kulottunga I's extension of the grant after an appeal by two envoys
[87:1:7] - **May 2026:** the **Netherlands** returned the Leiden plates.
[87:1:8] ~~ Sources: Rocket Indian History #1; NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 3 p.204; PMF Ancient & Medieval India p.404; app notes 1:87 (sub 0, 7)
## SUB 2 | Land Classes, Taniyur and Revenue
[87:2:0] # Land classes
[87:2:1] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [87:2:1.0] Eripatti | Land whose revenue maintained the village tank
  [87:2:1.1] Brahmadeya | Rent-free land gifted to Brahmins (sabha villages)
  [87:2:1.2] Vellanvagai | Land of non-Brahmin peasant proprietors (ur villages)
  [87:2:1.3] Devadana / Tirunamattukkani | Land to temples
  [87:2:1.4] Shalabhoga | Land for a school
  [87:2:1.5] Pallichchandam | Land to Jaina institutions
  [87:2:1.6] Ghatikas | Colleges attached to temples
[87:2:2] - **Taniyur:** a **very large village** (an important brahmadeya or nagaram) **administered as a single, separate unit**, outside the nadu (APPSC G1) – not kurram, kottam or nadu.
[87:2:3] - **UPSC 2016 pairs:** Eripatti ✓, Ghatikas ✓; "Taniyurs = villages donated to a single Brahmin or group of Brahmins" ✗ → **A and C (1 and 3)**.
[87:2:4] - **Land rights (kani):** **karanmai** = right to cultivate; **mitachi** = superior possessory right; **kaniyudaiyar** = land-owning farmers; **ulukudi** = tenants.
[87:2:5] # Revenue
[87:2:6] - **Rate:** land revenue normally **1/6 of the produce** (like the Pallavas and Kakatiyas); collected by village assemblies in cash, kind or both; **Rajaraja I's land survey**.
[87:2:7] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [87:2:7.0] Kadamai | Land revenue in kind
  [87:2:7.1] Antarayam | Rural tax in cash
  [87:2:7.2] Eccoru | Duty to feed visiting officials
  [87:2:7.3] Nettal | Compulsory labour
  [87:2:7.4] Vetti, Muttaiyal, Kudimai | Forced labour services
  [87:2:7.5] Irai / Ayam | Land tax / royal dues
[87:2:8] - **Remission:** exemptions granted through the **ur**; **Kulottunga I = Sungam Tavirtta Chola** (abolished tolls).
[87:2:9] - **Modern parallel:** **DILRMP** first phase ran **2008–2016**.
[87:2:10] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval India p.405-408, p.414; NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 3 p.205; app notes 1:87 (sub 3, 4)
## SUB 3 | Officials and Provinces
[87:3:0] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [87:3:0.0] Perundaram / Sirudaram | Highest / lower officials
  [87:3:0.1] Tirumandira-olai | Wrote the king's oral orders on palm leaf
  [87:3:0.2] Olai-nayagam | Checked and countersigned orders
  [87:3:0.3] Adhikari | Royal officer supervising local bodies
  [87:3:0.4] Nattar | Members of the nadu assembly
[87:3:1] - **Order (small to large):** **Ur → Nadu (kurram) → Kottam / Valanadu → Mandalam** – a kottam is above the nadu, not below it.
[87:3:2] - **Eight mandalams**, each under a viceroy, often a **prince**; officials paid in **revenue-bearing land**.
[87:3:3] - **Samanta:** a defeated king restored after accepting overlordship, tribute and military duty; tribute-paying lands = **samanta (vassal) territories**.
[87:3:4] TABLE head: Mandalam | Region
  [87:3:4.0] Cholamandalam | Core Kaveri country
  [87:3:4.1] Jayankondacholamandalam | Former Pallava Tondaimandalam
  [87:3:4.2] Mummudicholamandalam | Northern Sri Lanka
[87:3:5] - **Vengi:** Kulottunga I's sons governed as **Rajapratinidhi**.
[87:3:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 3 p.204-205; PMF Ancient & Medieval India p.407; app notes 1:87 (sub 1, 2)
## SUB 4 | Irrigation and the Temple
[87:4:0] - **Eri variyam:** managed village tanks and water distribution; repairs paid from **eripatti** land.
[87:4:1] - **Kallanai (Grand Anicut)** on the Kaveri = **Karikala** (Sangam); **tank irrigation** was a major feature of the Chola economy (also Vijayanagara, Kakatiyas).
[87:4:2] - **Araghatta:** a water wheel with earthen pots tied to its rim, used for irrigation.
[87:4:3] - **Temple:** biggest landholder, employer and lender, and the **meeting place of the village assembly**; Rajaraja I made the Cholamandalam sabhas serve the **Brihadeeswara, Thanjavur**.
[87:4:4] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval India p.414; Rocket Indian History #89; app notes 1:87 (sub 6)

=== NOTES 1:88 | Chola Economy and Merchant Guilds – Ayyavole, Manigramam; Overseas Trade with China and Srivijaya
## SUB 0 | Merchant Guilds – Ayyavole, Manigramam, Nanadesi
[88:0:0] TABLE head: Body | Base / activity
  [88:0:0.0] Ayyavole-500 (Ainnurruvar) | Originated at Aihole (Ayyavolu), Karnataka; pan-regional and overseas
  [88:0:0.1] Manigramam | Corporation of merchants in long-distance and overseas trade (IAS 1997)
  [88:0:0.2] Nanadesi | "Of many countries" – itinerant guild in foreign trade (UPPSC 2018)
  [88:0:0.3] Ubhaya Nanadesi | Both domestic and foreign trade
  [88:0:0.4] Nagaram (Nakaram) | Local merchant assembly of a market town
  [88:0:0.5] Anjuvannam | Guild of West Asian foreign merchants
[88:0:1] - **Guilds** (shrenis, pugas) had their own code (**bananju-dharma**), symbols and militias, and acted as bankers.
[88:0:2] - **Independence:** as Chola power declined the guilds became **more independent**; they were not confined to local trade.
[88:0:3] - **⚠ Distractors:** Chaturvedimangalam (Brahmin village), Parishad, Ashtadiggaja (Krishnadevaraya's poets), Sreni (general guild).
[88:0:4] - **NDA 2018:** "Ayyavole originated at Aihole" ✓; "Manigramam was subordinated to the Anjuvannam in the 13th century" ✗ → **only I**.
[88:0:5] # AP angle
[88:0:6] - **Penugonda** (West Godavari) = central trade centre of medieval Andhra (**APPSC G2 2012**); Ayyavole and Manigramam had **18 branches** across Vengi.
[88:0:7] - Eastern Chalukya **Nakaras** were headed by **Shreshthis**; **Tagara** = trade centre between Kalyan and Vengi.
[88:0:8] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 3 p.204; app notes 1:88 (sub 0); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manigramam
## SUB 1 | Temple Economy and the Chudamani Vihara
[88:1:0] - **Donations to temples:** **land, money and livestock** (cows, sheep for lamps), guild gifts and royal grants of paddy – **slaves** were not a donation category (CDS 2008).
[88:1:1] - **Chudamani Vihara, Nagapattinam:** Buddhist vihara built (**1006**) by the Srivijaya king **Sri Mara Vijayottunga Varman**; Rajaraja I granted it Anaimangalam village.
[88:1:2] ~~ Sources: NCERT Class VII Our Pasts-II ch.2; app notes 1:88 (sub 5)
## SUB 2 | Overseas Trade – China, Srivijaya, Ports
[88:2:0] - **China:** Chola embassies reached the **Song** court in **1015** and **1033**; **Kulottunga I** sent **72 merchants** in **1077**.
[88:2:1] - **Srivijaya:** friendly at first (Chudamani Vihara) → hostile under **Rajendra I** over the China route (1025).
[88:2:2] - **Guild records abroad:** **Barus (Lobu Tua)**, Sumatra – Ayyavole-500 Tamil inscription, **1088**; **Takua Pa**, Thailand – **Manigramam**; **Pagan**, Myanmar – Nanadesi Vishnu temple.
[88:2:3] - **Significance:** guild networks carried Chola trade and Dravidian culture across the Bay of Bengal.
[88:2:4] TABLE head: Port | Note
  [88:2:4.0] Nagapattinam | Main Chola port; Chudamani Vihara
  [88:2:4.1] Kaveripattinam (Puhar) | Sangam Chola port at the Kaveri mouth
  [88:2:4.2] Quilon (Kollam) | Kerala port; Arab and Chinese trade
[88:2:5] - **⚠ Trap:** **Kaveripattinam** was the early (Sangam) port-capital; **Nagapattinam** was the port of the later Cholas, not an early capital.
[88:2:6] - **West coast:** Arab merchants traded **horses and spices**; the **Anjuvannam** represented foreign merchants.
[88:2:7] - **Terms:** **Nagarams** = market centres; **Erivirappattanas** = protected mercantile towns; **Kasu** = gold coin.
[88:2:8] TABLE head: Exports | Imports
  [88:2:8.0] Textiles, pepper, spices, precious stones | Horses, Chinese silk, porcelain, camphor
[88:2:9] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval India p.405, p.414; app notes 1:88 (sub 1-4)

=== NOTES 1:89 | Chola Art – Brihadeshwara Temple, Dravida Style, Chola Bronzes (nataraja), Tamil Literature
## SUB 0 | Chola Bronzes – Nataraja
[89:0:0] - **Technique:** **lost-wax (cire perdue)** casting; bronze images were already cast in the **Pallava** period (8th–9th c.), but the **Chola** period (10th–12th c.) produced the finest; queen **Sembiyan Mahadevi** was a key patron.
[89:0:1] - **Nataraja period:** the bronze Nataraja developed under the **Imperial Cholas** (APPSC G1 2002; APPSC G1 PYQ; CGPSC 2013 "Chola art") – not the Pandyas, Cheras, Pallavas, Gandhara, Mathura or Mauryan art.
[89:0:2] - **Greatest creation** of South Indian sthapatis: **Nataraja** (IAS 1993) – not Mahishasuramardini, Rama or Somaskanda.
[89:0:3] - **APPSC "cire perdue Nataraja" PYQ:** options lacked the Cholas; of those given, the **Pallavas** (earliest South Indian bronzes) is the defensible answer (Ikshvakus, Vishnukundins, Eastern Chalukyas did not make them).
[89:0:4] TABLE head: Element | Meaning
  [89:0:4.0] Four hands (Ananda Tandava) | Standard form (UPSC 1995; UPRO 2021)
  [89:0:4.1] Damaru (upper right) | Creation – first sound
  [89:0:4.2] Agni (upper left) | Destruction
  [89:0:4.3] Abhaya mudra (lower right) | Protection
  [89:0:4.4] Lower left hand | Points to the raised foot – liberation
  [89:0:4.5] Dwarf Apasmara under the right foot | Ignorance
  [89:0:4.6] Man's earring right, woman's left | Fusion of male and female principles
[89:0:5] > Statements (UPRO 2021): "four hands" ✓; "man's earring right, woman's left" ✓ → **both**.
[89:0:6] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval India p.421; NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 3 p.211 (OCR); app notes 1:89 (sub 2)
## SUB 1 | Temple Life – Dance, Devadasis, Colleges
[89:1:0] - **Dance and music:** **Rajaraja I** appointed about **400 dancing girls** (with musicians and staff, paid by grants) at the Thanjavur temple; hymns of the Alvars and Nayanars sung in temples.
[89:1:1] - **Devadasis** ("female servants of God"): unmarried women dedicated to temple service, music and dance.
[89:1:2] - **Devadasis in the news (UPSC 1996 ×2):** the **Jagannath temple, Puri**, whose Devadasis (**Maharis**) served its rituals – not Pashupatinath, Kandariya Mahadev or Chausath Yogini.
[89:1:3] - **Vedic colleges:** Chola inscriptions record temple colleges at **Ennayiram** and **Tribhuvani** (near Pondicherry, South Arcot) (APPSC G2 2000; APPSC PYQ) – Chola, not Pallava or Pandya.
[89:1:4] - **Uttaramerur (Parantaka I):** important for the **kudavolai** election system.
[89:1:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 3 p.214-215 (OCR); PMF Ancient & Medieval India p.416; app notes 1:89 (sub 4)
## SUB 2 | Chola Temples and the Dravida Style
[89:2:0] - **Dravida style** = South India (APPSC G1 2008); reached its **peak under the Cholas**; continued under the Kalyani Chalukyas and Hoysalas.
[89:2:1] - "The **Pallavas laid the foundation**, the **Cholas** developed it on a monumental scale"; early Chola temples (**Vijayalaya's Narthamalai**, Pudukottai region) are of stone.
[89:2:2] - **Gopurams:** the mighty **gateways** of South Indian temples (State PSC) – not shikharas or mandapams.
[89:2:3] TABLE head: Temple | Builder | Feature
  [89:2:3.0] Koranganatha, Srinivasanallur | Parantaka I | Early Chola
  [89:2:3.1] Brihadeeswara (Rajarajeswara, Dakshina Meru), Thanjavur | Rajaraja I, 1010 | Shiva; granite; vimana 216 ft; capstone ~80 tonnes; largest and tallest in Tamil Nadu
  [89:2:3.2] Gangaikondacholapuram | Rajendra I | Vimana 180 ft, concave curvilinear profile
  [89:2:3.3] Airavatesvara, Darasuram | Rajaraja II | Horse-drawn stone chariot; Musical Steps
  [89:2:3.4] Kampaharesvara, Tribhuvanam | Kulottunga III | Late Chola
  [89:2:3.5] Sun temple, Kumbakonam | Kulottunga I | First of its kind in the south
[89:2:4] - **⚠ Trap (CDS 2009):** Brihadeeswara is a **Shiva** temple (huge linga; Tripurantaka) – "dedicated to Vishnu" is the wrong statement.
[89:2:5] - **Chidambaram** Nataraja temple: enlarged by the Cholas; **Chit Sabha** with **108 dance poses**; **not** in the UNESCO group.
[89:2:6] - **UNESCO "Great Living Chola Temples":** Thanjavur (**1987**) + Gangaikondacholapuram and **Darasuram** (2004).
[89:2:7] - **Order:** Pallava Shore temple → Brihadeeswara → **Gangaikondacholapuram** (latest of the three).
[89:2:8] - **Frescoes:** Brihadeeswara ambulatory – Shiva as **Tripurantaka**, **Rajaraja I with guru Karuvur Thevar**; Narthamalai paintings – Shiva and Parvati.
[89:2:9] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 3 p.207-215 (OCR); PMF Ancient & Medieval India p.420-421; app notes 1:89 (sub 1, 3)
## SUB 3 | Temple Styles and Andhra Temples
[89:3:0] TABLE head: Style | Tower | Examples
  [89:3:0.0] Nagara (north, from c. 5th c.) | Curvilinear shikhara | Khajuraho (Kandariya Mahadeva), Lingaraj
  [89:3:0.1] Dravida | Pyramidal vimana, gopurams, prakara | Kailasanatha, Brihadeeswara
  [89:3:0.2] Vesara | Hybrid; started by the Badami Chalukyas | Hoysala, Rashtrakuta temples
[89:3:1] # Temple terms
[89:3:2] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [89:3:2.0] Garbhagriha | Womb-house with the principal icon
  [89:3:2.1] Vimana | Pyramidal tower over the garbhagriha
  [89:3:2.2] Shikhara | Dome-like crown of the vimana
  [89:3:2.3] Antarala | Vestibule between sanctum and mandapa
  [89:3:2.4] Mandapa | Pillared hall
  [89:3:2.5] Prakara | Enclosure walls
[89:3:3] - **Mixed:** **Teli temple, Gwalior** – Dravida pinnacle with Nagara ornament.
[89:3:4] - **Pairs:** Kailasanathar, Kanchi = **Rajasimha** style; Virupaksha = **Hampi**; **Dilwara** = Mount Abu (not Morena); **Dashavatara, Devgarh** = **Gupta**; Jagannath, Puri founded by **Anantavarman Chodaganga**.
[89:3:5] # Andhra
[89:3:6] - **Kapoteswara temple:** **Chejarla** (Palnadu district) – a Buddhist apsidal shrine, later Shaiva (APPSC Welfare 2017 ×2; APPSC PYQ) – not Nallajerla, Velpur, Srikakulam or Alampur.
[89:3:7] - **Draksharama Bhimeswara** = **Chalukya-Chola** style; **Padmakshi, Hanamkonda** = Kakatiya (not Pallava).
[89:3:8] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval India p.421; app notes 1:89 (sub 0); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapoteswara_Temple,_Chejarla

=== NOTES 1:91 | Yadavas of Devagiri – Bhillama, Singhana, Hemadri and the Hemadpanti Style
## SUB 0 | Dynasty, Capital, Rulers and the Kakatiya Link
[91:0:0] # The dynasty
[91:0:1] - **Name:** **Seuna (Sevuna) Yadavas** of Devagiri; first **feudatories of the Western (Kalyani) Chalukyas** (and earlier the Rashtrakutas); ruled the western Deccan (Maharashtra) c. **1187–1317**.
[91:0:2] - **Mother tongue:** **Marathi** (APPSC G2 2000; APPSC PYQ) – not Telugu, Kannada or Urdu; the Yadavas **encouraged Marathi**; **Sanskrit** = language of scholarship (not Telugu at court).
[91:0:3] - **Founder of the independent kingdom:** **Bhillama V** threw off Kalyani Chalukya rule and built **Devagiri** (c. **1187**) as capital (APPSC G2 2000) – not Prola I, Prola II or Ganapati (Kakatiyas), not Shankaradeva.
[91:0:4] - **Daulatabad:** name given to Devagiri by **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** when he shifted his capital there (**1327**).
[91:0:5] # Rulers
[91:0:6] TABLE head: Ruler | Exam fact
  [91:0:6.0] Bhillama V | Founder; built Devagiri; beaten by Hoysala Veera Ballala II
  [91:0:6.1] Jaitugi (Jaitrapala) | Killed Kakatiya Rudradeva; held young Ganapatideva captive, released him (1199) and married his daughter Somaladevi to him
  [91:0:6.2] Singhana II (c. 1210–1246) | Greatest Yadava; title Teluguraya Sthapanacharya; defeated the Hoysalas; son Sarangapanideva later served at Rudramadevi's court
  [91:0:6.3] Krishna (1246–1261) | Fought the Hoysalas
  [91:0:6.4] Mahadeva (1261–1271) | His attack on the Kakatiyas was repulsed by Rudramadevi
  [91:0:6.5] Ramachandra (1271–1311) | Ruler at Alauddin Khalji's 1296 raid; later a vassal
  [91:0:6.6] Shankaradeva (1311–1313) | Died in Malik Kafur's invasion
  [91:0:6.7] Harapaladeva (1313–1317) | Last ruler; killed in Mubarak Khalji's invasion
[91:0:7] - **Rudradeva's killer:** **Jaitugi** (APPSC PYQ) – recorded by Hemadri and confirmed by the **Paithan copper plate** of Ramachandra; not Narasimha Deva or Namadeva.
[91:0:8] - **Why Ganapati was freed (1199):** as a counterweight to Hoysala **Veera Ballala II's** push into the **Krishna–Tungabhadra** region.
[91:0:9] - **Rudrama's victory over Mahadeva:** recorded in the **Bidar fort inscription** (APPSC PYQ) – not Bayyaram, Chandupatla or Hanumakonda.
[91:0:10] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval India p.410; NextGen AP History - Kakatiyas p.45, p.47; app notes 1:91 (sub 0, 1, 2)
## SUB 1 | Scholars – Hemadri, Sarngadeva, Changadeva; the Hemadpanti Style
[91:1:0] # Hemadri
[91:1:1] - **Chaturvarga Chintamani:** Sanskrit encyclopaedia by **Hemadri** (APPSC G2 2000 ×2; APPSC PYQ) – on **dharma, rituals, charity, pilgrimage and vratas**; not Vidyanatha, Jayapa Senani or Palkuriki Somanatha.
[91:1:2] - **Office:** **Shrikaranadhipa** (head of secretariat and records) under **Mahadeva and Ramachandra**.
[91:1:3] - **On Kakatiya Rudra:** Hemadri claimed **Jaitugi captured and sacrificed Rudra**.
[91:1:4] - **Hemadpanti style:** credited to Hemadri – local **black basalt**, dressed stones **interlocked without mortar** (**dry masonry**).
[91:1:5] # Other scholars and works
[91:1:6] TABLE head: Person | Work / role
  [91:1:6.0] Sarngadeva | Court musician of Singhana II; Sangita Ratnakara – base text of both Hindustani and Carnatic music (not Hemadri)
  [91:1:6.1] Changadeva | Court astronomer of Singhana II; grandson of Bhaskaracharya; school at Patan to teach Bhaskara's works
  [91:1:6.2] Bhaskaracharya (Bhaskara II) | Lilavati, the mathematics treatise (Uttarakhand PCS 2010) – not Ramanuja, Kautilya or Amartya Sen
  [91:1:6.3] Dnyaneshwar | Dnyaneshwari – Marathi commentary on the Bhagavad Gita, 1290, Nevasa, in Ramachandra's reign
  [91:1:6.4] Chakradhar Swami | Founder of the Mahanubhava sect (not Dnyaneshwar)
  [91:1:6.5] Mhaimbhat | Lilacharitra = first Marathi prose
[91:1:7] - Later Bhakti saints Namdev, Tukaram and Ramdas carried Upanishad and Gita ideas into Marathi.
[91:1:8] ~~ Sources: app notes 1:91 (sub 3, 4); https://www.britannica.com/biography/Bhaskara-II
## SUB 2 | Fall of Devagiri to Delhi
[91:2:0] TABLE head: Year | Event
  [91:2:0.0] 1296 | First Muslim invasion of the South: Alauddin Khalji, then governor of Kara under Sultan Jalaluddin, raids Devagiri and defeats Ramachandra; promised the yearly revenue of Ellichpur but did not send it
  [91:2:0.1] 1307–08 | Malik Kafur: Ramachandra submits and is taken to Delhi, then restored as a vassal
  [91:2:0.2] 1313 | Shankaradeva dies in Kafur's invasion
  [91:2:0.3] 1317–18 | Harapaladeva killed by Mubarak Khalji; kingdom annexed
  [91:2:0.4] After 1323 | Malik Burhanuddin of Devagiri given charge of Andhra; Devagiri = the Sultanate's Deccan base
[91:2:1] - **Significance:** Devagiri was the **first southern kingdom to fall** to Delhi and opened the road to Warangal, Dwarasamudra and Madurai.
[91:2:2] - **⚠ Trap:** Kafur's 1307–08 campaign brought the submission of **Ramachandra**, not Harapaladeva.
[91:2:3] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval India p.410; app notes 1:91 (sub 5)

=== NOTES 1:92 | Kakatiyas – Origins, Beta I, Rudradeva, Ganapatideva; Kakatiya–yadava–hoysala Relations
## SUB 0 | Origins, Overlords and First Mentions
[92:0:0] # Overlords
[92:0:1] - **First overlords:** the **Rashtrakutas** (APPSC G2 2005 ×2; G2 Mains 2017 ×2) – the Magallu record calls Gundaya and Eriya "Rashtrakuta", and the early emblem was **Garuda**.
[92:0:2] - **Then:** feudatories of the **Kalyani (Western) Chalukyas** – emblem **Varaha** (changed by **Prola I**); title **Mahamandaleswara** (APPSC G2 2001), borne by Beta II.
[92:0:3] - **⚠ Trap:** the **Eastern Chalukyas** only issued the Magallu grant; they were never Kakatiya overlords.
[92:0:4] - **Phases:** samanta (feudatory) 956–1162 → **sovereign 1163–1323** – the Kakatiyas ruled Andhra in the **12th–13th centuries** (APPSC Social & Cultural History).
[92:0:5] - **UPSC 2023:** none of the Hoysalas (10th–11th c.), Gahadavalas (11th c.), Kakatiyas or Yadavas (12th c.) was founded in the early 8th century → **None**.
[92:0:6] # First mentions and progenitor
[92:0:7] TABLE head: Record | Fact
  [92:0:7.0] Magallu grant (c. 950–956) of Eastern Chalukya Danarnava | First mention of the Kakatiyas – Kakatiya Gundyana (Kakara Gundana) (G2 Mains 2017; APPSC PYQ)
  [92:0:7.1] Bayyaram tank inscription of Mailamba (Ganapati's sister) | Best genealogy; line begins with Venna (Venna Bhupati) (Group-II)
  [92:0:7.2] Kazipet (Dargah) inscription | Names Beta I as the first Kakatiya king (APPSC G1 2002; APPSC PYQ ×2); records the accession of Durga Nripathi
[92:0:8] - **Early base:** **Hanamkonda (Anumakonda) Vishaya**, received by Beta I through his aunt **Viriyala Kamasani**.
[92:0:9] # Religion and identity
[92:0:10] - **Jains first:** the Kakatiyas were initially **Jains** and later **Shaivas** – the clan whose first rulers were Jains (2002 paper).
[92:0:11] - **Garuda emblem** from Jain Tirthankara **Shantinatha**; clan deity **Kakatamma (Kakati Devi)** = the Jain **Kushmandini**; **"Kakati" = gourd**.
[92:0:12] - **Saiva gurus:** **Rameswara Pandita** (Mallikarjuna matha, **Srisailam**) → **Beta II**; **Dhruveshwara Pandita** → **Mahadeva**; **Visvesvara Sivacharya** (Golaki Matha) → **Ganapatideva** (raja guru, APPSC PYQ ×3).
[92:0:13] - **Unifiers of Andhra:** the Kakatiyas were the **second dynasty after the Satavahanas** to unite all Telugu lands; they "gave a comprehensive form to Andhraism" – the dynasty that gave the **ultimate design to Andhra culture** (DAO 2011).
[92:0:14] - **Loose PYQ:** "one of the major dynasties that ruled Andhra" – key **Satavahanas**, the first major Andhra dynasty (all four options ruled Andhra).
[92:0:15] - **Eastern Deccan:** the **Kakatiyas** ruled the eastern Deccan in the 12th–14th c.; the Seunas held the west.
[92:0:16] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Kakatiyas p.35-37, p.41; PMF Ancient & Medieval India p.410; app notes 1:92 (sub 0, 9)
## SUB 1 | Capitals – Anumakonda to Orugallu (Warangal)
[92:1:0] # Who shifted the capital?
[92:1:1] TABLE head: Step | Ruler | Capital
  [92:1:1.0] 1 | Prola I | Made Anumakonda (Hanumakonda) the capital
  [92:1:1.1] 2 | Prola II | Developed Hanamkonda; Swayambhu temple in Orugallu
  [92:1:1.2] 3 | Rudradeva | Founded Orugallu and began the Warangal fort
  [92:1:1.3] 4 | Ganapatideva | Completed the fort and transferred the capital from Hanumakonda to Orugallu (Rocket: 1254); called it Andhranagari
  [92:1:1.4] 5 | After 1323 | Renamed Sultanpur
[92:1:2] - **Answer to "who shifted the capital?":** **Ganapatideva** (APPSC G2 2012; Architecture 2011; APPSC PYQ; G1 2024 match B-I).
[92:1:3] - **⚠ Disputed:** the Bekkallu inscription (1195) already calls Orugallu Rudradeva's capital, so some keys (G2 2019, Asst. Welfare Officers) gave **Rudradeva**; NextGen, Rocket and the G1 2024 official match credit **Ganapatideva**, who completed the move.
[92:1:4] - **Orugallu fort:** construction **begun by Rudradeva** (APSLPRB 2023), completed by Ganapatideva, strengthened by Rudramadevi.
[92:1:5] - **Kakatiya capital:** **Orugallu / Warangal** (APPSC 2019 ×2; Polytechnic Lecturers 2020) – not Vijayanagara, Amaravati, Vijayawada, Guntur or Visakhapatnam.
[92:1:6] - **Orugallu** = "single rock", the ancient name of Warangal; **Warangal** is the place that best reflects the Kakatiya contribution to culture (fort, Thousand Pillar temple, Ramappa nearby) (AEE 2008).
[92:1:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Kakatiyas p.11, p.15, p.45; Rocket AP History p.47; app notes 1:92 (sub 3)

  [92:2:1.1] Prola I | 1052–1076 | Arigajakesari | Made Anumakonda capital; Garuda → Varaha; Kesari Samudram
  [92:2:1.2] Beta II | 1076–1108 | Vikrama Chakri, Tribhuvanamalla | Saiva under Rameswara Pandita
  [92:2:1.3] Durgaraja | 1108–1116 | – | Gifts to Betesvara temple
  [92:2:1.4] Prola II | 1116–1157 | – | Victory pillar at Srisailam; killed by the Velanati Chodas; Yadava conflict began
  [92:2:1.5] Rudradeva (Prataparudra I) | 1158–1195 | Vidyabhushana | Independence 1163; wrote Nitisara; killed by Jaitugi
  [92:2:1.6] Mahadeva | 1195–1199 | – | Invaded the Yadavas to avenge Rudradeva; died on an elephant crossing a river

  [92:2:4.4] Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya ("founder of the Kakati Rajya"), Raya Pitamahanka | Recherla Prasaditya; key for G2 2002 = Recherla Rudra (the Recherla option)
  [92:2:4.5] Mahamandaleswara | Feudatory Kakatiyas

  [92:2:7.1] Thousand Pillar (Rudreshwara) temple, Anumakonda, 1163 | Rudradeva (Tribal Welfare Officer PYQ) – Shiva, Vishnu, Surya

[92:2:8] - **Ramappa (Rudreswara) temple** = **Kakatiya** (APPSC ASO); **UNESCO World Heritage Site 2021**; **floating bricks**; star-shaped platform.
[92:2:9] - **Feudatory families:** **Viriyala** (Kamasani), **Recherla** (Rudra, Prasaditya), **Malyala**, **Natavadi**.

## SUB 3 | Ganapatideva (1199–1262)
[92:3:0] - **Reign:** **1199–1262** (about **63 years**, the longest; APPSC AE 2011); first inscription **Manthena, 26 Dec 1199**; title **Andhra Deshadhiswara**.
[92:3:1] - **Accession:** held captive by Yadava **Jaitugi**; **Recherla Rudra** crushed revolts and installed him.
[92:3:2] - **Unifier:** brought **the whole Telugu area under one rule** after the Satavahanas (1199 PYQ ×2), from Ganjam to Kanchi – the Kakatiya who ruled all Andhradesa as one sovereign (APPSC G1 2003).
[92:3:3] - **Kanchi:** the most powerful Kakatiya, who **extended the empire up to Kanchi** (Group-I 1990-91; G1 1994) – not Beta I, Prola I or Prola II.
[92:3:4] - **Gurus:** raja guru **Visvesvara Sivacharya** – not Vidyanatha, Narahari Tirtha, Rameswara Pandita or Dhruveshwara Pandita.
[92:3:5] # Campaigns
[92:3:6] - **Velanadu:** 1201 coastal campaign – general **Mutyalachaundaraya** took **Divi**; married **Narama and Perama**, daughters of **Pinnachodi**; made their brother **Jayapa** **Gajasahani**.
[92:3:7] - **1210:** with **Choda Tikka** of Nellore killed **Prithviswara** → Velanati kingdom ended (title **Prithviswara Shirakhandika Kreeda Vinoda**); **1257:** with Akkana and Bayyana killed **Mummadi Rajendra Chola** – final end of the Velanati Chodas.
[92:3:8] - **Pithapuram inscription** of Velanati **Prithvisvara** names **Kolleru Lake** (G2 2017).
[92:3:9] - **Nellore:** restored **Manumasiddhi II** after the poet **Tikkana** came as envoy; Tikkana dedicated **Nirvachanottara Ramayana** to **Manumasiddhi**, not Ganapati.
[92:3:10] - **Kalinga:** fought the **Eastern Gangas** for southern Kalinga and Vengi.
[92:3:11] - **Defeat, 1263:** **Jatavarman Sundara Pandya** beat the Kakatiyas at **Muttukur** (Nellore); **Nellore fell to the Pandyas** (G2 Mains 2017 ×2) – not the Velanati Chodas, Yadavas or Hoysalas.
[92:3:12] # Works and succession
[92:3:13] - **Ramappa temple** (Recherla Rudra, 1213), **Lakkavaram** and **Ghanapur** tanks, **Ganapavaram** villages, **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** (1244).
[92:3:14] - **Telugu replaced Sanskrit** in inscriptions from his reign.
[92:3:15] - **Family:** no son → daughter **Rudramadevi succeeded him** (APPSC PYQ), raised as a son (putrika), trained by her mother **Kupama Devi**; married **Veerabhadra** of the **Nidadavolu Eastern Chalukyas**; daughter **Ganapamba** married the **Kota** chief; sisters **Mailamba** and **Kundamamba** married the sons of **Natavadi Buddharaja**.
[92:3:16] - Rudrama defeated the Pandyas, Eastern Gangas and Seunas – **not the Western Chalukyas**; Marco Polo visited Motupalli ("Mutfili") in her reign.
[92:3:17] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Kakatiyas p.11-15, p.47-51; app notes 1:92 (sub 4, 5)

[92:4:1] > Match (APPSC G2 Mains 2025 ×3): **a-III, b-IV, c-I, d-II** (Sanigaram–Prolaraja, Anumakonda–Rudradeva, Bayyaram–Mailamba, Motupalli–Ganapatideva).

## SUB 5 | Wars with the Yadavas, Hoysalas and Others; Legacy
[92:5:0] TABLE head: Opponent | Episode
  [92:5:0.0] Yadavas (Sevunas) | Conflict began under Prola II; Jaitugi killed Rudradeva and held Ganapati; Mahadeva died in the revenge war; Rudramadevi repulsed Yadava Mahadeva
  [92:5:0.1] Hoysalas | Veera Ballala II's advance made Jaitugi free Ganapati; Prataparudra's commander Pedarudru beat Ballala III after 1316
  [92:5:0.2] Velanati Chodas | Killed Prola II; ended 1210 / 1257
  [92:5:0.3] Pandyas (of Madurai) | Beat Ganapatideva at Muttukur, 1263
  [92:5:0.4] Delhi | Malik Kafur besieged Warangal in 1310 (tributary); 1323 fall; Prataparudra died jumping into the Narmada (Musunuri record)
[92:5:1] - **Legacy:** one tradition makes **Harihara and Bukka** treasury officers of **Prataparudra II** who fled to **Kampili** after 1323; the **Nayankara system** was carried on by Vijayanagara.
[92:5:2] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Kakatiyas p.17-19, p.45; app notes 1:92 (sub 6, 10)

  The early Kakatiyas were followers of Jainism. Which faith did they follow later?
  Vaishnavas | Buddhists | *Shaivas | Shaktas
  x: The early Kakatiyas were Jains who later became Shaivas (APPSC G2 2011); their sovereign phase ran from 1163 to 1323.
[n13bf68e2feb] sub0
  What is the meaning of 'Kakati', from which the Kakatiya clan deity takes its name?
  *Gourd | Elephant | Boar | Lion
  x: Kakati means gourd. Kakatamma, or Kakati Devi, was associated with the Jain Kushmandini before being absorbed into Hindu tradition.
[n0fdd843157a] sub0
  Which was the early territorial base of the Kakatiyas?
  Vengi Vishaya | *Hanamkonda Vishaya | Velanadu | Renadu
  x: The early Kakatiya base was Hanamkonda Vishaya (modern Karimnagar, Warangal, Khammam); they served the Rashtrakutas first and then the Kalyani Chalukyas.

  x: The Magallu grant of Eastern Chalukya Danarnava (956) first mentions the Kakatiya family through Gundyana.

  x: Beta II was initiated into Saivism by Rameswara Pandita of the Srisailam Mallikarjuna matha.

  x: The Kakatiyas ruled the eastern Deccan from Warangal in the 12th–14th centuries. The Seunas (Yadavas) ruled the western Deccan, and the Eastern Gangas ruled Odisha.

=== NOTES 1:93 | Rani Rudrama Devi and Prataparudra; Marco Polo's Account; Fall to the Delhi Sultanate
## SUB 0 | Prataparudra Yasobhushanam and Kakatiya Court Literature
[93:0:0] - **Prataparudra Yasobhushanam:** Sanskrit work on **alankara (poetics)** praising **Prataparudra II**, by his court poet **Vidyanatha** (APPSC G2 2000, 2011; Police Constable 2016; GS common paper; APPSC PYQ ×5) – not Prataparudra I or II themselves, Jayapa, Ambadeva, Sarangadhara, Rudradeva, Tikkana, Ketana, Baddena or Palkuriki Somanatha.
[93:0:1] - **Vidyanatha = Agastya** (G2 2012): historians identify the two; Agastya also wrote **Nalakirtikaumudi**, **Balabharata** and **Krishnacharita**.
[93:0:2] - **"What Bana was to Harsha, Vidyanatha was to Prataparudradeva."**
[93:0:3] - **Gangadevi**, author of **Madhura Vijayam** (Vijayanagara), hailed **Agastya** as her guru; Madhura Vijayam also describes the hardship after the conquest.
[93:0:4] # Other works of the age
[93:0:5] TABLE head: Work | Author
  [93:0:5.0] Nitisara (Neetisastram, Sanskrit polity) | Rudradeva (Kakati Rudra) (DAO 2011)
  [93:0:5.1] Sakala Niti Sammatamu (polity anthology) | Madiki Singana (APSLPRB 2023)
  [93:0:5.2] Niti Sara Muktavali, Sumati Satakam | Baddena
  [93:0:5.3] Nrittaratnavali (dance) | Jayapa Senani, Gajasahini of Ganapatideva
  [93:0:5.4] Prataparudra Charitramu | Ekamranatha – Kakatiya traditions (Jaitugi–Ganapati marriage), Rudrama's Yadava victory
  [93:0:5.5] Khazain-ul-Futuh | Amir Khusrau – Kafur's 1310 siege; Warangal fort double-walled with a moat; calls Prataparudra Ravaddar Dev
  [93:0:5.6] Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi | Barani
[93:0:6] - **Sakalya Malla** was another court poet of Prataparudra II.
[93:0:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Kakatiyas p.11, p.31-33, p.55, p.59, p.71; app notes 1:93 (sub 7)
## SUB 1 | Rudrama Devi (1262–1289)
[93:1:0] # Family and accession
[93:1:1] - **Daughter of Ganapatideva** and **Kupama Devi** (APPSC PYQ); Ganapati had **no son**, so she was raised as a son (**putrika**).
[93:1:2] - **Kakatiya** queen (Uttarakhand PCS 2021) – not Eastern Ganga, Hoysala or Western Chalukya.
[93:1:3] - **Co-regent from 1258** under the male name **Rudradeva Maharaja**; ruled to **1289**.
[93:1:4] - **First woman ruler of the Andhra region** (Rudramba; APPSC PYQ); **second great woman ruler of medieval India after Razia Sultana**.
[93:1:5] - **4th sovereign Kakatiya** (Rudradeva → Mahadeva → Ganapatideva → Rudrama).
[93:1:6] - **Husband:** Chalukya prince **Veerabhadra** (Nidadavolu).
[93:1:7] TABLE head: Daughter | Married / son
  [93:1:7.0] Mummadamma | Mahadeva; mother of Prataparudra II
  [93:1:7.1] Rudramma | Yadava prince Ellanadeva
  [93:1:7.2] Ruyyamma | Induluri Annaya
[93:1:8] - **Children:** **three daughters**, no son (APPSC Drug Inspector 2011).
[93:1:9] # Wars and title
[93:1:10] - **Statements (UPRO 2023):** "4th independent ruler" ✓ and "defeated the Pandyas, Eastern Gangas of Odisha and Seunas of Devagiri" ✓ → **both**.
[93:1:11] - **Rayagajakesari:** title taken for her victory over the **rulers of Devagiri** (Yadava **Mahadeva**, chased back to Devagiri) (APPSC G2 PYQ ×3) – not the Pandyas, Kalinga rulers or Vaidumbas.
[93:1:12] - **Internal revolt:** half-brothers **Harihara and Murari**, crushed with Recherla Prasaditya and others.
[93:1:13] - **Vengi:** occupied by Ganga **Narasimhadeva** (1262); regained **1278** when **Poti Nayaka and Prolinayaka** beat Virabhanudeva.
[93:1:14] - **Death, 1289:** killed fighting the Kayastha rebel **Ambadeva** (made head of Kadapa in 1272) with general **Mallikarjuna Nayaka**.
[93:1:15] - **Chandupatla inscription** (**Nalgonda**), set up by her servant **Puvvula Mummadi**, records her death (APPSC Asst. Welfare Officers) – not Tripurantakam (Ambadeva's victories), Gurjala or Induluru.
[93:1:16] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Kakatiyas p.15-17, p.51-53; NextGen previous papers p.14; app notes 1:93 (sub 0, 1, 2)
## SUB 2 | Marco Polo's Account
[93:2:0] - **Who:** **Marco Polo**, the **Venetian (Italian)** traveller; work **Il Milione / The Travels**.
[93:2:1] - **When:** visited in **Rudramadevi's** reign (DAO 2011; G2 2011 ×2; Group-II-A 1984) – reached the Coromandel coast in **1292**, towards the end of her reign.
[93:2:2] - **Where:** landed at the Kakatiya port **Motupalli ("Mutfili")** (Group-I 1990-91; G1 1994; APPSC PYQ) – not Ibn Battuta, Abdur Razzaq, Nicolo Conti, Domingo Paes, Jordanus, Hiuen Tsang or Columbus.
[93:2:3] TABLE head: Theme | Observation
  [93:2:3.0] Ruler | Praised the queen's strict and just rule and the country's prosperity
  [93:2:3.1] Trade | Flourishing sea trade; port duties at Motupalli; merchants not heavily taxed
  [93:2:3.2] Wealth | Diamond mines of the Golconda region (APPSC PYQ); fine textiles
  [93:2:3.3] Climate, food | Hot climate; rice the only local grain
[93:2:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Kakatiyas p.15, p.25-27, p.53; app notes 1:93 (sub 3)
## SUB 3 | Fall of Warangal (1323) and the Captivity of Prataparudra
[93:3:0] - **Captor:** **Ulugh Khan** (Juna Khan, later **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**), under Sultan **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq** (APPSC G2 2019; G2 PYQ; Group-II-A 1989) – not Malik Kafur, Alauddin Khalji or Malik Chajju.
[93:3:1] - **Year:** **1323** – the end of the Kakatiya kingdom (Group-II-B 1989); final siege about **five months**; **Bobbareddi's** withdrawal weakened the defence.
[93:3:2] - **Death:** Prataparudra **drowned himself in the Narmada** on the way to Delhi (**Vilasa** copper plate of Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka; one account says the Kaveri).
[93:3:3] - **Renaming:** Orugallu → **Sultanpur** (APPSC PYQ).
[93:3:4] - **After 1323:** Andhra under **Malik Burhanuddin**; **Malik Maqbul** (converted Brahmin Jagannatha Pandit) at Warangal; survivors **Prolaya Nayaka, Racherla Singama, Prolaya Vema** led the liberation → Musunuri and Reddi states.
[93:3:5] - **Causes:** southern disunity, weak cavalry, betrayal by chiefs, exhaustion from repeated raids – **not** a European sea blockade.
[93:3:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Kakatiyas p.19, p.57-59; NextGen previous papers p.14, p.58; app notes 1:93 (sub 6)
## SUB 4 | Prataparudra II – Campaigns and the Delhi Invasions
[93:4:0] - **Prataparudra II (1289–1323):** grandson of Rudrama through **Mummadamma**; title **Kumara Rudradeva**; last Kakatiya.
[93:4:1] - **Campaigns:** commanders beat **Ambadeva** at **Tripurantakam** (1291); **Ranganatha** of Nellore (Pandya ally) replaced by **Manuma Gandapalu**; Gonavithala pushed to Devagiri.
[93:4:2] - **Nayankara:** kingdom divided into **77 Nayankaras** held by military officers (**Nayakas**); each held a **fort**, kept troops and paid a **fixed tribute**; about **one-fourth** of the land; continued as Vijayanagara **Amaranayakas** → later **Poligars**.
[93:4:3] TABLE head: No. | Year | Commander | Outcome
  [93:4:3.0] 1 | 1303 | Alauddin's Malik Fakhruddin Juna | Repulsed at Upparapalli by Pothuganti Aili and Recherla Venna – first attack on Orugallu
  [93:4:3.1] 2 | 1309–10 | Malik Kafur | Siege; tribute and Delhi overlordship
  [93:4:3.2] 3 | 1318 | Mubarak Khalji's Khusrau Khan | Tribute renewed
  [93:4:3.3] 4 | 1321–22 | Ulugh Khan | Rumour of the Sultan's death; army chased back
  [93:4:3.4] 5 | 1323 | Ulugh Khan | Warangal fell
[93:4:4] - **1311:** Kakatiya troops under **Muppidi Nayaka** joined Kafur's march on Madurai; **1316:** tribute stopped after Alauddin's death.
[93:4:5] - **⚠ Trap:** the 1323 conquest was by Ulugh Khan, not Khusrau Khan.
[93:4:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Kakatiyas p.17-19, p.53-57; app notes 1:93 (sub 4, 5)

=== NOTES 1:94 | Kakatiya Administration – Nayankara System, Tank Irrigation, Trade, Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam
## SUB 0 | Motupalli Port and the Abhaya Sasanam
[94:0:0] - **Chief port:** **Motupalli** – the main Kakatiya seaport for external trade (APPSC G2 2000, 2011, 2012) – not Warangal (inland capital), Krishnapatnam, Pulicat, Nellore, Machilipatnam, Ghantasala, Dharanikota or Korangi.
[94:0:1] - **Other name:** **Desiyakonda (Deseeyakkonda / Desyakkonda) Pattanam** (APPSC G2 2019 ×2; G2 2012; APPSC PYQ) – not Nidadavolu, Vadarevu, Motukur, Mudigonda, Mukalapura or Malakapuram.
[94:0:2] # Abhaya Sasanam (Motupalli Charter)
[94:0:3] - **Issuer:** **Ganapatideva**, **1244** CE, a pillar inscription at Motupalli (APPSC G2 2019; Group-II-A 1984; Welfare Officers 2017 ×2; APPSC PYQ ×3) – not Rudramba, Ambadeva or Prataparudra.
[94:0:4] - **Content:** **protection and shelter to foreign (sea) merchants**; unfair taxes cancelled, only fixed duties; **compensation for shipwreck or theft**; no harassment by officials.
[94:0:5] - **Official posted:** **Siddayya Devudu**.
[94:0:6] - **Most important commercial document** of the period.
[94:0:7] - **Goods at Motupalli:** **sandal, camphor, rose-water, ivory**, pearls, corals, copper, silk, pepper.
[94:0:8] - **Marco Polo** visited Motupalli in **Rudramadevi's** reign.
[94:0:9] TABLE head: Port | Note
  [94:0:9.0] Motupalli | Chief port; Desiyakonda Pattanam
  [94:0:9.1] Krishnapatnam | Nellore coast
  [94:0:9.2] Hamsaladeevi | Krishna delta
[94:0:10] - **Kara Pattanam** = ports collecting import and export duties.
[94:0:11] - **⚠ Trap:** the **Motupalli Dharma Sasanam (1416)** is of Vijayanagara **Deva Raya I**, not Ganapatideva.
[94:0:12] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Kakatiyas p.27, p.53; NextGen previous papers p.14; Rocket AP History p.6, p.13; app notes 1:94 (sub 10)
## SUB 1 | Revenue, Village Officers and Coins
[94:1:0] # Land revenue
[94:1:1] - **Ari (Aari):** the Kakatiya **land tax / land revenue** (Juvenile Welfare 2011; APPSC PYQ) – generally **one-sixth** of the produce; taxpayers = **Arigapulu**; collectors = **Kolakandru**.
[94:1:2] - **Land classes:** **Magani** = irrigated wet land (food crops); **Metta** = rain-fed dry land.
[94:1:3] - **Tax-free:** temple lands, Brahmin grants, Ayagar lands, **Dashabandhamu** (land for tank upkeep).
[94:1:4] TABLE head: Tax | Meaning
  [94:1:4.0] Koru | Cess on wet land
  [94:1:4.1] Putti Wahindi | Cess on dry land
  [94:1:4.2] Pullari | Tax on grass (grazing)
  [94:1:4.3] Dari Sunkam | Road toll
  [94:1:4.4] Angadi Sunkam | Weekly-market tax
  [94:1:4.5] Kanika | Customary gift to the king or officials
  [94:1:4.6] Pellipannu | Wedding tax
[94:1:5] - **Not Kakatiya:** **Meruka** = Reddi wet-land tax; **Moturpha** = British tax on trades and looms; Vijayanagara **Krishnadevaraya** withdrew the marriage tax.
[94:1:6] # Village officers
[94:1:7] - **Ayagars:** **twelve (12)** village servants (APPSC PYQ) – Karnam, Reddi, Talari, purohita, smiths; paid by **shares of produce and service lands**, held land **without any cess or tax**.
[94:1:8] - **Karanam** = village accountant; **Reddi** = headman; **Talari** = village watchman.
[94:1:9] # Coins
[94:1:10] TABLE head: Coin | Metal
  [94:1:10.0] Mada / Gadyana | Gold – the Kakatiya gold coin (Group-II; Welfare Officers 2017; APPSC PYQ ×2)
  [94:1:10.1] Nishka | Gold
  [94:1:10.2] Ruka | Silver
  [94:1:10.3] Visa, Adduga, Padika | Smaller denominations
[94:1:11] - Few coins survive; types are known mainly from **inscriptions**.
[94:1:12] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Kakatiyas p.21, p.25-29, p.65; NextGen previous papers p.58; Rocket AP History p.18; app notes 1:94 (sub 2, 5, 11)
## SUB 2 | Guilds, Samayas and Trade Routes
[94:2:0] # Samayas and guilds
[94:2:1] - **Samaya (Samayamu):** a **caste organisation** / caste-occupational association – Mahajanulu (Brahmins), Nakaramu (Vaishyas); each elected a head; meeting in temple mandapams.
[94:2:2] - **Chitrameli:** the samaya (shreni) of **agricultural farmers** (APPSC G2 Mains; APPSC PYQ) – not goldsmiths, painters or dancers.
[94:2:3] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [94:2:3.0] Nakaram | Domestic merchants
  [94:2:3.1] Nanadesi | Foreign (inter-regional) merchants
  [94:2:3.2] Ubhaya Nanadesi | Merchants of both the Desis, Paradesis and Nanadesis
  [94:2:3.3] Ayyavole 500 | Guild named after Aihole
  [94:2:3.4] Virabanajam | Licensed for Pakanadu, Vengi and Hanumakonda (Tripurantakam inscription, 1282)
[94:2:4] - **Guild head:** **Setti / Sreshthi**; guilds had seals, emblems and militia and acted as bankers – but **no royal monopoly** over trade.
[94:2:5] # Routes (APPSC G1 2023 ×2)
[94:2:6] - **Kridabhiramamu routes:** **Motupalli–Tripurantakam–Ballari** and **Palnadu–Nalgonda–Nekarikallu–Orugallu** → answer **III and IV**; **Orugallu** was the inland trade hub.
[94:2:7] - **Tripurantakam** linked Motupalli and the salt towns to **Ballari** via Kurnool.
[94:2:8] - **Ketana:** chief inland route Kanchi → Nellore → Warangal → **Ayodhya**.
[94:2:9] - Kakatiyas controlled routes between the **Deccan interior and the eastern coast**.
[94:2:10] - **Kridabhiramamu:** Telugu play by **Vinukonda Vallabharaya** describing life in **Orugallu (Warangal)**.
[94:2:11] - **Imports:** **Arabian war horses**, pearls, silk, perfumes; **exports:** fine textiles, spices, diamonds, gold.
[94:2:12] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Kakatiyas p.25-27, p.63-69; NextGen previous papers p.14; https://www.ijraset.com/best-journal/development-of-internal-trade-routes-and-centers-under-the-kakatiyas; app notes 1:94 (sub 9)
## SUB 3 | Nayankara System and Administration
[94:3:0] # Nayankara system
[94:3:1] - **Introduced by:** **Prataparudra II** (Asst. Welfare Officers PYQ; APPSC 2025), who organised the kingdom into **77 Nayankaras** – ⚠ one book key and a NextGen Level-II line say Rudrama.
[94:3:2] - **How:** military commanders (**Nayakas**) were made administrators of **Sthalas / Mandalams** and given charge of **forts** – the Kakatiya empire was ruled through vassals called **Nayakas** (2002 paper).
[94:3:3] - **Land instead of salary:** villages called **Nayakasthalam**; Nayankaras held about **one-fourth** of the land; no monthly cash salary.
[94:3:4] - **Duties:** collect revenue → keep a fixed army for the king → pay a fixed annual sum.
[94:3:5] - **Sources:** **Ekamranatha's Pratapa Charitra**; Baddena's Niti Sastra Muktavali.
[94:3:6] - **Successor systems:** Vijayanagara **Amaranayaka** (land = **Amaram**) → **Poligars**.
[94:3:7] # Administration
[94:3:8] - **Nature of the state:** most scholars – **decentralised monarchy**; **Romila Thapar** – "metropolitan state"; **Burton Stein** – "segmentary state"; **Cynthia Talbot** – "Golden Age of the Shudras".
[94:3:9] - **Prime ministers:** **Malyala Hemadri Reddi** (Ganapatideva); **Muppidi Nayudu** (Prataparudra II).
[94:3:10] - **Units:** **Rashtra / Mandala** (largest) → Nadu → Sthala → Grama.
[94:3:11] - **72 Niyogas** (departments) under the **Bahattara Niyogadhipati**.
[94:3:12] - **Tirthulu / Ashtadasa Tirthas:** the **18 high officers (ministers) of state** (Sakala Neeti Sammatamu of **Madiki Singana**) – ministers, not water sources, temples or spies (APPSC PYQ).
[94:3:13] TABLE head: Officer | Role
  [94:3:13.0] Pradvivaka | Judicial adviser
  [94:3:13.1] Kayasthas | Scribes
  [94:3:13.2] Sunkadhikari | Collector of tolls and customs
[94:3:14] # Army
[94:3:15] - **Mula Balam** = king's own standing army; **Gaja Sahini** (elephants) = **Jayapa Senani** under Ganapatideva; **Ashwa Sahini** (cavalry) = **Gangaya Sahini**.
[94:3:16] - **Giridurga** = hill fort (also Jala, Vana, Sthala durgas); **Padmanayakas** = Recherla Velama chiefs, key commanders.
[94:3:17] - Warangal fort: inner stone wall with **45 bastions**.
[94:3:18] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Kakatiyas p.19-23, p.55; app notes 1:94 (sub 0, 1, 3, 4)
## SUB 4 | Tanks, Agriculture and Crafts
[94:4:0] TABLE head: Tank | Builder
  [94:4:0.0] Pakhala | Mummadi Nayaka (not Mailamba)
  [94:4:0.1] Laknavaram, Ghanapuram | Ganapatideva
  [94:4:0.2] Bayyaram | Mailamba
  [94:4:0.3] Santana Sagaram / Govardhana Samudram | Surambika (Reddi period)
[94:4:1] - **Golusukattu cheruvulu** = linked **chain tanks**; **Dashabandhamu** = tax-free land for tank upkeep.
[94:4:2] - **Sapta Santanalu:** tank-building was one of the seven **meritorious acts**.
[94:4:3] - **Porumamilla inscription (1369):** **Bhaskara, son of Bukka I** (Vijayanagara) – 12 requisites of a good tank.
[94:4:4] - **Crops:** fragrant rice near Orugallu, sugarcane, cotton; **maize was not grown**.
[94:4:5] TABLE head: Product | Centre
  [94:4:5.0] Ratna kambalu (diamond blankets), carpets | Warangal
  [94:4:5.1] Knives | Nirmal
  [94:4:5.2] Iron | Guthikonda and Palnadu
[94:4:6] - **Palnati Veeracharitra:** about **1,500 painters' houses** in Orugallu; **Machaladevi** was a woman painter.
[94:4:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Kakatiyas p.27, p.63; app notes 1:94 (sub 2, 6, 7, 8)
