=== NOTES 1:95 | Kakatiya Society and Religion – Veerashaivism, Jainism, Temple Institutions
## SUB 0 | Shaiva Sects, Veerashaivism and the Aradhyas
[95:0:0] # Shaiva sects
[95:0:1] TABLE head: Sect | Founder / trait
  [95:0:1.0] Pasupata | Oldest Shaiva sect; founded by Lakulisa (Nakulisa), 1st–2nd c. AD; popular into the Reddi period, declined under Vijayanagara
  [95:0:1.1] Kalamukha | Founded by Kalasana (Kalanana), disciple of Lakulisa; extremist; temple managers, gave anna dana; Simha Parishads
  [95:0:1.2] Kapalika | Offshoot of Pasupata (the "Vamacharyas" of the Kalamukhas); worship Bhairava; skull-bowl, Panchamudras
  [95:0:1.3] Aradhya | Brahmin Shaivas led by Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya; kept Vedic ritual and varna
[95:0:2] - **Pasupata founder:** **Lakulisa** (APPSC PYQ) – not Basava (Veerashaivism), Bijjala (Kalachuri king) or Kallata.
[95:0:3] - **Kapalikas emerged from:** **Pasupata Shaivism** (APPSC G2 2019; APPSC PYQ).
[95:0:4]   - ⚠ Sources differ: NextGen's PYQ list says "the Kapalikas emerged from the school of **Misra Saivam**" – the app keys Pasupata (most books) and shows the dispute.
[95:0:5] - **Kakatiya patronage:** early kings (Beta, Durga) were disciples of **Kalamukha** acharyas of the Srisailam Silamatha; Kalamukha centres – **Srisailam, Alampur, Vemulawada, Kaleshwaram**, Tripurantakam.
[95:0:6] # Aradhya acharyas – Siddhatraya
[95:0:7] - **12 Aradhya acharyas** in **four triads**; **Siddhatraya** = **Revana, Marula, Ekorama** (G2 2012; APPSC PYQ).
[95:0:8] - **Not a Siddhacharya:** **Udbhata** – a Sanskrit poetician (alankarika).
[95:0:9] # Veerashaivism
[95:0:10] - **Founder:** **Basaveshwara** (Basava), minister of **Kalachuri Bijjala** (Karnataka); spread into Andhra in the Kakatiya period through **Palkuriki Somanatha** (Basavapuranam, Panditaradhya Charitra).
[95:0:11] - **Followers:** **Lingayats**; gurus **Jangamas**; in Andhra inscriptions called **Veeravratulu**; main Andhra centre **Srisailam**.
[95:0:12] - **Teaching:** **rejected** the Vedas, caste, child marriage and sacrifice → drew artisans and lower groups (social mobility).
[95:0:13] - **Reddi period:** the **popular religion was Veerashaivism** (G2 2011), alongside Pasupata patronised by the kings.
[95:0:14] > Kakatiya age = the **"Shaiva era"**; dynastic deity **Svayambhu Shiva**.
[95:0:15] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - APPSC 04 p.28 (sects); NextGen Kakatiyas p.31; NextGen Post-Kakatiyas (Reddi religion); NextGen Previous Papers p.47; app notes 1:95 (sub 3, 4)
## SUB 1 | Caste Associations (Samayas) and Non-Brahmin Rule
[95:1:0] # Samayas
[95:1:1] - **Samaya / Samayamu** = **caste association** (G2 PYQ; APPSC PYQ ×2) – not Sreni-bandham (guild), Sangha or Kutamu.
[95:1:2] - **Bodies:** Brahmins – **Mahajanulu**; Vaishyas (Komatis) – **Nakaramu**; violators fined (**Samayadandam**), enforced by the **Samaya Senapati**.
[95:1:3] TABLE head: Group | Body / castes
  [95:1:3.0] Brahmins | Mahajanas (Vaidikas vs Niyogis)
  [95:1:3.1] Vaishyas | Nakaram
  [95:1:3.2] Panchanamuvaru | The five artisan (smith) groups
  [95:1:3.3] Ashtadasha kulas | 18 occupational groups inside Warangal fort (Kridabhiramam)
  [95:1:3.4] Veerashaivism | New castes Lingayats, Balijas, Jangamas
  [95:1:3.5] Vaishnavism | Satanis, Dasaris
[95:1:4] # Non-Brahmanisation
[95:1:5] - **Culmination:** the non-Brahmanisation of religion and politics **culminated under the Kakatiyas** (G2 PYQ; APPSC PYQ) – not the Vengi Chalukyas, Pallavas or Rashtrakutas.
[95:1:6] - **Why:** the Kakatiyas were **Sudras** (of **Pulinda/Boya** origin) who rose through military service; officials came from warrior and peasant groups (Nayankara); **Brahmins lost political clout**.
[95:1:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen Kakatiyas p.37, p.69; NextGen AP History - APPSC 07 p.1; app notes 1:95 (sub 0, 1)
## SUB 2 | Law Books and Women's Property
[95:2:0] TABLE head: Book | Author | Theme
  [95:2:0.0] Vignanesvaram (Telugu Mitakshara) | Ketana ("Abhinava Dandi") | Women's property → daughters and daughters' daughters
  [95:2:0.1] Purushartha Saramu | Sivadevayya | Polity: 72 Niyogas, king's daily council routine
  [95:2:0.2] Nitisara | Rudradeva | Polity
  [95:2:0.3] Niti Shastra Muktavali | Baddena (not Sivadevayya) | Polity
[95:2:1] - **Women's property rule:** "a woman's property is inherited wholly by her **daughters and daughter's daughters**" – **Vignanesvaram of Ketana** (G2 PYQ; G2 2019).
[95:2:2]   - ⚠ Trap: the G2 2019 book key "Purushartha Saramu" is wrong – Sivadevayya's work is on polity.
[95:2:3] ~~ Sources: NextGen Previous Papers p.14; NextGen AP History - APPSC 07 p.1; NextGen Kakatiyas p.68; Rocket AP History (Ketana); app notes 1:95 (sub 6)
## SUB 3 | From Jainism to Shaivism
[95:3:0] - **Early Kakatiyas:** **Jains** (G2 2011) → **Shaiva** from **Prola II / Rudradeva**.
[95:3:1] - **Decline of Jainism:** **Kalamukha and Veerashaiva hostility**; Jain–Saiva conflicts from Rudradeva's reign.
[95:3:2] - **Jain centres:** **Bodhan, Vemulawada, Patancheru, Kolanupaka**, Hanumakonda (Anumakonda).
[95:3:3] - **Padmakshi temple, Hanumakonda:** built by **Prola II**, **originally a Jain shrine**.
[95:3:4] - **Kadalalaya Jain basadi, Anumakonda:** built by **Mailama, wife of minister Bethana (Chetana)** – a minister's family, not the king.
[95:3:5] - **Tolerance:** Vaishnava shrines (Thousand Pillar Vasudeva, Prasanna Keshava) were also endowed.
[95:3:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen Kakatiyas p.29, p.37, p.43; NextGen AP History - APPSC 11 p.11; app notes 1:95 (sub 2)
## SUB 4 | Temples as Institutions – the Malkapuram Inscription
[95:4:0] - **Temples:** **landed corporations** with lands and staff; attached **monasteries and feeding houses**; courtesans (**Kalavatis**) sustained dance and music.
[95:4:1] - **Malkapuram inscription (1261, Rudramadevi's reign):** **Visvesvara Sambhu** of the **Golaki matha** (Kalamukha-**Pasupata** Saiva lineage), guru of Ganapatideva, set up a Saiva matha, a **college**, a **feeding house**, a **maternity home (prasuti sala)** and a hospital at **Mandadam**.
[95:4:2] - **Pasupata Saiva sect record:** the **Malkapuram** inscription (Junior Asst. PYQ) – not Bayyaram (Mailamba's tank, genealogy), Hanumakonda or Kazipet Dargah (Beta's Betheswara temple).
[95:4:3] ~~ Sources: NextGen Kakatiyas p.3, p.71; Epigraphia Indica (Malkapuram pillar inscription); app notes 1:95 (sub 5)
## SUB 5 | Royal Women Donors and Hero-stones
[95:5:0] TABLE head: Donor | Grant
  [95:5:0.0] Mailamba, Ganapatideva's sister | Bayyaram tank and inscription (1219)
  [95:5:0.1] Kuppambika, wife of Malyala Gunda | Gundeswara temple, Buddapuram; daughter of Gona Budda Reddy; called the first Telugu woman poet
  [95:5:0.2] Lakshmidevi, Prataparudra II's queen | Ramanatha temple, Yelledu
  [95:5:0.3] Prataparudra II | Endowed the Chennakeshava temple (1321)
[95:5:1] - **Viragallu (hero-stones):** memorials of warriors who died **in battle or cattle raids**.
[95:5:2] ~~ Sources: app notes 1:95 (sub 6, 7)

=== NOTES 1:96 | Kakatiya Art – Thousand Pillar Temple, Ramappa (unesco 2021), Warangal Fort
## SUB 0 | Ramappa (Rudreswara) Temple, Palampet
[96:0:0] TABLE head: Particular | Fact
  [96:0:0.0] Builder | Recherla Rudra, general of Ganapatideva (not a Kakatiya king); title Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya
  [96:0:0.1] Year | 1213 CE
  [96:0:0.2] Place | Palampet, old Warangal district – now Mulugu district (since 2019), Telangana
  [96:0:0.3] Names | Rudreswaralayam; deity Shiva as Ramalingeswara; named after its sculptor Ramappa
  [96:0:0.4] Type | Ekasila / single-shrine (ekakuta) temple on a star-shaped platform
  [96:0:0.5] UNESCO | World Heritage Site, 25 July 2021
[96:0:1] - **Builder:** **Recherla (Racherla) Rudra** (G1 1990-91; Labs 2012; APPSC PYQ ×2) – not Ganapatideva, Rudramba, Jayapa or Chaunda Senani.
[96:0:2] - **Year:** **1213** (G1 1990-91; G1 1994) – 1162 is the Thousand Pillar temple.
[96:0:3] - **Dynasty:** the **Kakatiyas** (ASO 2011).
[96:0:4] - **Ramappa tank:** also built by **Recherla Rudra** (1213), in Ganapatideva's reign.
[96:0:5] - **District:** **Warangal** in the books (APPSC PYQ) – now **Mulugu**.
[96:0:6] - **Type:** keyed **"Monolithic" (Ekasila)** (G2 2012); strictly a single-shrine (ekakuta) temple – the Trikuta is the Thousand Pillar temple.
[96:0:7] - **"The brightest gem in the galaxy of medieval temples of the Deccan":** Ramappa at **Palampeta**.
[96:0:8] # Features
[96:0:9] - **Star-shaped** platform; **floating bricks** in the vimana; **sandbox foundation**.
[96:0:10] - **Madanika** bracket figures in dance poses; **28** elephant-lion (Gajakesari) figures.
[96:0:11] - **Painted ceilings** with Ramayana–Mahabharata scenes – Ramappa is a site of **Kakatiya paintings**.
[96:0:12] ~~ Sources: NextGen Kakatiyas p.33; NextGen AP History - APPSC 07 p.16, p.23; NextGen AP History - APPSC 08 p.21; UNESCO WHC 1570; app notes 1:96 (sub 3)

## SUB 3 | Jayapa's Nritta Ratnavali and Perini Shiva Tandavam
[96:3:0] TABLE head: Work | Author | Post / court | Link
  [96:3:0.0] Nritta Ratnavali (Sanskrit) | Jayapa Senani (Jayana, Jayapa Nayaka) | Gaja Sahini (head of the elephant corps) of Ganapatideva | Ramappa madanika poses follow it
  [96:3:0.1] Gita Ratnavali, Vadya Ratnavali | Jayapa Senani | same | Music and instruments
  [96:3:0.2] Sangita Ratnakara | Sarangadeva | Yadavas of Devagiri | General music-dance treatise
[96:3:1] - **Author:** **Jayapa Senani** (G2-A 1989; Labs 2012) – not Racherla Rudra, Prolaya Nayaka or Ganapatideva.
[96:3:2] - **Profession:** **Gaja Sahini** (G2 2019; G2 PYQ) – not Asva Sahini, architect or dancer.
[96:3:3] - **Reign:** **Ganapatideva** (G1 2010; G1 PYQ) – a general and scholar of his court.
[96:3:4] - **Ramappa dance sculptures:** carved on the principles of **Jayapa's Nritta Ratnavali** (G2 2019 ×2) – not Ranganatha Ramayana or a separate "marga/desi" book; the text itself covers **Marga** (classical) and **Desi** (folk) dance and describes **Perini**.
[96:3:5] # Perini Shiva Tandavam
[96:3:6] - **What:** warrior dance of **male warriors before battle**, invoking Shiva, to drum beats; postures carved at Ramappa.
[96:3:7] - **Revived by:** **Nataraja Ramakrishna** (G2 PYQ; APPSC PYQ) from Nritta Ratnavali and the **Ramappa / Thousand Pillar** sculptures – not Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma, Yamini Krishnamurthy or Raja-Radha Reddy.
[96:3:8] ~~ Sources: NextGen Kakatiyas p.31, p.33; NextGen AP History - APPSC 07 p.1; app notes 1:96 (sub 7)

## SUB 5 | Kakatiya Rulers and Builders
[96:5:0] TABLE head: Ruler | Key facts
  [96:5:0.0] Rudradeva (Prataparudra I, 1158) | Thousand Pillar temple; began Orugallu
  [96:5:0.1] Mahadeva | After Rudradeva, before Ganapatideva

  [96:5:0.3] Rudramadevi (1262) | Title Rayagaja Kesari; Marco Polo visited
  [96:5:0.4] Prataparudra (1296) | Last ruler; ascended after Rudramadevi
[96:5:1] - **Brightest period of Telugu history:** the **Kakatiya** period – it unified the Telugu lands.
[96:5:2] - **Builders:** **Recherla Rudra** (not of the dynasty) – Ramappa; **Vellanki Gangadhara** – Prasanna Keshava; **Jagadala Mummadi** – **Pakhal** tank.

## SUB 6 | Kakatiya Style – Techniques and Features
[96:6:0] TABLE head: Feature | What it is
  [96:6:0.0] Stellate plan | Raised star-shaped platform
  [96:6:0.1] Sandbox foundation | Pits filled with sand, stone chips and earth – absorbs shocks; earthquake-resistant heritage engineering
  [96:6:0.2] Floating bricks | Light porous bricks in Ramappa's vimana – reduce dead weight of the tower
  [96:6:0.3] Ekasila | Monolithic carving (Nandi, pillars)
  [96:6:0.4] Kirtimukha | "Face of glory" motif (not monolithic carving)
  [96:6:0.5] Madanikas | Bracket figures on outer walls
[96:6:1] - **Style:** **Chalukyan / Vesara**, influence of the **Western Chalukyas of Kalyani**; **transitional** between early Chalukyan and Vijayanagara.
[96:6:2] - **Padmakshi temple** (Hanamkonda) was originally **Jain**.
[96:6:3] ~~ Sources: NextGen Kakatiyas p.33; app notes 1:96 (sub 4, 5)
## SUB 7 | Warangal Fort, Kala Thoranam and Kridabhiramam
[96:7:0] TABLE head: Line | Feature
  [96:7:0.0] Puttakota | Innermost enclosure
  [96:7:0.1] Mud fort (Mattikota) | 20 ft, moat, four gates
  [96:7:0.2] Kalukota | Outer stone fort, 77 towers
[96:7:1] - **Fort:** begun by Rudradeva, **completed by Ganapatideva**; Rudramadevi added a step-arch.
[96:7:2] - **Kakatiya Kala Thoranam:** **four ornate stone gateways** around the **Swayambhu Shiva** temple; in the **Telangana State emblem**.
[96:7:3] - **Ulugh Khan (1323):** **ruined** the Swayambhu temple – he did not build the Thoranams.
[96:7:4] - **Kridabhiramam:** **Vinukonda Vallabharaya**; a **Veedhi natakam** on life in Orugallu (abode of drama artists); English **"A Lover's Guide to Warangal"** by **David Shulman and Velcheru Narayana Rao**.
[96:7:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen Kakatiyas p.75; app notes 1:96 (sub 8)

=== NOTES 1:97 | Temple Architecture Styles of Andhradesa (11TH–16TH Centuries)
## SUB 0 | Famous Temples of Andhra Pradesh
[97:0:0] TABLE head: Temple | Deity | Point
  [97:0:0.0] Srikurmam (Srikakulam) | Kurma (Vishnu's 2nd avatara) | Only Kurma temple; only AP temple with two flagpoles (dhwajastambhas)
  [97:0:0.1] Arasavalli (Srikakulam) | Surya | The Sun temple of Andhra
  [97:0:0.2] Simhachalam | Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha | Present temple of Eastern Ganga Narasimha Deva I; Kalinga style
  [97:0:0.3] Mukhalingam | Madhukeswara | Eastern Ganga capital Kalinganagari
  [97:0:0.4] Kotappakonda (Palnadu) | Trikoteswara (Shiva) | Grand Maha Sivaratri festival
  [97:0:0.5] Lepakshi (Sri Sathya Sai) | Veerabhadra | Hanging pillar; Vijayanagara paintings
[97:0:1] - **Two flagpoles:** **Srikurmam** (G2 2001, 2002) – not Tirumala, Simhachalam or Yadagirigutta.
[97:0:2] - **Srikurmam district:** **Srikakulam** (Sachivalayam PYQ; the stem's "10th avatara" is wrong – Kurma is the 2nd).
[97:0:3] - **Sun temple:** **Arasavalli** (AEE 2008; IAS 2017 – only I; Amarkantak and Omkareshwar are not Sun temples).
[97:0:4] - **Maha Sivaratri in grand manner:** **Kotappakonda**.
[97:0:5] - **Jyotirlingas:** **12** (CGPSC 2011, 2012); AP's = **Srisailam** (Mallikarjuna).
[97:0:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - APPSC 07 (Arasavalli, Kotappakonda); Rocket AP History (temples table); app notes 1:97 (sub 3, 4)
## SUB 1 | Temple Components and the Three Orders
[97:1:0] - **Core:** **garbhagriha** + **mandapa**; **shikhara** (north) or **vimana** (south); axial **vahana with dhvaja pillar**.
[97:1:1] - **Dwarapalakas:** door-guardian figures **left and right** of the entrance or gopuram (Endowment 2022) – dikpalakas guard the eight directions, kshetrapalakas the site.
[97:1:2] - **Trikutalaya:** three shrines on one plan (Thousand Pillar temple).
[97:1:3] TABLE head: Order | Marker | Andhra example
  [97:1:3.0] Nagara | Curvilinear shikhara | Kalinga variant: Mukhalingam, Simhachalam
  [97:1:3.1] Dravida | Pyramidal vimana, gopurams | Eastern Chalukya delta temples; Vijayanagara
  [97:1:3.2] Vesara | Blend | Kakatiya temples
[97:1:4] - **Pattadakal:** **Papanatha** = Nagara; Virupaksha = Dravida.
[97:1:5] - **Siddhavatam (Kadapa):** western gopuram in a **1233 CE** Tamil-Grantha inscription of **Chola Rajendra III**.
[97:1:6] ~~ Sources: PMF Art & Culture 03 (temple parts); app notes 1:97 (sub 0)
## SUB 2 | Styles by Dynasty
[97:2:0] TABLE head: Dynasty | Features | Examples
  [97:2:0.0] Eastern Chalukya | Dravidian, from Pallava and Badami forms; laterite and limestone | Vijayaditya II – 108 temples; Biccavolu
  [97:2:0.1] Chalukya-Chola | Model for the Godavari region | Draksharama – Chalukya Bhima I
  [97:2:0.2] Kakatiya | Vesara; star platforms, sandbox, floating bricks – not wooden superstructures | Ramappa (1213), Thousand Pillar (Shiva, Vishnu, Surya – not Brahma)
  [97:2:0.3] Reddi | Renovations; forts | Kondaveedu (Guntur–Palnadu, near Chilakaluripet)
  [97:2:0.4] Vijayanagara | Chalukya and Chola roots (not Hoysala/Kalinga); Sahasra Stambha (thousand-pillared kalyana) mandapa, gopurams | Hampi; Lepakshi
[97:2:1] - **Eastern Chalukya ✗ trap:** "pure Vesara on Hoysala models" is wrong.
[97:2:2] ~~ Sources: app notes 1:97 (sub 1)
## SUB 3 | Pancharamas and Srisailam
[97:3:0] TABLE head: Pancharama | Place
  [97:3:0.0] Amararama | Amaravati
  [97:3:0.1] Draksharama | Draksharama – Shakti peetha Manikyamba
  [97:3:0.2] Somarama | Bhimavaram
  [97:3:0.3] Ksheerarama | Palakollu
  [97:3:0.4] Kumararama | Samalkot – Reddi additions
[97:3:1] - **Srisailam:** **Prolaya Vema Reddy** – steps to **Patalaganga (1346)**; **Anavema Reddy** – **Veera Siromandapam**; Shakti peetha **Bhramaramba**.
[97:3:2] - **2026:** master plans for **22** major temples (Simhachalam, Annavaram, Srikalahasti, Kanipakam).
[97:3:3] ~~ Sources: app notes 1:97 (sub 4)
## SUB 4 | Materials, Sculpture and Painting
[97:4:0] TABLE head: Material | Dynasty | Example
  [97:4:0.0] Sandstone hill | Vishnukundinas | Undavalli caves
  [97:4:0.1] Granite monolith | Vishnukundinas | Reclining Ananta Padmanabha, Undavalli
  [97:4:0.2] Black basalt (ekasila) | Kakatiyas | Thousand Pillar Nandi
  [97:4:0.3] Floating bricks | Kakatiyas | Ramappa vimana
[97:4:1] - **Sandbox technology:** foundation pits of sand, stone chips and earth cushion temples (Ramappa) against earthquakes.
[97:4:2] - **Ramappa madanikas** follow **Nritta Ratnavali** of **Jayapa Senani** (commander of **Ganapatideva**); Ramappa = UNESCO **2021**, built **1213**.
[97:4:3] - **Perini** revived by **Nataraja Ramakrishna**.
[97:4:4] - **Kakatiya painting (Machaladevi)** led to the **Lepakshi** style.

  Sandbox foundations | Floating bricks | *Sahasra Stambha Mandapa | Star-shaped platforms
  x: Vijayanagara temples are marked by the Sahasra Stambha Mandapa and composite carved pillars; the other three are Kakatiya features.

  x: Kumararama is at Samalkot (Chalukya Bhimavaram); Somarama is at Bhimavaram, Ksheerarama at Palakollu and Amararama at Amaravati.

[nf8850b862c5] sub4
  What does the Kakatiya 'sandbox technology' used in temples such as Ramappa refer to?
  *Foundation pits filled with sand, stone chips and earth that cushioned the temple against earthquakes | Sand-cast bronze images placed in the garbhagriha | Hollow sand-filled pillars that lightened the vimana | A sand moat dug around the temple for defence
  x: Kakatiya builders filled foundation pits with sand, stone chips and earth to cushion temples on black cotton soil, which is why Ramappa survived earthquakes.

=== NOTES 1:98 | Reddi Kingdoms of Addanki, Kondavidu and Rajahmundry – Prolaya Vema Reddi to Kumaragiri Reddi
## SUB 0 | Court Poets – Errana and Srinatha
[98:0:0] # Errana (Errapragada)
[98:0:1] - **Patron:** court poet of the founder **Prolaya Vema Reddi** (APPSC G2 2011, 2012; APPSC PYQ ×5) – not Anavota, Anavema, Allada Reddi or Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka.
[98:0:2] - **Dedication:** his **Harivamsam** is dedicated to **Prolaya Vema**.
[98:0:3] - **Kavitrayam:** **last of the Kavitrayam**; completed the Telugu Mahabharata (**remaining Aranya Parva – Aranya Parva shesham**).
[98:0:4] - **Works:** **Nrisimha (Narasimha) Puranam** (APPSC G2 2017; PYQ ×2), Harivamsam, Ramayana.
[98:0:5] - **Titles:** **Prabandha Parameswara**, **Sambhudasa**.
[98:0:6] - **⚠ Trap:** the **Vidyadhikari** (education officer) post belonged to **Srinatha**, not Errana – a stem that calls Errana "Vidyadhikari" still points to his patron Prolaya Vema.
[98:0:7] # Srinatha (c. 1365–1441)
[98:0:8] - **Patron and office:** **Vidyadhikari** (education officer) under **Pedakomati Vema Reddi** (APPSC G1 2002; G2 2001, 2002; Welfare Officers 2017; PYQ ×2); composed his Sanskrit inscriptions.
[98:0:9] - **Title:** **Kavi Sarvabhauma**; also Andhra Bhasha Naishadhabhava, Sarvavidya Parangata.
[98:0:10] - **At Vijayanagara:** defeated **Gauda Dindima Bhatta**, court poet of **Deva Raya II** → **Kanakabhishekam**, **Ganda Penderam** and the Kavisarvabhauma honour.
[98:0:11] - **Later life:** after 1424 joined the Rajahmundry court of **Veerabhadra Reddi**; after 1448, poverty in Palnadu.
[98:0:12] TABLE head: Work | Note
  [98:0:12.0] Haravilasam | Sea-borne trade; to Avachi Tippayya Setti
  [98:0:12.1] Palnati Veera Charitra | Life of the Palnadu people (PYQ)
  [98:0:12.2] Sringara Naishadham | From Sriharsha's Naishadhiyacharita; to Mamidi (Madiki) Singana
  [98:0:12.3] Bhimakhandam (Bhimeswara Puranam) | Praises Bhimeswara of Draksharamam
  [98:0:12.4] Kasikhandam | Religious; to Veerabhadra Reddi's court
  [98:0:12.5] Sivaratri Mahatyam, Maruttarat Charitra | Other works
[98:0:13] - **Kavya Yuga:** Srinatha is said to have opened the Kavya (prabandha) age; his writings are cited as evidence of **paper** use in the **15th century** (APPSC G2 2012).
[98:0:14] - **⚠ Not his:** **Madanavilasabanam** (Naganatha, Anavota's court) is NOT by Srinatha.
[98:0:15] # Other Court Poets
[98:0:16] TABLE head: Poet | Patron | Works / titles
  [98:0:16.0] Vamana Bhatta Bana | Pedakomati Vema | Vema Bhupala Charitra (prose life of Pedakomati), Nalabhyudayam, Hamsa Sandesam, Usha Parinayam, Kanaka Rekha Kalyanam, Shabda Ratnakaram; title Sahitya Chudamani
  [98:0:16.1] Bala Saraswati | Anavota | Composed Anavota's Sanskrit inscriptions
  [98:0:16.2] Bammera Potana | Contemporary of Pedakomati and Srinatha | Andhra Bhagavatam, Narayana Satakam, Bhogini Dandakam, Veerabhadra Vijayam
[98:0:17] ~~ Sources: NextGen post kakatiyas p.7, p.9-11, p.15; NextGen AP History - APPSC Exams 08 p.23-26; Rocket Sheets p.5, p.9, p.26; app notes 1:98 (sub 10)
## SUB 1 | Ruler-Authors and Their Works
[98:1:0] TABLE head: Work | Author | Note
  [98:1:0.0] Sangeeta Chintamani | Pedakomati Vema | Music (APPSC G2 2011 ×3, 2019; PYQ ×3)
  [98:1:0.1] Sahitya Chintamani | Pedakomati Vema | Poetics – not by Potana
  [98:1:0.2] Srungara Deepika | Pedakomati Vema | On Amaru Shataka
  [98:1:0.3] Saptasati Saratika | Pedakomati Vema | On Gatha Saptasati
  [98:1:0.4] Vasantarajiyam | Kumaragiri | Sanskrit, on dance (APPSC G2 2012)
  [98:1:0.5] Kumaragiri Rajiyam | Kataya Vema | Commentary on Kalidasa's three plays – only named after Kumaragiri
  [98:1:0.6] Sangeeta Sudhakaram | Singabhupala II | Recherla Velama of Rachakonda – not a Reddi
  [98:1:0.7] Kavyalankara Chudamani | Vinnakota Peddana | Rajahmundry literary circle
  [98:1:0.8] Tatva Prakashika | Sivalinga Reddi (Kandukur) | –
[98:1:1] - **Pedakomati Vema (1402–1420):** title **Sarvajna Chakravarti**; the Reddi king skilled in **music**; author of the four works above.
[98:1:2] - **Kumaragiri:** expert in **Bharata Natya**; title **Karpura Vasantarayalu**.
[98:1:3] - **Match (Prelims 2023):** Vasantarajiyam – Kumaragiri; Srungara Naishadham – Srinatha; Sahitya Chintamani – Pedakomati Vema; Vema Bhupala Charitra – Vamana Bhatta Bana → **all four correct**.
[98:1:4] - **⚠ Trap:** **Sarangadhara/Sarngadeva** wrote Sangita Ratnakara, the text Singabhupala II commented on – not Sangeeta Chintamani.

## SUB 2 | Society, Festivals and Women
[98:2:0] # Vasantotsavam and Dance
[98:2:1] - **Vasantotsavam (spring festival):** the **most popular festival** of the Reddi period – colours and scents sprinkled (Holi-like) (APPSC G2 PYQ).
[98:2:2] - **Popularised by:** **Kumaragiri Reddi**, who held it every year → title **Karpura Vasantarayalu** (Welfare Officers 2017 ×2); Anavema too was called Vasantaraya.
[98:2:3] - **Funding:** merchant **Avachi Tippayya Setti**, made head of the **Sugandha Bhandagara** (scent store) for the festival (recorded in Haravilasam).
[98:2:4] - **Court dancer:** **Lakumadevi** – **Bharatanatyam**, at **Kumaragiri's** court (APPSC G2 2012; PYQ ×3) – not Machaladevi, Chellava or Muddupalani.
[98:2:5] - **Literature on him:** **C. Narayana Reddy** wrote **Karpura Vasanta Rayalu** on Kumaragiri.
[98:2:6] # Women and Tanks
[98:2:7] TABLE head: Woman | Fact
  [98:2:7.0] Surambika (Suryambika) | Queen of Pedakomati Vema; dug the Santana Sagaram (Santana Payonidhi) tank at Phirangipuram (APPSC G2 2019; PYQ ×2)
  [98:2:7.1] Lakumadevi | Court dancer of Kumaragiri Reddi
  [98:2:7.2] Anitalli | Issued the Kaluvacheru inscription (1423)
[98:2:8] - **Tank inscription:** composed by **Srinatha**; her son **Racha Vema** cut the **Jaganobbaganda** canals to feed it.
[98:2:9] - **⚠ Trap:** **Govardhana Samudram**, Anna Samudram and Vemana Samudram are NOT Surambika's tank – the answer is **Santana Sagaram**.
[98:2:10] # Social Life
[98:2:11] - **Castes:** warrior-farmer backbone **Kammas, Kapus, Reddis, Velamas**; traders **Komatis**; tax-free Brahmin **agraharas**.
[98:2:12] - **Customs:** sati, devadasis, cockfights, ram fights, hero worship (Veerapuja); belief in **Parusavedi** (alchemy).
[98:2:13] - **Devadasis:** trained in music, dance and ritual; respected performers at **Shiva temples** (incl. Pancharamas).
[98:2:14] - **Time:** measured with clocks – the **Ghatika Yantra** (water clock), called **Ghatikagara** in the APPSC key (Telugu "gadiyaram" = clock).
[98:2:15] - **Music:** instrument **Jalakaranda** – **Dharmasagara inscription**; desi dances Jakkini, Perani; foreign dance Parasika.
[98:2:16] ~~ Sources: NextGen post kakatiyas p.6, p.9, p.12-14; NextGen AP History - APPSC Exams 08 p.24-25; Rocket Sheets p.7; app notes 1:98 (sub 7)
## SUB 3 | Rulers, Capitals and Chronology
[98:3:0] # The Reddi Kingdom
[98:3:1] - **Period:** about **1325–1448 CE** – **Kondavidu line c. 1325–1424**; **Rajahmundry line 1402–1448**.
[98:3:2] - **Successor state:** one of the three states after **1323** (fall of the Kakatiyas) – **Reddis, Musunuris, Recherla Velamas**.
[98:3:3] - **Called:** the **"second golden age" of Telugu** culture – kings were themselves authors.
[98:3:4] - **Features:** **Panta** clan (Deseti kula); emblem **Bull**; family deity **Mula Guramma**; royal language **Sanskrit**.
[98:3:5] # Kondavidu Rulers in Order
[98:3:6] TABLE head: Ruler | Period | Key fact
  [98:3:6.0] Prolaya Vema Reddi (founder) | 1325–1353 | Capital Addanki; expelled Tughlaq forces; 74 forts; Errana
  [98:3:6.1] Anavota (Anapota) Reddi | 1353–1364 | Shifted capital to Kondavidu; developed Motupalli; abolished gold tax
  [98:3:6.2] Anavema Reddi (greatest) | 1364–1386 | Most charitable; beat Kalinga Gajapatis; Veera Siromandapam
  [98:3:6.3] Kumaragiri Reddi | 1386–1402 | Vasantarajiyam; Vasantotsavam; Lakumadevi
  [98:3:6.4] Pedakomati Vema Reddi | 1402–1420 | Sangeeta Chintamani; Srinatha
  [98:3:6.5] Racha Vema Reddi (last) | 1420–1424 | Puriti Pannu; killed by his people
[98:3:7] - **Order (APPSC G2 Mains 2025; Welfare Officers):** Prolaya Vema → **Anavota → Anavema → Kumaragiri → Pedakomati Vema** → Racha Vema.
[98:3:8] - **Prolaya Vema's reign:** up to **1353** (Mani Kesavara inscription) – the "1325–1353" span (Inter Board 2012).
[98:3:9] - **Kumaragiri succeeded Anavema**; Pedakomati occupied Kondavidu (1402) because Kumaragiri was childless.
[98:3:10] # Capitals and Forts
[98:3:11] - **Sequence:** **Addanki → Kondaveedu (Kondavidu) → Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry)**.
[98:3:12] - **Who shifted Addanki → Kondavidu:** **Anavota (Anapota) Reddi**, son of Prolaya Vema – **Manyapuram inscription** (APPSC G2 2012; PYQ) – not Anavema, Kumaragiri or Pedakomati.
[98:3:13] TABLE head: Capital / fort | Region | Feature
  [98:3:13.0] Addanki | Prakasam | First capital, Prolaya Vema
  [98:3:13.1] Kondavidu | Guntur (near Chilakaluripet) | Replaced Addanki; later fought over by Gajapatis and Vijayanagara
  [98:3:13.2] Rajahmundry | Godavari | Second seat, 1402–1448
  [98:3:13.3] Kondapalli | Krishna | Hill fort credited to Prolaya Vema
[98:3:14] - **Forts:** Prolaya Vema built **74 forts**, including **Kondaveedu, Kondapalli and Dharanikota**.
[98:3:15] - **Kondapalli fort:** main gate **Dargah Darwaza** (tomb of Gulab Shah); **Golconda Darwaza** at the other end; palace **Tanisha Mahal**.
[98:3:16] - **⚠ Trap:** Kondavidu is in Guntur – NOT in East Godavari or near Eluru.
[98:3:17] # Prolaya Vema Reddi – Founder
[98:3:18] - **Career:** served **Prataparudra**, then in **Kapaya Nayaka's** court (Anitalli / Kaluvacheru inscription); founded the kingdom in **1324/1325** after expelling **Tughlaq** forces from coastal Andhra.
[98:3:19] - **Brother Mallareddi:** took **Motupalli**, repulsing the Bahmani **Hasan Gangu** (1347).
[98:3:20] # Anavema and Kumaragiri
[98:3:21] - **Anavema:** with the **Padmanayakas and Vijayanagara** beat the **Kalinga Gajapatis**; took **Nidadavolu** (gave it to Choda Bhima), **Rajahmundry, Pithapuram, Simhachalam, Konaseema** – not Kandukur; minister **Mamidi Peddanamatya**, army chief **Chennamanayaka**; **most charitable** Reddi king.
[98:3:22] - **Kumaragiri:** **Pedakomati Vema**, who opposed his accession, was made **feudatory of Chandolu** and heir; brother-in-law **Kataya Vema** conquered the east up to **Cuttack**.
[98:3:23] - **Rajahmundry division:** first under his son **Anavota**, then **Kataya Vema (1395)**.
[98:3:24] - **1402:** Pedakomati seized Kondavidu; Kumaragiri fled to Rajahmundry.
[98:3:25] - **Pedakomati Vema:** recovered territory from **Vijayanagara (1404)**; died fighting the Velamas (1420).
[98:3:26] - **Racha Vema:** last Kondavidu king; killed as a tyrant – **Kondaveeti Kaifiyat**.
[98:3:27] ~~ Sources: NextGen post kakatiyas p.3, p.5-9; NextGen AP History - APPSC Exams 08 p.23; Rocket Sheets p.7, p.42, p.47; app notes 1:98 (sub 0, 1, 2)
## SUB 4 | Trade – Motupalli Port and Haravilasam
[98:4:0] - **Haravilasam (Srinatha):** the Reddi-period work giving information on **sea-borne (foreign) trade**, imports and exports (APPSC G2 2011 ×2, 2012, 2019; G2 Mains; PYQ) – not Harivamsam, Kasikhandam or Bhimeswara Puranam.
[98:4:1] - **Dedicated to:** merchant **Avachi Tippayya Setti**, famous for **overseas trade** (China, Sinhala, Sumatra, Malaya).
[98:4:2] - **Assertion–Reason:** Haravilasam gives sea-trade information (A) and is dedicated to Tippayya Setti (R) – **both true, R not the explanation**.
[98:4:3] - **Motupalli:** chief Reddi port; taken by **Mallaya Reddi**; dock developed by **Anavota**.
[98:4:4] - **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam:** issued by **Somaya**, minister of **Anavota**, to protect and encourage trade (bilingual Telugu–Tamil; lower duties).
[98:4:5] - **Motupalli epigraph:** fixes **tariff rates** on port trade.
[98:4:6] - **Imports:** Chinese goods, sandalwood, camphor, spices; elephants from Sri Lanka.
[98:4:7] - **Traders:** **Komatis** ran inland and coastal trade; trade centres Penugonda, Kondaveedu, Rajahmundry, Draksharama.
[98:4:8] - **Earlier route:** the Buddhist **Vinayavatthu** mentions the **"Andhra Path"**.
[98:4:9] ~~ Sources: NextGen post kakatiyas p.10, p.13; NextGen AP History - APPSC Exams 08 p.23-26; Rocket Sheets p.9; app notes 1:98 (sub 6)
## SUB 5 | Religion and Temple Building
[98:5:0] - **Popular religion:** **Veerashaivism** (APPSC G2 2011; PYQ); the kings patronised **Pashupata Shaivism** – the tempting wrong option.
[98:5:1] - **Ghoderayas:** Shaiva gurus who spread Shaivism from **Tripurantakam**; the Reddi kings were their disciples.
[98:5:2] - **Vaishnavism:** **Vadagalai** matha at **Ahobilam**; **Kumaragiri and Kataya Vema** were Vaishnava patrons.
[98:5:3] - **Srisailam practices:** Bhrugupatham (leaping from the hill); **Champudu Gullu** at Tripurantakam.
[98:5:4] TABLE head: Work | Builder
  [98:5:4.0] Veera Siromandapam, Srisailam (for Siro-karthanam devotees) | Anavema (APPSC G2 2011; PYQ)
  [98:5:4.1] Anavemagiri mandapas, Simhachalam | Anavema
  [98:5:4.2] Steps (Sopanamargas) to Patala Ganga, Srisailam (1346) and to Ahobilam | Prolaya Vema (not Pedakomati)
  [98:5:4.3] Pilgrim rest-houses at Ahobilam and Srisailam; walls of Ahobilam and Mahanandi | Prolaya Vema
  [98:5:4.4] Amareswara temple, Amaravati restored | Vallaya Vemana, minister of Anavota
[98:5:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen post kakatiyas p.5, p.7-8, p.12-13; NextGen AP History - APPSC Exams 08 p.23; Rocket Sheets p.25, p.45; app notes 1:98 (sub 8)

  [98:6:5.4] Kaluvacheru (1423) | Anitalli | Recapture of Rajahmundry; the 75 Nayakas of the liberation
  [98:6:5.5] Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam | Somaya (Anavota) | Trade
  [98:6:5.6] Sarpavaram | Kataya Vema | Treaty with Harihara II
[98:6:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen post kakatiyas p.4, p.7-8, p.14; Rocket Sheets p.7, p.47; NextGen previous papers (Rachur Durgavibhala); app notes 1:98 (sub 11)
## SUB 7 | Administration and Taxes
[98:7:0] - **Puriti Pannu:** tax on **childbirth**, levied by **Racha Vema**, the last Kondavidu king, who was killed by his people for it (APPSC G2 2019; PYQ ×2) – not Kumaragiri, Kataya Vema or Anavota.
[98:7:1] TABLE head: Tax | Meaning
  [98:7:1.0] Puriti Pannu | Childbirth – Racha Vema
  [98:7:1.1] Kanika | Presents / gifts to king or officials
  [98:7:1.2] Pullari | Cattle-grazing tax (Kakatiya usage)
  [98:7:1.3] Illari | House tax
  [98:7:1.4] Ari | Land tax
  [98:7:1.5] Meruka | Tax on wetlands
  [98:7:1.6] Gold tax | Abolished by Anavota
[98:7:2] - **Land revenue:** Bhumi Sistu – the main income; land measured with the Kesarpati gada.
[98:7:3] - **Village:** **12 Ayagars** – **Karnam** (accountant), **Reddi / Peddakapu** (headman), **Talari** (watchman); paid in **Manyam** land or **Mera** (crop share).
[98:7:4] - **Exempt:** temple lands, Brahmin grants and Ayagar lands.
[98:7:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen post kakatiyas p.5, p.13-14; Rocket Sheets p.10; app notes 1:98 (sub 5)
## SUB 8 | Rajahmundry Reddis, Wars and the End of Reddi Rule
[98:8:0] TABLE head: Ruler | Period | Fact
  [98:8:0.0] Anavota (Kumaragiri's son) | to 1395 | First ruler of the division
  [98:8:0.1] Kataya Vema Reddi | 1395–1414 | Fought Pedakomati; killed at Kakaraparthi (1414) by Gajaraju Tippa
  [98:8:0.2] Allada Reddi (regent) | 1414–c. 1420 | Ran the state for Veerabhadra Reddi
  [98:8:0.3] Veerabhadra Reddi | c. 1414–1448 | Nominal king; husband of Anitalli
  [98:8:0.4] Vema (Veda) Reddi | 1423–1448 | Prime minister and de facto ruler
[98:8:1] - **Anitalli:** daughter of **Kataya Vema**, wife of **Veerabhadra Reddi**; issued the **Kaluvacheru** inscription after the **recapture of Rajahmundry** (1423).
[98:8:2] - **Allada Reddi's conflict:** **Deva Raya I** backed Kataya Vema against Kondavidu; **Annadeva** took parts of Vengi with **Velama** support.
[98:8:3] # Wars by Opponent
[98:8:4] TABLE head: Opponent | Event
  [98:8:4.0] Velamas | Battle of Bhimavaram – Reddis expelled the Velamas from Palnadu (APPSC G2 2019 key)
  [98:8:4.1] Bahmanis | Mallareddi took Motupalli from Hasan Gangu; Gajarao Tippa beat Firoz Shah's army at Kambhammetta (1396)
  [98:8:4.2] Vijayanagara | Kataya Vema beat Harihara II; Sarpavaram treaty – Harihara's daughter Vijayalakshmi married Kataya's son
  [98:8:4.3] Gajapatis | Anavema beat the Kalinga Gajapatis; Kapileswara annexed Rajahmundry (1446–48)
[98:8:5] # Rajahmundry Between Gajapati and Vijayanagara
[98:8:6] TABLE head: Year | Event
  [98:8:6.0] 1420 | Gajapati Ganga Ganapati took Rajahmundry
  [98:8:6.1] 1423 | Veerabhadra and Vema recovered it
  [98:8:6.2] 1429 | Veerabhanu Deva occupied it; Deva Raya II expelled him up to Simhachalam and restored the Reddis as feudatories
  [98:8:6.3] 1446–48 | Kapileswara Gajapati annexed Rajahmundry
[98:8:7] - **Deva Raya II:** title **Gajabetekara** ("hunter of elephants"); enlisted Muslim **archers** (Ferishta).
[98:8:8] # End of Reddi Rule
[98:8:9] TABLE head: Line | Ended by
  [98:8:9.0] Kondavidu | Vijayanagara (Deva Raya II), 1424 → Rajahmundry survived 24 more years as a Vijayanagara feudatory
  [98:8:9.1] Rajahmundry | Kapileswara Gajapati of Orissa, 1448
  [98:8:9.2] Kandukur branch | Deva Raya I reduced them to feudatories
[98:8:10] ~~ Sources: NextGen post kakatiyas p.9; NextGen AP History - APPSC Exams 08 p.24; app notes 1:98 (sub 3, 4)

  Devaraya II of Vijayanagara | Veerabhadra Reddy of Rajahmundry | *Pedakomati Vema Reddy of Kondaveedu | Sarvajna Singabhupala of Rachakonda
  x: Srinatha was Vidyadhikari at the Kondaveedu court of Pedakomati Vema Reddy and wrote the king's Sanskrit inscriptions. Under Veerabhadra Reddy at Rajahmundry he wrote Bhimakhandam and Kasikhandam; at Devaraya II's court he won the title Kavi Sarvabhauma; Sarvajna Singabhupala is linked with Potana's refusal of patronage.

=== NOTES 1:99 | Musunuri Nayaks and the Velama (recherla) Chiefs of Rachakonda–devarakonda
## SUB 0 | Liberation Movement and Prolaya Nayaka
[99:0:0] # Fall of Warangal (1323)
[99:0:1] - **1323:** Warangal fell; **Prataparudra** died (jumped into the Narmada); **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** renamed it **Sultanpur (Sultanpurti)**; Andhra under **Malik Burhanuddin**, deputy **Malik Maqbul**.
[99:0:2] - Of Prataparudra's **75** generals only **three** survived: **Prolaya Nayaka, Recherla Singama, Prolaya Vema Reddi**.
[99:0:3] # The Liberation Movement (Vimochanodyamam)
[99:0:4] - **What:** the **first organised resistance to Muslim rule** in Andhra – the "freedom struggle of the Andhras"; Andhra freed within about two years.
[99:0:5] - **Leader:** **Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka** (APPSC PYQ ×2; G2) – not Prolaya Vema Reddi, Singama, Kapaya, Kolani Rudra or Annayadeva.
[99:0:6] - **Headquarters:** **Rekapalli** (near Bhadrachalam).
[99:0:7] - **Participants (did not lead):** Prolaya Vema Reddi, Recherla Singama, **Koppula Prolaya Nayaka**, Kolani Rudra, Vengi Bhupala, Manchikonda Ganapati Nayaka, Kapaya Nayaka.
[99:0:8] - **Kaluvacheru grant (1423):** issued by the Reddi queen **Anitalli**; names the **75 Nayakas** who backed Prolaya.
[99:0:9] - **Successor states:** **Musunuri (1325–1368), Recherla Velama (1325–1475), Reddi (1325–1448)**.
[99:0:10] # Prolaya Nayaka – Founder of the Musunuri Kingdom
[99:0:11] - **Family:** son of **Potinayaka**; **Kamma** community (**Chaturthanvayas**); surname from the village **Musunur**.
[99:0:12] - **Capital:** **Rekapalli** on the **Godavari** near Bhadrachalam (APPSC G2 2017; PYQ ×2) – not Rachakonda (Recherla) or Sangama.
[99:0:13] - **Vilasa copper-plate grant (1330):** issued by **Prolaya Nayaka**; describes **conditions after the fall of the Kakatiyas** – Tughlaq atrocities, his rise, agrarian relief, **agraharas restored** (village Vilasa to the Brahmin Vennama) (PYQ ×2).
[99:0:14] - **Successor:** childless → his cousin **Kapaya Nayaka**.
[99:0:15] ~~ Sources: NextGen post kakatiyas p.1-4; Rocket Sheets p.6, p.42; app notes 1:99 (sub 0, 1)
## SUB 1 | Kapaya Nayaka – Titles, Warangal and the Bahmanis
[99:1:0] - **1336:** with Hoysala **Veera Ballala III**, **Prolaya Vema Reddi** and **Singama**, took **Orugallu (Warangal)** from **Malik Maqbul**; ruled from Warangal (1336–1368).
[99:1:1] - **Nephew Anapota Nayaka** = governor of **Vengi**; **Polavaram inscription** names 14 members of the lineage, only 3 ruled.
[99:1:2] # Titles
[99:1:3] TABLE head: Title | Holder
  [99:1:3.0] Andhra Suratrana | Kapaya Nayaka – first holder (APPSC PYQ; G2 2011 ×2; Welfare Officers)
  [99:1:3.1] Andhradesadhisvara | Kapaya (earlier Kakatiya Ganapatideva)
  [99:1:3.2] Katakachurakara | Kapaya
[99:1:4] - **⚠ Andhra Suratrana:** NextGen and Rocket give it **only to Kapaya**; one G2 2011 key gave **Anavema Reddi**, who is said to have used it later. **Kavirajamarga** is NOT Kapaya's title.
[99:1:5] # Kapaya and the Bahmanis
[99:1:6] TABLE head: Year | Event
  [99:1:6.0] 1347 | Kapaya helped Hasan Gangu found the Bahmani kingdom at Gulbarga
  [99:1:6.1] 1350 | Lost Kaulas
  [99:1:6.2] 1356 | Lost Bhuvanagiri
  [99:1:6.3] 1361 | Son Vinayaka Deva burnt alive by Muhammad Shah I
  [99:1:6.4] 1364–65 | Truce: Golconda ceded + 33 lakhs, turquoise throne, elephants, horses; Golconda became the boundary
  [99:1:6.5] 1367–68 | Battle of Bhimavaram: Anapota Nayaka (Recherla) killed Kapaya – Musunuri rule ends; Telangana to the Velamas
[99:1:7] - **Allies sought:** **Bukka I** of Vijayanagara; **Firoz Shah Tughlaq** of Delhi.
[99:1:8] - **After Kapaya:** the **Reddis took coastal Andhra**, the **Velamas absorbed Musunuri Telangana**.
[99:1:9] - **Ferishta's Tarikh-i-Ferishta** calls Telangana **"Tilang"**.
[99:1:10] - **Order:** Fall of Warangal (1323) → Vilasa grant (1330) → Orugallu recovered (1336) → Bhimavaram (1367–68). Vijayanagara (1336) arose **before** the Bahmanis (1347).
[99:1:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen post kakatiyas p.4-5; Rocket Sheets p.47; app notes 1:99 (sub 1, 2)
## SUB 2 | Recherla Court Literature
[99:2:0] TABLE head: Work | Author | Subject
  [99:2:0.0] Sangeeta Sudhakaram | Singabhupala II (Sarvajna Singa Bhupala) | Music – commentary on Sarngadeva's Sangita Ratnakara (APPSC G2 2011 ×3, 2012)
  [99:2:0.1] Rasarnava Sudhakara | Singa Bhupala | Sanskrit dramaturgy and poetics
  [99:2:0.2] Ratna Panchalika | Singa Bhupala | Play
  [99:2:0.3] Simhasana Dwatrimsika | Koravi Goparaju | 32 throne stories of Vikramaditya in Telugu (PYQ)
[99:2:1] - **⚠ Trap:** Sangeeta Sudhakaram is by **Singabhupala II**, a **Velama** – not Singabhupala I, Kumaragiri or Kataya Vema Reddi.
[99:2:2] - **Potana:** refused to dedicate his **Bhagavatam** to **Sarvajna Singama Nayaka II**; dedicated it to **Lord Rama** (PYQ).
[99:2:3] ~~ Sources: NextGen post kakatiyas p.11-12; NextGen AP History - APPSC Exams 08 p.26; Rocket Sheets p.10, p.31; app notes 1:99 (sub 6)
## SUB 3 | Recherla Velamas – Rulers, Capitals and Forts
[99:3:0] - **Also called:** **Padmanayakas**; began as Kakatiya feudatories; family history **Velugoti Varivamsavali**; lineage founder **Betala Nayudu**; dated **c. 1325–1475**.
[99:3:1] TABLE head: Ruler | Fact
  [99:3:1.0] Singama Nayaka I | Founder of the independent kingdom; freed Nalgonda–Mahabubnagar; expanded to the Krishna–Tungabhadra doab; killed by the Jallipalli chiefs (not at Bhimavaram)
  [99:3:1.1] Anapota Nayaka | Singama's son; capital Amanagallu → Rachakonda; won Bhimavaram (1367–68)
  [99:3:1.2] Sarvagna Singa Bhupala (II) | Sanskrit scholar-king of Rachakonda
[99:3:2] - **Devarakonda:** second branch capital; **Mada Nayaka**, younger brother of **Anapota Nayaka**, made its ruler; succeeded by **Pedda Vedagiri**.
[99:3:3] - **End:** **Sultan Quli Qutb Shah** of Golconda annexed **Rachakonda and Devarakonda**.
[99:3:4] - **Forts:** **Rachakonda** – **cyclopean masonry without mortar**; **Devarakonda** – **14th-century hilltop fort**.
[99:3:5] - **⚠ Trap:** Anapota **Nayaka** (Velama) killed Kapaya; Anapota **Reddi** moved the Reddi capital to Kondaveedu.
[99:3:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen post kakatiyas p.5; app notes 1:99 (sub 3)
## SUB 4 | Velama Battles and Foreign Relations
[99:4:0] TABLE head: Battle | Opponents | Outcome
  [99:4:0.0] Jallipalli | Singama vs Jallipalli Kshatriyas (aided by the Reddis) | Singama killed
  [99:4:0.1] Dharanikota | Madanayudu and nephew Naganayudu vs Anavota Reddi | Velamas won (revenge for Singama); titles Jagadabbaganda, Rayavesa Bhujanga
  [99:4:0.2] Bhimavaram (1367–68) | Anapota vs Kapaya | Kapaya killed
[99:4:1] - **Palnadu (APPSC G2 2019 key):** the Reddis defeated and expelled the Velamas who had penetrated Palnadu at the **Battle of Bhimavaram** – mark Bhimavaram, but know it also as the Velama–Musunuri battle.
[99:4:2] TABLE head: Power | Relation
  [99:4:2.0] Vijayanagara | Deva Raya I allied with them
  [99:4:2.1] Vengi | Velamas helped Annadevu take Vengi from Kataya Vema
  [99:4:2.2] Reddis | Pedakomati Vema died fighting them (1420)
  [99:4:2.3] Bahmanis | Mahmud Gawan crushed the Telangana revolts with Velama help
  [99:4:2.4] Gajapatis | Lingamanidu of Devarakonda sought help from Gajapati prince Hamvira
[99:4:3] - **Pattern:** later sided with the Bahmanis and Gajapatis **against Vijayanagara and the Reddis**.
[99:4:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen post kakatiyas p.5; app notes 1:99 (sub 4, 5)
## SUB 5 | Velama Families and Dynastic Capitals
[99:5:0] TABLE head: Family | Region
  [99:5:0.0] Recherla | Rachakonda, Devarakonda (Telangana)
  [99:5:0.1] Damerla | Sri Kalahasti (APPSC Forest Range Officers 2022)
  [99:5:0.2] Velugoti | Venkatagiri
  [99:5:0.3] Ravu | Bobbili
  [99:5:0.4] Pithapuram line | Pithapuram estate (Godavari) – not Rachakonda
[99:5:1] - **Poligar system:** Velama, Reddi and Raju families became zamindars.
[99:5:2] TABLE head: Dynasty | Capital
  [99:5:2.0] Musunuri | Rekapalli; Kapaya – Warangal
  [99:5:2.1] Recherla | Amanagallu → Rachakonda; Devarakonda
  [99:5:2.2] Reddi | Addanki → Kondaveedu (Anapota Reddi) → Rajahmundry – not Devarakonda
  [99:5:2.3] Kakatiya | Anamakonda first, then Warangal (not the only capital)
  [99:5:2.4] Salankayana | Vengipuram
  [99:5:2.5] Anupa (under Gautamiputra Satakarni) | Mahishmathi
[99:5:3] ~~ Sources: Rocket Sheets p.42; app notes 1:99 (sub 7)

=== NOTES 1:100 | Gajapatis of Orissa in Andhra; Bahmani Incursions Into Andhradesa
## SUB 0 | Bahmani Kingdom – Founder and Capitals
[100:0:0] - **Founded:** **1347** (14th century) by **Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah** – **Hasan Gangu / Zafar Khan** (UPPSC 1995, 2005; UKPSC 2002; State PSC) – not Firuz Shah, Mahmud Gawan, Malik Ambar or Mujahid Shah.
[100:0:1] - **First capital:** **Gulbarga**, renamed **Hasanabad** (CGPSC 2014) – not Bidar or Daulatabad.
[100:0:2] - **Four regions:** **Gulbarga, Daulatabad, Berar, Bidar** (Golconda was not one).
[100:0:3] - **Andhra link:** **Kapaya Nayaka** helped Hasan Gangu found it.
[100:0:4] - **Bidar:** **Ahmad Shah I** shifted the capital from Gulbarga to Bidar (APPSC G2 2003).
[100:0:5] - **Mahmud Gawan:** minister of **Muhammad III**; kingdom largest under him; **executed in 1481** – the kingdom then broke into five sultanates.
[100:0:6] - **⚠ Dates:** **1336** = Vijayanagara; **1347** = Bahmani.
[100:0:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen qutabshahis p.1; NextGen post kakatiyas p.4; app notes 1:100 (sub 0)
## SUB 1 | Krishnadevaraya and Prataparudra Gajapati
[100:1:0] - **Defeated Gajapati:** **Prataparudra Gajapati** (APPSC PYQ) – Kalinga campaign **1513–1519**.
[100:1:1] - **Order of campaign:** 1. **Udayagiri** (Nellore) – fell after an **18-month siege**; 2. Kandukuru, Vinukonda, Addanki, **Kondaveedu**; 3. **Kondapalli**, Bejawada; 4. march to **Cuttack**.
[100:1:2] - **Victory pillars:** at **Potnuru (Potnur)** and **Simhachalam** (APPSC G2-B 1991) – not Penugonda, Lepakshi or Hampi.
[100:1:3] - **Peace (c. 1518–19):** Prataparudra's daughter **Annapurna Devi** (Bhadradevi / Tukkadevi) married Krishnadevaraya; **lands north of the Krishna returned** to the Gajapati.
[100:1:4] - **⚠ Not a term:** **Cuttack and the Gajapati heartland were NOT annexed**.
[100:1:5] - **Earlier:** **Saluva Narasimha** drove the Gajapatis out of south-eastern Andhra by **c. 1470** and occupied land up to the Godavari.
[100:1:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen vijayanagara kingdom p.19-20; app notes 1:100 (sub 5, 7)
## SUB 2 | Gajapati Rulers in Andhra
[100:2:0] - **Title:** **Gajapati = "Lord of Elephants"** – taken by the Suryavamsi rulers of Orissa (UPPSC 2016); capital **Cuttack**; rule **c. 1434–1541**.
[100:2:1] - **Order of Andhra campaigns:** **Kapilendra → Purushottama → Prataparudra**.
[100:2:2] TABLE head: Ruler | Andhra campaign
  [100:2:2.0] Kapilendra (Kapileswara) – founder | Attacked Tiran Andhra (1448) (Penugonda inscription); annexed Rajamahendravaram after 1446, ending the Rajahmundry Reddis; took Kondaveedu c. 1450
  [100:2:2.1] Hamvira (Kapileswara's son) | Defeated the Bahmani army attacking Devarakonda; 1471 – Bahmani puppet
  [100:2:2.2] Purushottama | Won the throne after a struggle; refused to help Muhammad III
  [100:2:2.3] Prataparudra | Lost Udayagiri, Kondaveedu, Kondapalli to Krishnadevaraya
[100:2:3] # Key Places
[100:2:4] TABLE head: Place | Note
  [100:2:4.0] Rajamahendravaram | Reddis had been helped by Vijayanagara commander Mallappa Odayar (Draksharama inscription, 1444)
  [100:2:4.1] Kondaveedu | Under Vijayanagara till 1449 → fell to the Gajapatis c. 1450
  [100:2:4.2] Udayagiri (Nellore) | Major Gajapati stronghold in southern Andhra
[100:2:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen vijayanagara kingdom p.12-13; app notes 1:100 (sub 2, 3)
## SUB 3 | Gajapati Administration in Andhra
[100:3:0] TABLE head: Officer / unit | Function
  [100:3:0.0] Naidu | Revenue officers in the southern (Telugu) regions (APPSC GS 2025 key)
  [100:3:0.1] Bisoyi (Visayi) | Officer of a vishaya in Orissa proper
  [100:3:0.2] Nayakas and samantas | Collected revenue and kept order
  [100:3:0.3] Dandapata | Large province (whole districts) with a standing army
[100:3:1] - **⚠ Disputed:** the Draughtsman paper's printed key gave **Bisayee** for the southern revenue officer; the APPSC GS 2025 key and the app's notes give **Naidu**.
[100:3:2] - **Social order:** the **Reddi-era social order was kept**, not abolished.
[100:3:3] ~~ Sources: app notes 1:100 (sub 4)
## SUB 4 | Bahmani Incursions Into Andhradesa
[100:4:0] TABLE head: Sultan / commander | Incursion
  [100:4:0.0] Muhammad Shah I | Fought Kapaya; burned Vinayaka alive (1361); took Golconda by the 1364–65 truce
  [100:4:0.1] Firoz Shah | Beaten at Kambhammetta (1396) by Gajarao Tippa; repulsed at Kandukuru (1398) by Machareddi; allied with Pedakomati against Rajamahendravaram (1417)
  [100:4:0.2] Muhammad III + Mahmud Gawan | Crushed Telangana revolts; subdued Orugallu and took Kondaveedu; pushed into Odisha (1471)

=== NOTES 1:101 | Telugu Language and Literature to the 14TH Century – Nannaya, Tikkana, Errana, Palkuriki Somanatha
## SUB 0 | Kavitrayam – the Andhra Mahabharatam
[101:0:0] # The trinity (Kavitrayam)
[101:0:1] TABLE head: Poet | Century / patron | Share of the Mahabharata | Titles
  [101:0:1.0] Nannaya Bhattaraka | 11th c.; Rajaraja Narendra (Eastern Chalukya, r. 1018–1061), Rajamahendravaram | Adi, Sabha and part of Aranya Parva (up to the 142nd padya) | Adikavi, Vaganusasana (Vagaanushaasanudu – "maker of speech")
  [101:0:1.1] Tikkana Somayaji | 13th c.; minister-poet of Manumasiddhi II of Nellore (Telugu Chodas) | The remaining 15 parvas (Virata to Swargarohana) | Kavibrahma, Ubhayakavimitrudu
  [101:0:1.2] Errana (Errapragada) | 14th c.; court poet of Prolaya Vema Reddi (Reddi kingdom of Addanki) | Rest of Aranya Parva left by Nannaya – completed the Telugu Mahabharata; last of the Kavitrayam | Prabandha Parameswara, Sambhudasa
[101:0:2] - **First translator** of the Mahabharata into Telugu = **Nannaya** (APPSC G1 1994; Port Officer 2011; Degree Lecturers 2012; flashcard) – he **started** the Andhra Mahabharatam; Tikkana and Errana completed it.
[101:0:3] - **Who translated 15 parvas:** **Tikkana** – not Nannaya, Potana or Errana.
[101:0:4] - **Not in the trinity:** **Pampa (Pampana)** – Kannada poet (APPSC JL 2020); also not Srinatha, Potana or Nannechoda.
[101:0:5] - **Telugu Mahabharata translators:** **Nannaya and Tikkana** (UPPSC 2012 ×2) – **Kamban** wrote the **Tamil Ramayana**; Kuttan is no Telugu translator.
[101:0:6] - **Three eras:** the Telugu Mahabharata was completed over the **Eastern Chalukya, Kakatiya and Reddi** eras.
[101:0:7] - **Reddi patronage:** Errana, who completed the translation, was patronised by the **Reddy kings** (Prolaya Vema) – Nannaya (Chalukya) and Tikkana (Nellore Choda) were not.
[101:0:8] # Mahabharatas in other languages
[101:0:9] TABLE head: Composer | Language | Work
  [101:0:9.0] Pampa | Kannada | Vikramarjuna Vijaya (Pampa Bharata)
  [101:0:9.1] Sarala Dasa | Odia (not Bengali) | Mahabharata
  [101:0:9.2] Kasirama Das | Bengali (not Oriya) | Kashidasi Mahabharata
  [101:0:9.3] Perundevanar | Tamil – first Tamil Mahabharata (Bharatam Padiya Perundevanar) | (Kamban = Tamil Ramayana)
[101:0:10] - UPSC 1997: correctly matched = **Pampa – Kannada**; Tikkana is **Telugu**, not Marathi.
[101:0:11] # Epic background asked with the Kavitrayam
[101:0:12] - **Ramayana** chapters = **Kandas** (Mahabharata = **Parvas**).
[101:0:13] - **Ajnatavasa:** the Pandavas hid in the kingdom of **Virata**; **Yudhishthira** took the name **Kanka** (Bhima – Vallabha, Arjuna – Brihannala).
[101:0:14] - **Virata Parva:** popular belief that **reading the Virata Parva brings rain** (APPSC Endowment 2022).
[101:0:15] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Eastern Chalukyas p.20, p.33; NextGen Rocket Sheets AP History p.5, p.30, p.51; NextGen AP History Part 5 p.10, p.14; app notes 1:101 (sub 3, 12)
## SUB 1 | Pavuluri Mallana and Rajaraja Narendra's Grants
[101:1:0] # Pavuluri Mallana – the first Telugu mathematician
[101:1:1] - **Court mathematician** of **Rajaraja Narendra** (APPSC BC/Tribal Welfare 2017; ABCWO) – not Chalukya Bhima, Gunaga Vijayaditya or Ammaraja I.
[101:1:2] - **Work:** **Ganitasara Sangrahamu / Sara Sangraha Ganitam** ("Pavuluri Ganitam") – Telugu verse rendering of **Mahaviracharya's** Sanskrit **Ganitasarasangraha** (9th c.) – **first mathematics book in Telugu** (G2 2019 ×2; G2 Mains flashcard). Mahaviracharya is the original Sanskrit author, not the Telugu translator.
[101:1:3] - **Reward:** agrahara **Navakhandavada** from Rajaraja Narendra (G2 2008 ×2; G2 2012; APPSC PYQ ×2) – not Nandampudi, Asanapuram or Kaluchumbarru. Titles **Sukavi, Satkalasila**.
[101:1:4] # The two grants – never swap them
[101:1:5] TABLE head: Agrahara | Recipient | Fact
  [101:1:5.0] Navakhandavada | Pavuluri Mallana | Reward for the Telugu mathematics work
  [101:1:5.1] Nandampudi | Narayana Bhattu | For helping Nannaya "Andhraise" the Mahabharata; the Nandampudi grant was composed by Nannaya
[101:1:6] - **Narayana Bhattu:** knew eight languages – **Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara**; later **Someshwara I** of Kalyani made him his representative at Rajamahendravaram.
[101:1:7] - **⚠ Trap:** Nandampudi was given **to Narayana Bhattu**, not to Nannaya – Nannaya only wrote the inscription.
[101:1:8] # G2 Mains 2025 match (repeat of a G2 PYQ)
[101:1:9] TABLE head: Author | Work
  [101:1:9.0] Pavuluri Mallana | Ganitasara Sangraham
  [101:1:9.1] Vinukonda Vallabharaya | Kreedabhiramam
  [101:1:9.2] Aryadeva (disciple of Nagarjuna) | Chittavisuddhi Prakarana
  [101:1:9.3] Dignaga (father of Buddhist logic) | Pramana Samuccaya
[101:1:10] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Eastern Chalukyas p.20-21, p.33; NextGen previous papers p.18; NextGen Rocket Sheets AP History p.56; app notes 1:101 (sub 4, 7)
## SUB 2 | Kakatiya-Age Poets – Gona Budda Reddy, Baddena, Marana, Manchana
[101:2:0] TABLE head: Poet | Work | Exam fact
  [101:2:0.0] Gona Budda Reddy | Ranganatha Ramayanam (by c. 1250) | First Telugu Ramayana (translated from Sanskrit) and the greatest / first dwipada kavya
  [101:2:0.1] Tikkana | Nirvachanottara Ramayanam (first work, to Manumasiddhi II); Kavi Vakbandham, Krishna Satakam | Prose-less (only verse) Uttara Ramayana – not the first full Telugu Ramayana
  [101:2:0.2] Baddena (Bhadra Bhupala) | Sumati Satakam, Nitisastra Muktavali | Not Gona Budda Reddy, Somanatha or Krishnadevaraya
  [101:2:0.3] Marana (Tikkana's disciple) | Markandeya Puranam | Dedicated to Kakatiya commander Gannaya (Ganna Reddy)
  [101:2:0.4] Manchana (Manchena) | Keyurabahu Charitra | From Rajasekhara's Sanskrit Viddhasalabhanjika
  [101:2:0.5] Hulakki Bhaskara | Bhaskara Ramayanam | Champu Ramayana (one claim: first champu kavya)
[101:2:1] - **First Ramayana in Telugu** = **Gona Budda Reddy** (JA NTRUHS; G-W Sachivalayam; APPSC PYQ "by 1250") – not Tikkana, Baddena, Somanatha, Hulakki Bhaskara or Tallapaka Timmakka. "Ranganatha" is the name in the title, not a separate poet.
[101:2:2] - **Tikkana statements (FSO):** court poet of the **Nellore Telugu Chodas** ✓; Nirvachanottara Ramayana to **Manumasiddhi II** ✓; **Marana and Ketana** his disciples ✓; **Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam is Ketana's**, not Tikkana's ✗.
[101:2:3] - **Tikkana's philosophy:** **Harihara Advaita** – he dedicated his Bharatam to **Hariharanatha** (Siva + Vishnu).
[101:2:4] # Match pairs asked (G2 Mains 2025; JA NTRUHS)
[101:2:5] TABLE head: Work | Author
  [101:2:5.0] Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam | Ketana
  [101:2:5.1] Markandeya Puranam | Marana
  [101:2:5.2] Nirvachanottara Ramayanam | Tikkana
  [101:2:5.3] Keyurabahu Charitra | Manchena
  [101:2:5.4] Andhra Mahabharatam | Nannayya Bhattaraka
  [101:2:5.5] Dasakumara Charita | Mulaghatika Ketana
  [101:2:5.6] Harivamsamu | Errana (Yerrapragada) – to Prolaya Vema (Uttara Harivamsa = Nachana Somana)
[101:2:6] - **Errana's other works:** **Harivamsam**; **Narasimha (Nrusimha) Puranam** – first **Kshetra-mahatmya** kavya; Errana = **first prabandha** writer (one claim).
[101:2:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Kakatiyas p.3-5, p.31, p.33, p.55, p.73; NextGen AP History Part 5 p.10; NextGen Rocket Sheets AP History p.9-10; app notes 1:101 (sub 5, 7)
## SUB 3 | Kreedabhiramam and Kakatiya Court Works
[101:3:0] # Kreedabhiramam
[101:3:1] - **Author:** **Vinukonda Vallabharaya (Vallabhamatya)**, early 15th c.; a Telugu rendering of **Ravipati Tripurantakudu's** Sanskrit **Premabhiramam**.
[101:3:2] - **Form:** a **vidhi natakam** (street play) in **verse** – asked as **"poetry"** (APPSC PYQ); "Kreeda" = amusement, not a sports text; not grammar. English: *A Lover's Guide to Warangal* (Velcheru Narayana Rao and David Shulman).
[101:3:3] - **City described:** **Orugallu (Warangal)** in great detail – markets, temples, nightlife, festivals (APPSC G1 2002 ×2; G2 2002; APPSC PYQ ×2) – not Rajasekhara Charitra, Kalapurnodayam, Nilambari; not Amaravati, Rajamahendravaram or Pithapuram.
[101:3:4] - **"Abode of actors / drama artists":** **Orugallu** (G2 2011 ×3) – not Dwarasamudram, Devagiri or Madhura.
[101:3:5] - **Character Machaladevi:** a famous courtesan (dancer) of Warangal in **Kreedabhiramam** – not Himabindu, Veyipadagalu or Amuktamalyada.
[101:3:6] # Other Kakatiya-court works
[101:3:7] TABLE head: Author | Work | Note
  [101:3:7.0] Vidyanatha (Agastya) | Prataparudra Yasobhushanam (Prataparudriyam), Sanskrit alankara | Court of Prataparudra II (G2 2011) – not Ketana, Baddena or Tikkana
  [101:3:7.1] Jayapa Senani | Nritta Ratnavali (Sanskrit, dance) | Gaja Sahini (elephant commander) of Ganapatideva – his post is not the reason for his treatise
  [101:3:7.2] Rudradeva | Nitisara (statecraft) | Kakatiya ruler; ⚠ the Kesari Samudram tank is credited to Prola I (see row 92), not Rudradeva
  [101:3:7.3] Ekamranatha | Prataparudra Charitra | History of the Kakatiyas
  [101:3:7.4] Ravipati Tripurantakudu | Premabhiramam; Niroshthya Ramayanam | –
[101:3:8] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Kakatiyas p.3-5; NextGen previous papers p.22; NextGen Rocket Sheets AP History p.9, p.29; app notes 1:101 (sub 9)
## SUB 4 | Ketana – Abhinava Dandi
[101:4:0] TABLE head: Work | Significance
  [101:4:0.0] Dasakumara Charitra | Telugu rendering of Dandin's Sanskrit prose classic; first Telugu story kavya; dedicated to Tikkana
  [101:4:0.1] Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam | First grammar written in Telugu (196 padyas)
  [101:4:0.2] Vijnaneswariyamu (Vignanesvaram) | Telugu Mitakshara of Vijnaneswara – commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti; first Telugu dharmasastra
[101:4:1] - **Title "Abhinava Dandi"** ("the new Dandin") = **Mula Ghatika Ketana** (APPSC PYQ ×4; G2 PYQ; ABCWO flashcard) – **conferred by Tikkana** for the Dasakumara Charitra – not Marana, Potana, Tikkana, Peddana or Mallana.
[101:4:2] - **Mitakshara into Telugu:** **Ketana** (G1 2010 re-exam; G1 PYQ; APPSC PYQ) – not Vijnaneswara himself, Visweswara, Madiki Singana, Shivadevayya, Sayana or Baddena.
[101:4:3] - **Women's property rule:** "women's property is inherited wholly by the **daughters and the daughter's daughters**" – found in **Ketana's Vignanesvaram** (Mitakshara rule) (NextGen previous papers). **Purushartha Saramu** is **Shivadevayya's** separate work.
[101:4:4] - **Other Kakatiya law/ethics works:** Purushartha Saramu – **Shivadevayya**; Sakala Niti Sammatamu – **Madiki Singana**; Nitisastra Muktavali and Sumati Satakam – Baddena.
[101:4:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 5 p.10; NextGen AP History - Kakatiyas p.59, p.73; NextGen previous papers p.14; NextGen Rocket Sheets AP History p.9, p.30, p.52
## SUB 5 | Nannaya – Adikavi and Andhra Shabda Chintamani
[101:5:0] - **Court poet, teacher and adviser** of **Rajaraja Narendra**; the Chalukyas, claiming lunar descent like the Pandavas, encouraged him to "Andhraise" the Mahabharata (c. 1045–65), helped by **Narayana Bhattu**.
[101:5:1] - **Andhra Shabda Chintamani** (Andhra Bhashanushasanam) = the first grammar of Telugu, **written in Sanskrit**, **attributed to Nannaya** (G2 Mains 2017; G2 PYQ; APPSC PYQ) – not Tikkana, Errana or Peddana. ⚠ Modern scholars doubt the attribution, but exams credit Nannaya.
[101:5:2] - **Statements (G2 PYQ):** I. translated the Mahabharata as Andhra Mahabharatam ✓; II. credited with Andhra Shabda Chintamani ✓; III. "Nandampudi donated to Nannaya" ✗ – Nandampudi went to **Narayana Bhattu**.
[101:5:3] - **Title Vaganusasana / Vagaanushaasanudu ("maker of speech")** = **Nannaya** (ATWO) – not Peddana, Veeresalingam or C. Pullaiah; also **Adikavi**, Vidyadvaitudu, **Vagadheeshwara**, Shabda Shasanudu.
[101:5:4] - **Other works:** **Indravijayam**, **Chamundika Vilasam**; pioneered the **Champu** style (prose + verse); used the **Akkara** metre borrowed from **Kannada**.
[101:5:5] - **Significance:** Nannaya **fixed the grammar and literary register** of classical Telugu and began the Kavitrayam tradition; his **Andhra Mahabharatamu = first book in Telugu**.
[101:5:6] - **Word "Tenugu":** first used by **Nannaya** (NextGen); ⚠ some books credit Ketana with "Telugu".
[101:5:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Eastern Chalukyas p.20, p.33; NextGen Rocket Sheets AP History p.9, p.57; app notes 1:101 (sub 4)
## SUB 6 | Telugu Language, Earliest Inscriptions and Court Languages
[101:6:0] # The language
[101:6:1] - **Family:** **Dravidian** (South-Central branch, with **Gondi and Kui**) – not Aryan, Sanskrit or Pali families (Dy. EO 2008).
[101:6:2] - **Oldest** spoken and literary language of South India = **Tamil** (Polytechnic Lecturers 2012); Tamil got classical status first (2004).
[101:6:3] - **"Italian of the East":** **Telugu** – coined by the Venetian **Niccolo de' Conti** (15th c.) because its words **end in vowels**.
[101:6:4] - **"Desa bhashalandu Telugu lessa":** **Krishnadevaraya**, in Amuktamalyada.
[101:6:5] - **Official languages of AP:** **Telugu** (since 1966) and **Urdu** as second official language (**all districts** since the 2022 amendment).
[101:6:6] - **Classical language:** Telugu and **Kannada**, **31 October 2008**; total **11** classical languages after **3 October 2024**.
[101:6:7] - **Telugu Language Day:** **29 August**, birth anniversary of **Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy** (not Gurajada).
[101:6:8] - **Trilinga** theory: Srisailam, Kaleshwaram, Draksharama.
[101:6:9] # Before written Telugu literature
[101:6:10] - **Satavahana royal language = Prakrit**; **Hala's Gathasaptasati** is in **Prakrit** (Maharashtri), with Telugu words like atta, potta, pilla, pandi.
[101:6:11] - **First Telugu word:** **Nagabu** (Amaravati; found by **Veturi Prabhakara Sastri**); **Vepuru** – Myakadoni; **-ambul** – Chikkulla plates (Vishnukundins).
[101:6:12] # Earliest inscriptions
[101:6:13] TABLE head: Inscription | Issuer | Significance
  [101:6:13.0] Kalamalla (Kadapa) | Renati Chola Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya, c. 575 | First Telugu inscription (prose)
  [101:6:13.1] Erragudipadu | Renati Chola Punyakumara | First fully available; geya (song) style
  [101:6:13.2] Vipparla | Jayasimha (Vallabha) I, Eastern Chalukya | First complete early Telugu text (G2 2017)
  [101:6:13.3] Chejarla | Kubja Vishnuvardhana | Over 50% Telugu words
  [101:6:13.4] Addanki | Panduranga, commander of Gunaga Vijayaditya III | First poetic inscription – Taruvoja metre
  [101:6:13.5] Kandukur, Dharmavaram | Gunaga Vijayaditya | Seesa
  [101:6:13.6] Bezawada | Yuddhamalla II | First Madhyakkara
[101:6:14] - Other early records: Lakshmipuram (Jayasimha I, first complete Telugu prose), Sataluru (Champakamala), **Chebrolu** (**Marga and Desi** forms); Motupalli is a later Kakatiya record, not pre-Nannaya.
[101:6:15] - **Pitikayagulla** (Prakasam, 8th c.): shows post-Badami Chalukya influence on the script – not the first poetic inscription and not Gunaga Vijayaditya's.
[101:6:16] - **June 2026:** an ASI survey of the **Nallamala** Tiger Reserve copied **25 inscriptions** (2nd–16th c.).
[101:6:17] - **Bhattiprolu** (c. 400 BCE, Guntur): **Prakrit** inscriptions in a **variant of Brahmi**, carrying early Telugu place and personal names.
[101:6:18] - Script: Brahmi (Bhattiprolu) → common **Old Kannada–Telugu** script (Kadamba–Chalukya age) → separate rounded Telugu script **11th–14th c.**
[101:6:19] # Court languages
[101:6:20] - **Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi:** asked "official language" → **Telugu** (G2 2008; NextGen previous papers; Rocket) – Telugu entered royal records and literature under them; ⚠ the prasasti (praise) of their grants stayed in **Sanskrit**, grant details in **Telugu**.
[101:6:21] - **Kakatiyas:** inscriptions **mostly in Telugu** (APPSC PYQ key) – Telugu became the administrative language; ⚠ NextGen calls Sanskrit their royal language; Telugu grammar, poetics and desi metres grew in this age.
[101:6:22] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Eastern Chalukyas p.33; NextGen Powerplay #1 Part 5.1 p.9; NextGen previous papers p.8; NextGen AP History Part 7 p.8; NextGen Rocket Sheets AP History p.3, p.6, p.16; NextGen AP History - Kakatiyas p.71; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kakatiya_dynasty; app notes 1:101 (sub 0-2)
## SUB 7 | Shiva Kavis – Palkuriki Somanatha, Panditaradhya, Nannechoda
[101:7:0] TABLE head: Poet | Work | Note
  [101:7:0.0] Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya | Sivatattvasaram (~400 kanda poems) | Spread Veerashaivism (Aradhya Shaivism) in Andhra; originator of the Sataka form
  [101:7:0.1] Nannechoda | Kumarasambhavam | Title Kavirajasekhara; began the eight descriptions of prabandha
  [101:7:0.2] Palkuriki Somanatha | Basava Puranam, Panditaradhya Charitra, Vrushadhipa Satakam | Kakatiya age; Prathama Andhra Viplava Kavi
[101:7:1] - **Basava Puranam** = **Palkuriki Somanatha** (G2 2019), in **dwipada** – life of **Basava** and **Veerashaivism**; **not Vemulavada Bhimakavi** (the wrong pair in the G1 PYQ), not Tikkana, Marana or Ketana.
[101:7:2] - **Panditaradhya Charitra** = Palkuriki Somanatha (G1 1994) – first Telugu **encyclopaedia**; lists 20 textile varieties – not Manucharitra, Amuktamalyada or Keyurabahu Charitra.
[101:7:3] - **Who spread Veerashaivism in Andhra:** **Panditaradhya** (Mallikarjuna, 12th c.) – **Basava** founded it in Karnataka; Somanatha later popularised it through Telugu literature.
[101:7:4] - **Desi kavita movement:** Somanatha led it against Sanskrit-heavy marga style; popularised **dwipada**, ragada.
[101:7:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - Andhra Cholas p.3; NextGen AP History - Kakatiyas p.3, p.31; NextGen previous papers p.59; NextGen Rocket Sheets AP History p.9; app notes 1:101 (sub 6)
## SUB 8 | Grammar, Forms, Firsts and Other Early Works
[101:8:0] # Grammar and prosody
[101:8:1] TABLE head: Work | Author
  [101:8:1.0] Andhra Shabda Chintamani | Nannaya – grammar in Sanskrit
  [101:8:1.1] Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam | Ketana – first grammar in Telugu
  [101:8:1.2] Kavijanasrayam | Malliya Rechana – first work on prosody
  [101:8:1.3] Kavyalankara Chudamani | Vinnakota Peddana – first alankara work
  [101:8:1.4] Kavi Vakbandham | Tikkana
  [101:8:1.5] Appakaviyam | Kakunuri Appakavi (17th c.)
[101:8:2] # Forms and their first examples
[101:8:3] TABLE head: Form | First / chief example
  [101:8:3.0] Champu | Nannaya's Bharatam style; Bhaskara Ramayanam (one claim)
  [101:8:3.1] Dwipada | Ranganatha Ramayanam; popularised by Palkuriki
  [101:8:3.2] Sataka | Sivatattvasaram (Panditaradhya) / Vrushadhipa Satakam (Palkuriki)
  [101:8:3.3] Prabandha | Errana first writer; Nannechoda began the eight descriptions; peak – Ashtadiggajas
  [101:8:3.4] Kshetra-mahatmya | Nrusimha Puranam (Errana)
  [101:8:3.5] Yakshagana | Sugriva Vijayam (Kandukuri Rudrakavi)
  [101:8:3.6] Dvyarthi kavya | Raghavapandaviyam (Pingali Surana)
[101:8:4] - **Ages:** Nannaya (11th c.) → **Shiva Kavi Yugam 1060–1260** → Tikkana (13th) → Errana (14th) → Srinatha (15th) → Prabandha/Rayala (16th) → **Dakshinatya** (southern Nayaka, 17th–18th) → modern.
[101:8:5] - **Jinendra Kalyanabhyudayamu** (Jain) – **Appayacharya**, Prataparudra's time.
[101:8:6] - **Sasyanandamu** – **Donayamatya** (14th c.): Telugu work on agricultural knowledge and rainfall forecasting (APPSC 2017) – not Haravilasamu (Srinatha).
[101:8:7] - **"Telugu literature was first influenced by which empire"** (APPSC GS 2019 key) – **Vijayanagara Empire**, i.e. its golden age under Krishnadevaraya; literature itself began under the Eastern Chalukyas.
[101:8:8] - **Author–book mix (G-W Sachivalayam):** **Hala** – Gathasaptasati; **Nannaya** – Mahabharata; **Paravastu Chinnaya Suri** – **Neeti Chandrika**; **Kattamanchi Ramalinga Reddy** – **Musalamma Maranam**.
[101:8:9] ~~ Sources: NextGen Rocket Sheets AP History p.9-10; app notes 1:101 (sub 8, 10)
## SUB 9 | Beyond the 14th Century – Srinatha, Prabandha and Other Poets
[101:9:0] - **Srinatha** (c. 1365–1441): court of **Pedakomati Vema Reddi**; title **Kavisarvabhauma** from **Deva Raya II**'s court (defeated Dindima Bhatta).
[101:9:1] TABLE head: Work | Note
  [101:9:1.0] Sringara Naishadham | Nala–Damayanti (from Sriharsha)
  [101:9:1.1] Haravilasam | To merchant Tippayya Setti
  [101:9:1.2] Kashikhandam | At Kataya Vema's request
  [101:9:1.3] Bhimakhandam | Bhimeswara of Draksharama
  [101:9:1.4] Palnati Veera Charitra | Battle of Palnadu
[101:9:2] - **Veerabhadra Vijayam** = **Bammera Potana** (Sahaja Panditya), not Srinatha.
[101:9:3] - **Prabandha:** epic kavya gave way to prabandha – **strict metrical rules**, single episode, elaborate descriptions, strong shringara; Reddi courts (Errana, Srinatha) → peak with the **Ashtadiggajas**.
[101:9:4] TABLE head: Work | Author
  [101:9:4.0] Manucharitra | Allasani Peddana (Andhra Kavita Pitamaha)
  [101:9:4.1] Parijatapaharanam | Nandi Timmana
  [101:9:4.2] Kalapurnodayam, Raghavapandaviyam, Prabhavati Pradyumnam | Pingali Surana
  [101:9:4.3] Rajasekhara Charitra | Madayagari Mallana
  [101:9:4.4] Kalahastiswara Satakam | Dhurjati
  [101:9:4.5] Ramabhyudayam | Ayyalaraju Ramabhadra
  [101:9:4.6] Varadambika Parinayam (Sanskrit) | Tirumalamba
  [101:9:4.7] Madhura Vijayam (Sanskrit) | Gangadevi (not Pingali Surana)
  [101:9:4.8] Bhadraparinayamu (1878, 19th c.) | Allamaraju Subrahmanya Kavi
[101:9:5] - **Titles:** Kavibrahma – Tikkana; Sambhudasa – Errana; Kavisarvabhauma – Srinatha; Kaviraja Sikhamani – Nannechoda; Sahaja Panditya – Potana.
[101:9:6] # Poets of other languages

=== NOTES 1:103 | Rajput States and Society; Chandella, Solanki and Paramara Contributions
## SUB 0 | Solankis (Chalukyas of Gujarat) – Somnath, Modhera, Rani-ki-Vav, Dilwara
[103:0:0] TABLE head: Ruler | Contribution
  [103:0:0.0] Mularaja I (c. 940) | Founder; capital Anhilwada (Anahilapataka, Patan)
  [103:0:0.1] Bhima I (Bhimadeva I) (1022-1064) | Somnath raided by Mahmud 1025; rebuilt Somnath after Mahmud left; built Modhera Sun temple; minister Vimal Shah built Vimal Vasahi (c. 1031); queen Udayamati built Rani-ki-Vav in his memory
  [103:0:0.2] Jayasimha Siddharaja (1092-1142) | Patron of Hemachandra; Sahasralinga tank at Patan; gave aid (1 lakh balotras) to rebuild a demolished mosque at Khambhat (Muhammad Aufi)
  [103:0:0.3] Kumarapala (1142-1171) | Jain, disciple of Hemachandra; rebuilt Somnath in stone; curbed animal killing – sent ministers to stop cruelty to animals in Kashi
  [103:0:0.4] Mularaja II (1175-1178) | Defeated Ghori at Kayadara near Mount Abu (1178), regent Naika Devi
[103:0:1] - **Somnath rebuilt after Mahmud:** **Bhimdev (Bhima I)** – books key "Bhimdev"; Kumarapala later rebuilt it in stone; Mularaja was only the founder.
[103:0:2] - **Hemachandra** (Shvetambara Jain; Siddha-Hema grammar, Kumarapalacharita, Trishashti Shalaka Purusha-charitra): court scholar of Jayasimha Siddharaja **and Kumarapala** – PYQ key **Kumarapala**, whose adviser he was.
[103:0:3] - **Mosque at Khambhat:** **Jayasimha Siddharaja** – a tolerant ruler.
[103:0:4] - Solankis were Shaivas who also patronised Jainism.
[103:0:5] TABLE head: Monument | Builder | Place
  [103:0:5.0] Modhera Sun temple | Bhima I | Modhera, Mehsana district (old Patan region), Gujarat
  [103:0:5.1] Rani-ki-Vav stepwell | Queen Udayamati | Patan, Gujarat; UNESCO 2014; on the ₹100 note (lavender, 2018)
  [103:0:5.2] Vimal Vasahi, Dilwara | Vimal Shah, Bhima I's minister, c. 1031; Rishabha (Adinatha) | Mount Abu (Aravalli hills), Rajasthan
  [103:0:5.3] Luna Vasahi, Dilwara | Vaghela ministers Vastupala and Tejpal, 1230; Neminatha | Mount Abu, Rajasthan
  [103:0:5.4] Somnath | Rebuilt by Bhima I, then Kumarapala; Old Somnath by Ahilyabai Holkar (1783); present temple 1951 | Gujarat; Shiva jyotirlinga
[103:0:6] - **Dilwara Jain temples:** **Mount Abu**, Rajasthan – not Palitana, Sonagiri or Girnar.
[103:0:7] - **Modhera** (only Gujarat temple among Dakshinark, Konark and Martand); **fully solarised** village (MNRE, 6 MW + 15 MWh storage), inaugurated **9 October 2022**.
[103:0:8] - Somnath style: **Maru-Gurjara**; **Somnath Swabhiman Parv** (January 2026).
[103:0:9] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval 04 p.4-5 (Chalukyas of Gujarat), p.12-14 (Hemachandra); Rocket Indian History 01 p.110; Rocket Indian History 02 p.14 (Vimal Vasahi); NextGen Indian History - APPSC 03 p.27; app notes 1:103 (sub 4, 5)
## SUB 1 | Chandelas and the Khajuraho Temples
[103:1:0] TABLE head: Particular | Fact
  [103:1:0.0] Founder | Nannuka (9th c.); moon-descended (Chandratreya) – not Agnikula
  [103:1:0.1] Region | Jejakabhukti = Bundelkhand, named after Jayashakti (Jeja), grandson of Nannuka
  [103:1:0.2] Centres | Khajuraho (Kharjjuravahaka), Mahoba, Kalanjar
  [103:1:0.3] Rulers | Yashovarman (Lakshmana temple), Dhanga (c. 950-999, first independent; Vishvanatha temple), Vidyadhara (resisted Mahmud; Kandariya Mahadeva), Paramardi (Parmal)
[103:1:1] - **Khajuraho patrons:** the **Chandelas** – not the Gurjara-Pratiharas, Paramaras, Chahamanas, Mauryas, Holkars, Scindias or Bundelas.
[103:1:2] - **Khajuraho group:** built c. **950-1050 CE**; **Chhatarpur** district, **Madhya Pradesh**; UNESCO; Shaiva, Vaishnava and Jain temples.
[103:1:3] - **Kandariya Mahadeva** (largest; **Shiva**) – built by Chandela **Vidyadhara**; **Lakshmana** temple – Vishnu.
[103:1:4] - **Not at Khajuraho:** **Dashavatara temple** – it is at **Deogarh** (Lalitpur, UP), Gupta period; Kandariya Mahadev, **Chausath Yogini** and **Chitragupta** are at Khajuraho.
[103:1:5] - **Dhangdev (Dhanga):** ruler of the **Chandelas of Jejakabhukti**.
[103:1:6] - **Alha and Udal:** of **Mahoba**, commanders of Chandela **Paramardidev (Parmal, 1165-1203)**, who fought Prithviraj Chauhan.
[103:1:7] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval 04 p.2-3 (Chandellas); Rocket Indian History 01 p.31, p.52, p.110; Rocket Indian History 02 p.14; NextGen Indian History - APPSC 03 p.27; app notes 1:103 (sub 1, 5)
## SUB 2 | Paramaras of Malwa – Bhoja, Dhar and Bhojshala
[103:2:0] TABLE head: Particular | Fact
  [103:2:0.0] Founder | Upendra (Krishnaraja), 9th c., Rashtrakuta feudatory
  [103:2:0.1] Capital | Dhara (Dhar), Malwa (Bhoja moved it from Ujjain)
  [103:2:0.2] Rulers | Siyaka II, Munja, Sindhuraja (Navasahasanka), Bhoja (c. 1010-1055); last Mahalakadeva (killed 1305 by Alauddin's forces)
  [103:2:0.3] Sources | Navasahasanka Charita of Padmagupta, Prabandha Chintamani of Merutunga, Udaipur Prashasti (genealogy, praises Bhoja), Harsola plates – all of these
[103:2:1] - **King Bhoja ruled over:** **Dhar** (Malwa) – not Bastar or Mahakaushal.
[103:2:2] - **Navasahasanka Charita:** about the **Paramaras** (Sindhuraja) – not Cholas, Pandyas or Pallavas.
[103:2:3] # Bhoja's works and monuments
[103:2:4] TABLE head: Work | Subject
  [103:2:4.0] Samarangana Sutradhara | Architecture, town planning and mechanical devices / artificial scientific equipment (yantras)
  [103:2:4.1] Saraswati-Kanthabharana | Poetics and grammar
  [103:2:4.2] Rajamartanda (Bhojavritti), Yuktikalpataru, Rajamriganka, Champu-Ramayana, Sringara Prakasa | Yoga-sutra commentary, polity, astronomy, poetry
[103:2:5] - **Book on artificial scientific equipment:** **Bhoja** (Samarangana Sutradhara).
[103:2:6] - **Bhojshala, Dhar:** centre of Sanskrit learning; temple of **Goddess Saraswati (Vagdevi)**; Muslims call it **Kamal Maula Mosque**.
[103:2:7] - **Bhojshala in news:** ASI survey ordered **2024** (under a **2003** ASI arrangement both communities worshipped on separate days); **May 2026** – **Madhya Pradesh High Court** declared it a Hindu temple on ASI findings.
[103:2:8] - **Bhojpur (Bhojeshwar) temple:** unfinished **Shiva** temple, **Raisen** district, beside Bhoja's man-made lake (Bhojtal).
[103:2:9] - **Tribhuvan Narayan temple, Chittor** (now Samiddheshwar): built by **Paramara Raja Bhoja**; restored by Rana Mokal.

## SUB 3 | Rajput Origins, Dynasties and Regions
[103:3:0] - Rajput states rose after the **collapse of the Gurjara-Pratihara Empire** (10th c.) – former Pratihara feudatories.
[103:3:1] TABLE head: Theory | Proponent / claim
  [103:3:1.0] Agnikula (born from Vasishtha's fire at Mount Abu) | Chand Bardai (Prithviraj Raso): Pratiharas, Chaulukyas (Solankis), Paramaras, Chahamanas (Chauhans)
  [103:3:1.1] Suryavanshi / Chandravanshi | Solar / lunar descent claims (Chandelas – lunar)
  [103:3:1.2] Foreign origin (Scythians, Hunas, Gurjaras) | Col. James Tod, V.A. Smith
  [103:3:1.3] Kshatriya descent | G.H. Ojha, C.V. Vaidya
[103:3:2] - **Agnikula clans (NDA 2008):** Pratiharas, **Chalukyas** (= Solankis), Paramaras, Chahamanas – **all four (I, II, III and IV)**.
[103:3:3] - **Hammir Mahakavya** (Nayachandra Suri): the Chauhans were **Suryavanshis** (solar line).
[103:3:4] TABLE head: Dynasty | Founder | Capital / region
  [103:3:4.0] Chahamana (Chauhan) | Vasudeva | Sakambhari → Ajmer (Vigraharaja IV), Delhi
  [103:3:4.1] Tomara | Anangapala | Dhillika (Delhi); horseman-and-bull coins; ousted by Chauhans 1151
  [103:3:4.2] Gahadavala | Chandradeva (1089) | Kannauj, Varanasi; Govindachandra, Jaichand
  [103:3:4.3] Kalachuri (Chedi) | Kokalla I | Tripuri (Jabalpur)
  [103:3:4.4] Kachwaha | Dulha Rai (10th c.) | Amber (Dhundhar) → Jaipur
[103:3:5] - **Kachwahas:** rulers of **Amber** (not Mewar, Marwar or Rashtrakuta); dynasty founded in the **10th century AD**.
[103:3:6] - **Nahargarh Fort, Jaipur:** built by Kachwaha **Sawai Jai Singh II** in **1734**.
[103:3:7] - **Lakshmidhara:** minister of Gahadavala **Govindachandra**; his **Kritya-kalpataru** is the first great **Nibandha** (digest of Smriti, epic and Puranic texts), 12th c.
[103:3:8] - **Mehrauli Iron Pillar:** a **Gupta** work moved to Delhi – not Anangapala's.
[103:3:9] TABLE head: Medieval name | Present region
  [103:3:9.0] Champaka | Chamba, Himachal Pradesh (not Central India)
  [103:3:9.1] Durgara | Jammu
  [103:3:9.2] Kuluta | Kullu, Himachal Pradesh (not Malabar)

## SUB 4 | Mewar – Rana Kumbha and the Chittor Towers
[103:4:0] TABLE head: Monument / work | Fact

  [103:4:0.2] Jain Kirti Stambha, Chittor | Merchant Jijaji (Jeeja), 12th c.; dedicated to Adinath
  [103:4:0.3] Kumbhalgarh fort | Rana Kumbha

[103:4:2] - **"Kirti Stambha of Chittor":** books and NextGen Rocket key **Rana Kumbha** (his tower is also called Kirti Stambha); the separate Jain Kirti Stambha is Jijaji's.
[103:4:3] - **Kumbha on music:** **Sangeet Raj**, Sangeet Mimansa, Rasik Priya (Gita Govinda commentary) – the Rajput ruler who wrote on music.
[103:4:4] - **Kumbha's court scholars:** **Muni Sundar Suri**, **Natha**, **Tilla Bhatt**, Mandan, Kanha Vyas – **not Muni Jin Vijay** (a 20th-century scholar).
[103:4:5] - **Rani Padmini's jauhar** at Chittor: against **Alauddin Khalji**.

[103:6:0] TABLE head: Temple | Fact
