=== NOTES 1:120 | Saluva and Tuluva Dynasties; Krishnadevaraya - Conquests, Amuktamalyada, the Ashtadiggajas
## SUB 0 | Ashtadiggajas, Bhuvana Vijayam and the Golden Age of Telugu
[120:0:0] # The Ashtadiggajas
[120:0:1] - **Who they were:** **eight Telugu poets** ("eight elephants" holding up the eight directions) – not ministers, warriors or advisers (UP UDA 2001).
[120:0:2] - **Patron:** **Krishnadevaraya** (APPSC G2 2019; AP History PYQ; RAS 2010) – not Rama Raya, Achyutaraya, Tirumala Raya, Devaraya II, Shivaji or Rajendra I.
[120:0:3] - **Golden age:** his reign (1509–29) = **golden age of Telugu literature**, the **Prabandha** era (UP UDA 2006) – not Konkani, Malayalam or Tamil.
[120:0:4] - **Why we remember him:** for his **literary patronage** (AP History PYQ) – the Ashtadiggajas in the **Bhuvana Vijayam**.
[120:0:5] # Poet → work → title
[120:0:6] TABLE head: Poet | Main work | Title / note
  [120:0:6.0] Allasani Peddana | *Manucharitramu* (Swarochisha Manu Sambhavam) | Andhra Kavita Pitamaha; greatest of the eight; poet of Telugu and Sanskrit
  [120:0:6.1] Nandi Timmana | *Parijatapaharanamu* | Mukku Timmana; the king's favourite
  [120:0:6.2] Dhurjati | *Sri Kalahasteeswara Mahatyam* and Satakam | Shaiva poet of Kalahasti
  [120:0:6.3] Madayyagari Mallana | *Rajasekhara Charitramu* | Early social narrative
  [120:0:6.4] Ayyalaraju Ramabhadrudu | *Ramabhyudayamu*, Sakalakathasara Sangrahamu | Ramayana in Telugu
  [120:0:6.5] Pingali Surana | *Raghava Pandaviyamu*, *Kalapurnodayamu*, Prabhavati Pradyumnamu | Dvyarthi kavya (double meaning)
  [120:0:6.6] Ramarajabhushana (Bhattumurti) | *Vasucharitramu*, Narasabhupaliyamu | Vasucharitra dedicated to Tirumala Raya
  [120:0:6.7] Tenali Ramakrishna | *Panduranga Mahatmyamu* (also Ghatikachala Mahatmyam, Udbhataradhya Charitra) | Court wit
[120:0:7] - **Manucharitramu:** by **Allasani Peddana** (APPSC G2 2019; IAS 2007) – not Kalapurnodayam or Raghava Pandaviyam (Pingali Surana), or Haravilasam (Srinatha).
[120:0:8] - **Andhra Kavita Pitamaha:** **Allasani Peddana** (Raj. PCS 2023; WBCS 2007) – not Bhattumurti, Tenali Ramakrishna, Pingali Surana, Srinatha, Sayana or Madhava. **Andhra Bhoja** is the king's own title.
[120:0:9] - **Panduranga Mahatyam:** **Tenali Ramakrishna** (APPSC Jr Asst) – not Peddana, Dhurjati or the king.
[120:0:10] - **RAS 2021 statements:** Krishnadevaraya wrote Amuktamalyada ✓; he is called Andhra Bhoja ✓; Peddana "well versed in **Sanskrit and Tamil**" ✗ (he was a **Telugu and Sanskrit** poet) → **1 and 2 only**.
[120:0:11] - **Gandapenderam:** the king himself fixed this anklet on **Peddana's** foot.
[120:0:12] - **"Prabandha Parameshwara"** is **Errana's** title, not Nandi Timmana's.
[120:0:13] # Bhuvana Vijayam and the Tippalur grant
[120:0:14] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [120:0:14.0] Bhuvana Vijayam | "Conquest of the world"; Krishnadevaraya's court hall of poets; House of Victory
  [120:0:14.1] Ashtadiggajas | Eight elephants of the eight directions → eight pillar-poets
  [120:0:14.2] Kavula Samstha | Institution of poets – the Tippalur inscription's name for them
[120:0:15] - **Tippalur inscription:** gift of **Tippalur agrahara** (Kadapa) to the poets by **Krishnadevaraya**, not Achyutaraya.
[120:0:16] # Languages patronised
[120:0:17] - Vijayanagara patronised **Telugu, Kannada, Sanskrit and Tamil** – all four (Grama Sachivalayam) – so "**Tamil, Telugu and Sanskrit**" is the SSC 2007 answer (Hindi, Marathi, Malayalam, Urdu are wrong).
[120:0:18] - **Kannada:** **Mallanarya** of Krishnadevaraya's court wrote *Bhava Chinta Ratna* and *Veerasaivamrita* in **Kannada** (Raj. PCS 2024).
[120:0:19] - **Correct combination (Grama Sachivalayam):** **Krishnadevaraya – Amuktamalyada – Sahiti Samarangana Sarvabhauma** ✓. Wrong: Hala's title is not Devanampriya (Ashoka's); Peddana wrote **Manucharitra**, not Vasucharitra; Srinatha's title is **Kavisarvabhauma**.
[120:0:20] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History – Vijayanagara (src/ap-history/nextgen-10-vijayanagara.txt) p.4, p.32-33; NextGen Rocket Sheets AP History; app notes 1:120 (sub 9)
## SUB 1 | Amuktamalyada and Krishnadevaraya's Own Works
[120:1:0] # Amuktamalyada
[120:1:1] - **Author:** **Krishnadevaraya** himself (APPSC AEE; Tribal Welfare Officer; AP History PYQ) – not Peddana, Tenali Ramakrishna, Nannaya, Nanne Choda, Palkuriki Somanatha, Gona Budda Reddy, Gangamba or Praudha Devaraya.
[120:1:2] - **Language:** **Telugu** – his only Telugu work; a work on **statecraft** (rajaniti) as well as devotion. NDA 2017 "NOT correct": "**wrote Amuktamalyada in Sanskrit**".
[120:1:3] - **Other name:** **Vishnuchittiyam**; meaning "**one who offers the garland she has worn**".
[120:1:4] - **Legend:** **Andhra Mahavishnu of Srikakulam** (Krishna district) told the king in a **dream** to write it, while he was **resting at Srikakulam** during the **Kalinga campaign**; dedicated to **Lord Venkateswara**.
[120:1:5] - **Central theme:** the **wedding of Goda Devi (Andal) with Sri Ranganatha** (Endowment 2022) – not his victories, the Ashtadiggajas or his literary achievements; sub-stories **Yamunacharya Charitra** and **Maladasari Katha**.
[120:1:6] - **Political maxims:** kingship, administration and statecraft; social, religious and economic life.
[120:1:7] - Preface: "**Desa Bhashalandu Telugu Lessa**" (Telugu is the best of the regional languages).
[120:1:8] - One of the **Telugu Pancha Kavyas**; the **first Telugu work named after its heroine**.
[120:1:9] # What Amuktamalyada does NOT contain (G2 2003; AP History PYQ)
[120:1:10] - Its preface **describes the king's Kalinga campaign** (the march to Vijayawada and the halt at Srikakulam), and the work **discusses political matters**.
[120:1:11] - It does **not** reveal a **genealogy from Bukkaraya to Krishnadevaraya** – the Tuluvas were not descendants of Bukka → this is the answer.
[120:1:12] - ⚠ Some keys of the G2 2003 paper print "describes the invasions"; that is wrong, since the preface narrates the Kalinga campaign.
[120:1:13] # Works → language
[120:1:14] TABLE head: Work | Language
  [120:1:14.0] Amuktamalyada | Telugu (his only Telugu work)
  [120:1:14.1] Jambavati Kalyanam / Parinayam (drama; Krishna weds Jambavati; mentions Virupaksha, Vasantotsavams) | Sanskrit (APPSC G2 2019; G2 Mains; AP History PYQ)
  [120:1:14.2] Usha Parinayam | Sanskrit
  [120:1:14.3] Madalasa Charita | Sanskrit
  [120:1:14.4] Rasamanjari | Sanskrit
  [120:1:14.5] Jnana Chintamani | Sanskrit
  [120:1:14.6] Satyavadhu Parinayam | Sanskrit
[120:1:15] - **Court musician:** **Lakshminatha** wrote *Sangita Suryodaya*.
[120:1:16] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History – Vijayanagara p.4; Wikipedia, Amuktamalyada (preface: Kalinga campaign, Srikakulam dream); app notes 1:120 (sub 7)
## SUB 2 | The Saluva Dynasty and the Two Usurpations
[120:2:0] # Decline of the Sangamas
[120:2:1] - **Nuniz** called **Virupaksha II** a drunkard and **Praudha Raya** worthless; Gajapati and Bahmani invasions ate into the kingdom.
[120:2:2] # The two usurpations
[120:2:3] TABLE head: Year | Event
  [120:2:3.0] 1485 | First usurpation: Saluva Narasimha of Chandragiri expels Praudha Raya; ends the Sangama dynasty, begins the Saluva dynasty
  [120:2:3.1] 1505 | Second usurpation: Vira Narasimha (son of Tuluva Narasa Nayaka) kills Immadi Narasimha, the last Saluva, at Penugonda; begins the Tuluva dynasty
  [120:2:3.2] 1509 | Krishnadevaraya crowned on 8 August 1509
  [120:2:3.3] 1529 | Achyutaraya crowned at Tirupati
  [120:2:3.4] 1543 | Sadasiva made a figurehead under Aliya Rama Raya
  [120:2:3.5] Jan 1565 | Talikota (Rakshasi-Tangadi / Bannihatti): Rama Raya beheaded; flight to Penukonda
[120:2:4] - **Dynasty after the first usurpation:** **Saluva** (AP History PYQ). **Came to power:** **1485** (G2 2012).
[120:2:5] - **Founder of the Saluva dynasty:** **Saluva Narasimha (Narasimharaya)** (SSC 2005; AP History PYQ) – not Immadi Narasimha (last Saluva), Vira Narasimha (Tuluva founder), Praudha Devaraya or Rama Raya.
[120:2:6] - **UPSC 2003 A–R:** A "Saluva Narasimha ended the old dynasty and took the royal title" ✓; R "to save the kingdom from further degeneration and disintegration" ✓ and **explains A**.
[120:2:7] - **IAS 2004 (×3): all four correct** – Saluva Narasimha ended the Sangamas; Vira Narasimha deposed the last Saluva; Vira Narasimha → younger brother **Krishnadevaraya**; Krishnadevaraya → half-brother **Achyuta Raya**.
[120:2:8] - **Chronology (APSLPRB 2023):** Deva Raya II (Sangama) → Saluva Narasimha → Achyuta Deva Raya (Tuluva) → Venkatapati II (Aravidu) = **ii, iv, i, iii**.
[120:2:9] # Saluva Narasimha (1485–91)
[120:2:10] TABLE head: Angle | Fact
  [120:2:10.0] Origin | Telugu clan from Kalyana; governor of Chandragiri
  [120:2:10.1] Capital | Kalyanapuram → Chandragiri
  [120:2:10.2] Title | Raya Maharasu; his general Tuluva Narasa Nayaka took the throne for him
  [120:2:10.3] Army | Arab horses from Ormuz, Arab cavalry; introduced Samugaris (gunmen)
  [120:2:10.4] Lost | Udayagiri to Gajapati Purushottama
  [120:2:10.5] Court poet | Rajanatha Dindima – *Saluvabhyudayam*
  [120:2:10.6] Contemporary | Annamacharya (Tallapaka, 1408–1503): 32,000 kirtanas on Venkateswara; wife Timmakka wrote Subhadra Kalyanam
[120:2:11] - **Annamayya was a contemporary of:** **Saluva Narasimha Raya** (APPSC G2 2011; AP History PYQ) – not Harihara, Devaraya I, II or III.
[120:2:12] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History – Vijayanagara p.3, p.13-15; NextGen previous papers (src/ap-history/nextgen-previous-papers.txt); Rocket AP History; app notes 1:120 (sub 0, 1)
## SUB 3 | Titles and Towns of Krishnadevaraya
[120:3:0] # Titles
[120:3:1] TABLE head: Title | Note
  [120:3:1.0] Yavana Rajya Sthapanacharya | For restoring the Bahmani Sultan Mahmud Shah (freed from Ali/Kasim Barid) after the Raichur–Bidar campaign; celebrated in Manucharitra
  [120:3:1.1] Andhra Bhoja, Sahiti Samarangana Sarvabhauma | Literary patronage
  [120:3:1.2] Gajapati Gajakuta Pakaveni, Dakshinapatha Swami, Kannada Rajya Rama Ramana, Mururaya Raganda, Paribhuta Suratrana | Others
[120:3:2] - **Yavana Rajya Sthapanacharya = Krishnadevaraya** (asked ×5: G2 2000; AP History PYQ) – not Deva Raya I or II, Saluva Narasimha, Tuluva Narasa Nayaka, Virupaksha II, Harihara II or Tirumala Raya.
[120:3:3] - **Andhra Bhoja = Krishnadevaraya** (JPSC 2013) – not Rajendra Chola, Harihara or Bukka.
[120:3:4] - **Gajabetekara** is **Devaraya II's** title, not Krishnadevaraya's. **Andhra Kavita Pitamaha** is Peddana's.
[120:3:5] # Towns founded
[120:3:6] TABLE head: Town | Named after
  [120:3:6.0] Nagalapuram (suburb of Vijayanagara) | His mother Nagala Devi / Nagamamba (Nagalamba)
  [120:3:6.1] Hospet (Tirumaladevipattana) | Queen Tirumaladevi
[120:3:7] - **Nagalapuram built by:** **Krishnadevaraya** (G2 2000; State PSC) – not Bukka I, Devaraya I, Harihara or Virupaksha. **Nagamamba** = **mother of Krishnadevaraya** (AP History PYQ).
[120:3:8] - ⚠ Do not confuse with **Nagalapuram in Palnadu** (ancient **Halampuram**).
[120:3:9] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History – Vijayanagara p.4, p.19; app notes 1:120 (sub 6)
## SUB 4 | Tuluva Succession, Court and Contemporaries
[120:4:0] # Tuluva origin
[120:4:1] - From **Tuluvanadu** near Mysore; progenitor **Timmaraju**; mother tongue **Kannada**, but **Telugu** favoured at court.
[120:4:2] - **Tuluva Narasa Nayaka:** Saluva general and real ruler under Immadi Narasimha; died 1503. **Founder of the Tuluva dynasty = Vira Narasimha** (1505), not Narasa Nayaka.
[120:4:3] - **Krishnadevaraya belonged to the Tuluva dynasty** (AMVI 2023) – not Pandya, Kakatiya or Qutb Shahi.
[120:4:4] # Succession
[120:4:5] TABLE head: Ruler | Immediate successor
  [120:4:5.0] Praudha Deva Raya | Saluva Narasimha
  [120:4:5.1] Immadi Narasimha | Vira Narasimha
  [120:4:5.2] Vira Narasimha (1505–09) | Krishnadevaraya (his younger half-brother)
  [120:4:5.3] Krishnadevaraya (1509–29) | Achyuta Deva Raya (his half-brother)
[120:4:6] - **King before Krishnadevaraya:** **Vira Narasimha** (G2-A 1989). **After him:** **Achyuta Devaraya** (Asst. Archaeologist 2011) – not Rama Raya or Sadasiva.
[120:4:7] - **Aravidu rule began with:** **Tirumala Deva Raya** (Penukonda).
[120:4:8] - **Death of Krishnadevaraya:** **1529** (NextGen; reign often written 1509–1529/30).
[120:4:9] # Court
[120:4:10] - **Prime Minister:** **Saluva Timmarusu (Appaji)** – minister of **Krishnadevaraya** (AP History PYQ), not Saluva Narasimha, Rajaraja Narendra or Kyatya Varma; later blinded on suspicion.
[120:4:11] - **Rajaguru:** **Vyasatirtha (Vyasaraya)**, Madhva saint (AP History PYQ) – not Vidyaranya (Sangama founders' guru). His disciple **Purandaradasa** (father of Carnatic music) was a contemporary.
[120:4:12] # Contemporaries
[120:4:13] - **Babur** (1526–30): Krishnadevaraya was his contemporary (FRO 2009; SI 2011); Babur praised him in the **Tuzuk-i-Baburi** as the most powerful ruler of India. Not Akbar, Aurangzeb, Firoz Tughlaq or Alauddin Khalji.
[120:4:14] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History – Vijayanagara p.3-5, p.17-20; app notes 1:120 (sub 2)
## SUB 5 | Krishnadevaraya's Campaigns – Raichur, Golconda and Kalinga
[120:5:0] # Campaigns
[120:5:1] TABLE head: Campaign | Year | Result
  [120:5:1.0] Diwani / Kovilkonda | 1509–10 | Bahmani "jihad" crushed; Yusuf Adil Khan killed
  [120:5:1.1] Raichur Doab and Bidar | 1510–12 | Raichur taken; freed Sultan Mahmud Shah from Barid → title Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya
  [120:5:1.2] Ummattur / Sivasamudram | 1512–13 | Gangaraja defeated; new province at Srirangapatna
  [120:5:1.3] Kalinga | 1513–1519 | Udayagiri, Kondaveedu, Kondapalli, Simhachalam, Cuttack (1518)
  [120:5:1.4] Battle of Raichur | 1520 | Ismail Adil Shah of Bijapur routed with Portuguese help; Gulbarga taken 1523
[120:5:2] - **Bijapur Sultan at Raichur (1520):** **Ismail Adil Khan / Shah** (G2 2000; AP History PYQ) – not Ahmed Barid, Muhammad Shah I or Mujahid Shah.
[120:5:3] - **"Great battle of 1520":** the battle of Raichur, which Telugu texts name **Gobburu** (the field near Raichur) – G2-A 1989; **Mudgal** was Devaraya I vs Firoz Shah Bahmani.
[120:5:4] - **Battle of Golconda:** fought against **Quli Qutb Shah** of Golconda (BPSC 1999), who had taken forts while the king fought the Gajapatis – not Qutbuddin Aibak, Ismail Adil Shah or the Gajapati.
[120:5:5] - **Yusuf Adil Khan** (Kovilkonda, 1509–10) ≠ **Ismail Adil Shah** (Raichur, 1520).
[120:5:6] # The Kalinga campaign against Prataparudra Gajapati
[120:5:7] TABLE head: Fort / place | What happened
  [120:5:7.0] Udayagiri (1513–14) | Fell after an 18-month siege; Balakrishna idol taken to Hampi (Krishna temple built for it)
  [120:5:7.1] Kondaveedu | Taken with Saluva Timmarusu's help (split Veerabhadra Gajapati's army); king performed Talapurusha Danam at Amaravati
  [120:5:7.2] Kondapalli and Bejawada | Gajapati forces defeated
  [120:5:7.3] Vinukonda, Addanki, Kandukuru | Also taken
  [120:5:7.4] Cuttack | Reached in 1518; Gajapati sued for peace
[120:5:8] - **Idol taken from Udayagiri:** **Balakrishna** (G2-A 1989) – not Ramachandra, Ugranarasimha or Virupaksha.
[120:5:9] - **Victory pillar (Jayastambha) for the conquest of coastal Andhra:** **Potnuru** (Padmanabham mandal, near Visakhapatnam; Bezawada inscription 1516: "Simhadri-Potnuru") – AP History PYQ; G2 PYQ. Not Kondaveedu, Kondapalli, Udayagiri, Rajahmundry or Nagarjunakonda. Lists of his pillars give **Potnuru and Simhachalam** (the inscription's "Simhadri-Potnuru").
[120:5:10] - ⚠ The old note "APPSC key (2025) gave Kondaveedu" is unverified; Kondaveedu was a fort taken, not the pillar site.
[120:5:11] - **Temple grants:** **Simhachalam** – diamond necklace to Varaha Narasimha; **Mangalagiri** – land to **Lakshmi Narasimha**.
[120:5:12] - **Peace terms:** Prataparudra's daughter (**Tukka / Bhadradevi**) married Krishnadevaraya; lands **north of the Krishna** went back to the Gajapati.
[120:5:13] - **Salt:** **Pedaganjam and Chinaganjam** were famous for salt; the salt pans at **Pedaganjam** were taxed.
[120:5:14] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History – Vijayanagara p.19-20; Wikipedia, Battle of Raichur; Deccan Chronicle (Potnuru Vijayastupam, 2016); app notes 1:120 (sub 3, 4)

  [120:6:0.1] Gangadevi / Gangamba (queen of Kumara Kampana) | *Madhura Vijayam* – Kampana's conquest of Madurai | Sanskrit

## SUB 7 | The Portuguese and Foreign Visitors
[120:7:0] # Portuguese
[120:7:1] TABLE head: Ruler | Portuguese contact
  [120:7:1.0] Vira Narasimha | Allied with Viceroy Francisco de Almeida → horses and military training
  [120:7:1.1] Krishnadevaraya – Goa (1510) | Backed Afonso de Albuquerque's capture of Goa from Bijapur
  [120:7:1.2] Krishnadevaraya – Raichur (1520) | Portuguese help
  [120:7:1.3] Sadasiva / Rama Raya | Defeated Governor Martin de Souza for damaging temples; João de Castro made peace

  [120:7:4.0] Domingo Paes (Portuguese) | Vivid eyewitness description of the House of Victory, the king's looks and the city (G2 Mains)

## SUB 8 | Achyutaraya, Sadasiva and Aliya Rama Raya
[120:8:0] - **Achyutaraya** (1529–42): named heir by Krishnadevaraya; crowned at **Tirupati** and **Srikalahasti** (the only king crowned at Tirumala-Tirupati).
[120:8:1] - **Assembly hall:** Achyutaraya's sabha = **Venkatavilasa Mantapam** (AP History PYQ); Krishnadevaraya's = **Bhuvana Vijayam**. (NextGen also has Venkatapati II's literary meets at "Venkatapati Vilasam".)
[120:8:2] - **Aliya Rama Raya:** Krishnadevaraya's **son-in-law**, of the **Aravidu** family; killed **Salakam Tirumala** (1543); made **Sadasiva** a figurehead.
[120:8:3] - **Talikota** (January **1565**), also **Rakshasi-Tangadi** / Bannihatti: Rama Raya beheaded; Sadasiva and Tirumala fled to **Penukonda**. **Last Tuluva ruler = Sadasiva**.
[120:8:4] - **Latest – Sadasivakona inscriptions** (ASI, **June 2026**): three **trilingual** (Telugu, Tamil, Kannada) inscriptions of **1554 CE** in the **Seshachalam forest, Tirupati district**; record Sadasiva Raya's holy bath and transfer of **Kaanika** taxes from Gudimallam temple lands.
[120:8:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History – Vijayanagara p.5, p.20-22; app notes 1:120 (sub 11)

=== NOTES 1:121 | Vijayanagara Administration - Nayankara and Ayagar Systems, Amaram Tenure, Revenue and Army
## SUB 0 | Central Departments – Kandachara, Athavane and the Council
[121:0:0] # Departments
[121:0:1] - **Rayavachakam** records **nine departments**, each headed by a **Samprati**.
[121:0:2] TABLE head: Department | Function
  [121:0:2.0] Kandachara | Military – standing army, headed by the Senapati / Dalavayi
  [121:0:2.1] Athavane / Attavana | Revenue / finance
  [121:0:2.2] Bhandara (Sri Bhandara) | Treasury
  [121:0:2.3] Dharmasana | Judicial; Pradvivaka = judge
[121:0:3] - **Kandachara dealt with military affairs / defence** – asked ×7 (APPSC G2 2019; G2 Mains; SI 2016; AP History PYQ ×3; G2 PYQ). Not revenue, finance, land survey (Bhoomi Sisthu), police, justice or religious institutions; **Athavana** = revenue, **Dandaniti** / **Mansabdari** are distractors.
[121:0:4] # Officers and the council
[121:0:5] TABLE head: Officer | Role
  [121:0:5.0] Mahapradhani / Prime Minister | Chief minister presiding over the council of pradhanis; also called Sarva Sirah Pradhani, Sabhanayaka, Tantranayaka; e.g. Saluva Timmarusu
  [121:0:5.1] Dalavayi | Commander-in-chief
  [121:0:5.2] Rayasams | Secretaries (Kondamarasu, Ayyamarasu)
  [121:0:5.3] Karanikas | Scribes
[121:0:6] - **President of the imperial council:** the **Prime Minister** (AMVI 2009) – "Sabhanayaka" is only another name of the same office; the king was advised by, not president of, the council.
[121:0:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History – Vijayanagara p.28; NextGen previous papers p.15 (Kandachara); app notes 1:121 (sub 1)
## SUB 1 | Amara-Nayankara System and the Palegars
[121:1:0] # Amaram and Amaranayakas
[121:1:1] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [121:1:1.0] Amaram | Land granted to military chiefs instead of cash salary; the Rayas owned all land
  [121:1:1.1] Amaranayakas | Holders; also Nayaks, Palaiyagars, Poligars
  [121:1:1.2] Mahamandaleshwara | Their title; more autonomy than Durgadannayakas
[121:1:2] - **Nayakas were:** **military chiefs controlling particular territories** (CDS 2001) – not central ministers, cavalry soldiers or temple priests.
[121:1:3] - **Amaranayakas were NOT** "wise men who advised the rulers" – they were **military commanders**, **collected taxes**, and their **contingents** fought for the king.
[121:1:4] - **Administrative system (G1 2007):** the **Amaranayaka** (Amara-Nayankara) system – a military governor (Nayaka) given amarams for salary and army expenses.
[121:1:5] - Within the amaram: **collected taxes**, kept **law and order**, administered their territory (**palaiyam**).
[121:1:6] - **Obligations:** tribute (**Kappam**); a quota of troops, horses, elephants; attend court at **Mahanavami** with gifts; maintain forts, temples, irrigation.
[121:1:7] # Kakatiya nayankara vs Vijayanagara amara-nayankara
[121:1:8] TABLE head: Point | Kakatiya nayankara | Vijayanagara amara-nayankara
  [121:1:8.0] Origin | Prataparudra II | Grew out of the Kakatiya system
  [121:1:8.1] Scale | 75 or 77 nayakas | About 200 nayakas
  [121:1:8.2] Outcome | Discontent among older feudatories | Semi-independent, then independent Nayaka states after 1565 (Madurai, Tanjore, Keladi)
[121:1:9] # Palegars (Poligars)
[121:1:10] - **Origin:** **amara-nayakas** → Palegars when the centre weakened after **Talikota (1565)**; hereditary; **forerunners of the zamindars**.
[121:1:11] - **Who were they:** **territorial administrative and military governors** (UPPSC 2015) – not ordinary zamindars, Mahajans or traders.
[121:1:12] - **Duties under the Nayakas:** administer palaiyams, collect taxes, maintain law and order – **NOT building health and education centres**.
[121:1:13] - **Thomas Munro**, with **Campbell**, crushed the Rayalaseema Palegars and then introduced the **Ryotwari** system.
[121:1:14] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History – Vijayanagara p.28-29; app notes 1:121 (sub 4, 5, 6)
## SUB 2 | Revenue and Taxes
[121:2:0] - **Chief feature of the financial system:** **land revenue** (BPSC 1999) – usually **1/6** of produce, **1/4 or 1/3** on fertile land; land-tax documents = **Adhuvanatantram**.
[121:2:1] # Land classes
[121:2:2] TABLE head: Term | Land
  [121:2:2.0] Nanja | Wet
  [121:2:2.1] Punja | Dry
  [121:2:2.2] Bagayati | Garden
  [121:2:2.3] Banjara | Waste
[121:2:3] - **Neerarambamu / Magani** (irrigated): tax in **grain**, higher; **Kaadarambamu / Metta** (dry): cash, lower.
[121:2:4] # Tax terms
[121:2:5] TABLE head: Tax | Meaning
  [121:2:5.0] Navidadere / Kondaju | Barbers' tax
  [121:2:5.1] Maneyanna / Manevana / Illari Pannu | House tax
  [121:2:5.2] Melivamsam | Plough tax (G1 match)
  [121:2:5.3] Tudimeya | Marriage tax (G1 match)
  [121:2:5.4] Meruka | Tax on sale and purchase (APPSC G2 2011)
  [121:2:5.5] Putrodaya Kanuka | Birth of a son
  [121:2:5.6] Kalyana Kanika | Wedding tax on both parties
  [121:2:5.7] Siddhaya | Fixed levy: Pinje (cotton ginners), Eidipi (toddy tappers), Jati (professions)
[121:2:6] - **G1 match:** Navidadere–barbers, Melivamsam–ploughs, Manevana–houses, Tudimeya–marriage = **a-II, b-III, c-IV, d-I**.
[121:2:7] - **Meruka ≠ Mera:** Mera = the Ayagars' harvest share; Merulu = the Talari's grain gifts; Meruka = sale–purchase tax (not Magani/Metta land or export–import).
[121:2:8] - **Marriage tax:** first remitted by **Saluva Narasimha**; **totally withdrawn by Krishnadevaraya** (Rocket; NextGen previous papers – APPSC G1 2010). ⚠ Some keys give Sadasiva Raya; Sadasiva's inscriptions (Rama Raya's regency) record the **barbers'** tax remission (at Kandoja's request).
[121:2:9] - Market (**santhalu**) tax rights auctioned to **Sunkandarlu**.
[121:2:10] ~~ Sources: NextGen Rocket Sheets AP History (src/ap-history/rocket-ap-history.txt) p.18; NextGen previous papers (src/ap-history/nextgen-previous-papers.txt) p.45; NextGen AP History – Vijayanagara p.6, p.28; South Indian Inscriptions IX (Amarapuram 1544, barbers' exemption); app notes 1:121 (sub 8)
## SUB 3 | Justice and Police
[121:3:0] - **Pradvivaka:** adviser to the king in the **judiciary**; judge who explained legal texts (APPSC G2 2019; G2 PYQ) – not military, revenue or espionage.
[121:3:1] - **Authoritative law book:** **Parasara Madhaviyam** – Madhavacharya's commentary on the Parashara Smriti (with Yajnavalkya) – not Amuktamalyada or the Arthashastra.
[121:3:2] - **Himsodbhava** = criminal; **Dhanodbhava** = civil.
[121:3:3] - The **Raya** was the supreme judge; ministers like **Timmarusu** ("Dharma Pratipalaka") also tried cases.
[121:3:4] - **Punishments:** treason – **death**; theft – **mutilation**; Brahmins – **life imprisonment** instead of death.
[121:3:5] # Police
[121:3:6] TABLE head: Level | Police (Kavali system)
  [121:3:6.0] Village | Talari
  [121:3:6.1] Sthala | Kavali Daru
  [121:3:6.2] Towns | Peta Kavalidaru
[121:3:7] - **Padikaval:** the system in which **police rights were sold** to individuals (AP History PYQ) – not Athavana or Kandachara.
[121:3:8] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History – Vijayanagara p.28; Rocket AP History p.15 (Pradvivaka); NextGen previous papers p.14; app notes 1:121 (sub 10)
## SUB 4 | Provincial and Village Administration – the Ayagars
[121:4:0] # Provincial units
[121:4:1] TABLE head: Unit | Head
  [121:4:1.0] Rajya / Mandala (province) – the largest unit | Prince (Sangama princes titled Odeyar) or Durga Dannayaka
  [121:4:1.1] Nadu / Seema (district) | Nadagauda; Parupatyagar
  [121:4:1.2] Sthala / Kampana | Reddi, Gauda, Sthalakaranam
  [121:4:1.3] Grama (village) | 12 Ayagars
[121:4:2] - **Biggest unit:** **Mandalam** (RPSC 2012) – not Kottam, Nadu or Kurram.
[121:4:3] - **Parupatyagar:** the king's officer of the nadu/sima who **collected revenue** and **repaired and maintained forts** (AP History PYQ).
[121:4:4] - About **17 rajyams** under **Achyutaraya**. Governors could **mint coins** and levy or remit taxes, and were **frequently transferred**.
[121:4:5] TABLE head: Andhra Rajya | Fact
  [121:4:5.0] Udayagiri | Most important; Paka and Muliki districts
  [121:4:5.1] Chandragiri | Saluva Narasimha was its governor before 1485
  [121:4:5.2] Penukonda | Tirumala's headquarters after Talikota
  [121:4:5.3] Gooty (Gutti) | Fort raised to rajya status
[121:4:6] # Village – the Ayagars
[121:4:7] - **12 hereditary Ayagars** per village: Karanam (accountant), Reddi (head), Talari (watchman), Purohita, plus artisans – Kamsali, Kummari, Vadrangi, **Kase (mason / house-builder)**, Kammari, Chakali, Mangali.
[121:4:8] - **Pay:** no cash salary – tax-free **Manyam** lands and a harvest share **Mera**.
[121:4:9] TABLE head: Officer | Duties
  [121:4:9.0] Karanam | Accounts, land and crop registers
  [121:4:9.1] Reddi | Village head (Gauda / Gowda in Karnataka) and revenue collector
  [121:4:9.2] Talari | Watchman; collected Merulu
  [121:4:9.3] Begari | Supervised forced labour (vetti)
[121:4:10] - **Village headman:** **Gowda** (APPSC Jr Asst key) – the Karnataka name of the Andhra **Reddi**; Chowdhary and Parupatyadar are wrong.
[121:4:11] - **Brahmins as Karanams:** **Harihara I** followed the **Kakatiya** practice (APPSC Jr Asst) – the Sangamas inherited Kakatiya village administration.
[121:4:12] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History – Vijayanagara p.29; Rocket AP History; app notes 1:121 (sub 3, 7)
## SUB 5 | Army, Forts and the Nature of the State
[121:5:0] # Army
[121:5:1] - Two divisions: the **Siddha (standing) army** under the **Dalavayi** (via Kandachara), paid every **4 months**, and the **Amaranayaka** contingents.
[121:5:2] - **Bukka I** = first to use **cannon**; **Saluva Narasimha** introduced **Samugaris** (gunmen).
[121:5:3] - **Horses** (Arabian, Persian) imported through **Goa, Honnavar, Bhatkal**.
[121:5:4] - **Four kinds of forts:** **Giri** (hill), **Sthala**, **Jala**, **Vana** – under **Durga Dannayakas**.
[121:5:5] - **Against sieges:** Vijayanagara enclosed **large agricultural tracts within the fortified area** (APPSC G1 2017; NCERT Themes II ch. 7) – granaries were the usual practice elsewhere.
[121:5:6] # Nature of the state
[121:5:7] - **King:** supreme head and fountain of justice, acting within **Dharma** and with **his ministers'** counsel.
[121:5:8] - **Nilakanta Sastri:** "**military administration**"; **Burton Stein:** "**segmentary state**".
[121:5:9] # Political maxims in Amuktamalyada
[121:5:10] TABLE head: Area | Maxim
  [121:5:10.0] Revenue | Bulk of revenue to the army
  [121:5:10.1] Trade | Improve harbours; encourage import of horses, elephants, gems; treat foreign merchants generously
  [121:5:10.2] Welfare | Build tanks; win over forest tribes rather than only crush them
  [121:5:10.3] Forts | Brahmins should command forts
[121:5:11] - It refers to the king's **campaigns** and gives political advice, but gives **no genealogy from Bukka**.
[121:5:12] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History – Vijayanagara p.28-29; NCERT Themes in Indian History II ch. 7; app notes 1:121 (sub 0, 2, 9)

## SUB 2 | Society – Castes and Social Groups
[122:2:0] - **Vipravinodins (Vipravinodulu):** **Brahmin jugglers** who gave **indoor entertainment to Brahmins only** (APPSC G2 2017, 2019; ×6) – a sect of **Brahmins**, not Shudras, weavers, Kshatriyas or Vaisyas.
[122:2:1] - **Balanjalu (Balijas, Veerabalijas):** **traders / business** – like the Ayyavalu; not weavers, herders or barbers.
[122:2:2] - **Four varnas** and about **18 castes**.
[122:2:3] TABLE head: Group | Occupation
  [122:2:3.0] Vaidikas / Niyogis | Brahmin priests / Brahmin officials
  [122:2:3.1] Settis, Komatis, Balijas | Traders
  [122:2:3.2] Sudras | Farmers – backbone of the kingdom
  [122:2:3.3] Vira Panchalas | Artisans (gold, iron, brass, wood, stone)
  [122:2:3.4] Kaikkolars, Padmasalis, Jandra, Kuruba | Weavers
[122:2:4] - **Valangai (right-hand)** = mainly agricultural and trading groups; **Idangai (left-hand)** = mainly **artisans** and some traders; the division began in **Chola** times.
[122:2:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen previous papers p.10, p.15; NextGen Vijayanagara Kingdom p.30 (weavers); app notes 1:122 (sub 1, 2)
## SUB 3 | Women, Marriage and Social Customs
[122:3:0] - **Sati, polygamy and dowry** were prevalent and **child marriages were common** (NextGen) – "child marriages were unknown" is the wrong statement.
[122:3:1] - **Most popular form of marriage:** **Brahma vivaha** (the father gives his daughter to a suitable groom) – not Daiva, Gandharva or Prajapatya.
[122:3:2] - **No strict purdah**; women served as bodyguards, wrestlers, accountants, dancers; learned women **Gangadevi** and **Tirumalamba**.
[122:3:3] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [122:3:3.0] Kanyashulkam | Bride price
  [122:3:3.1] Varashulkam | Dowry
  [122:3:3.2] Benabaga | Slavery
  [122:3:3.3] Devadasis | Temple dancers trained in music and dance; often land-owning and respected
[122:3:4] - Prostitution was state-recognised and **taxed** (Abdur Razzaq).
[122:3:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen Vijayanagara Kingdom p.6 ("Sati, child marriages, and dowry systems were prevalent"); app notes 1:122 (sub 3)
## SUB 4 | Religion and Festivals
[122:4:0] - **Tutelary deity:** **Virupaksha** (a form of Shiva, Pampapati of Hampi) – the kings ruled on his behalf; family deity of the Sangamas.
[122:4:1] - **Mahanavami (Dasara):** the festival celebrated on the grandest scale every year – on the **Mahanavami Dibba** built by Krishnadevaraya; nayakas brought tribute; the financial year began with it; described by **Paes and Abdur Razzaq**; Burton Stein compared it to an **Ashvamedha**.
[122:4:2] - Vasantotsava (spring festival) – in Krishnadevaraya's **Jambavati Parinayam**.
[122:4:3] TABLE head: Ruler / dynasty | Faith / act
  [122:4:3.0] Sangamas | Shaiva; guru Kalamukha Kriya Shakti
  [122:4:3.1] Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu | Vaishnava; Tirupati rose under Saluva Narasimha
  [122:4:3.2] Devaraya II | Enlisted Muslims in the army; built a mosque
  [122:4:3.3] Venkatapati Raya II (Aravidu) | Venkateswara replaced Virupaksha as main deity; allowed a church at Chandragiri (Jesuits)
[122:4:4] - Centres: **Srisailam, Tripurantakam, Srikalahasti** (Shaiva); Tirupati, Mangalagiri (Vaishnava); **Ahobilam, Kadiri** (Narasimha); Narahari Tirtha spread Dvaita from **Srikurmam**.
[122:4:5] - **Penugonda (West Godavari)** = seat of **Vasavi Kanyaka Parameswari** (Arya Vysyas) – not Penukonda (Anantapur).
[122:4:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen Vijayanagara Kingdom p.31; NextGen previous papers p.13 (Vasavi at Penugonda); app notes 1:122 (sub 4, 5)
## SUB 5 | Agriculture and Irrigation – Porumamilla and the Tanks
[122:5:0] - **Porumamilla inscription (Kadapa):** lays down the **12 rules (Dwadasa Sutras)** for building a **tank (tataka)** (APPSC G2 2012, 2019; ×3) – issued by Prince **Bhaskara (Bhaskara Bhavadura / Bhaskara Mantri)**, son of Bukka I, for the **Anantasagaram** tank (**1369**) – not Tummalagudem, Korlagallu, Bitragunta, Palampet, Pakhala or Bodhan.
[122:5:1] - **Narasambudhi tatakam** = **Vijayanagara** period (Saluva Narasimha, Anantapur) – not Kakatiya, Yadava, Hoysala, Velama or Reddi.
[122:5:2] - Kings promoted agriculture by building **tanks (ponds), dams and wells** – tank-building was one of the **Saptasantanas** (seven meritorious acts).
[122:5:3] TABLE head: Ruler | Work
  [122:5:3.0] Bukka I | Siruveru tank near Penukonda
  [122:5:3.1] Saluva Narasimha | Narasambudhi tank
  [122:5:3.2] Krishnadevaraya | Nagalapuram tank (Portuguese engineers), Toragallu dam, Kambham tank
[122:5:4] - Temple economy: **Devadaya** = temple villages / endowments; **Sri Bhandara** = temple treasury kept by the Karanam; **Samayas** (merchant guilds) met in **temple mandapas**; main state revenue = **land tax**.
[122:5:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen previous papers p.15 ("Porumamilla inscription describes the 12 rules ... tank construction"); Rocket AP History (inscriptions table: Porumamilla – Prince Bhaskara Bhavadura); NextGen Vijayanagara Kingdom p.30; app notes 1:122 (sub 7)
## SUB 6 | Trade, Industries and Ports
[122:6:0] - **Chief import = horses** (from Arabia, Persia, Central Asia) (APPSC; WBCS 2020) – not pearls, precious stones, silk, pottery, wine or gold; **chief export = Kalamkari** cloth.
[122:6:1] - **Kudirai Chettis** = local **horse merchants** of the **Vijayanagara** empire (NCERT Themes II) – not Chola, Delhi Sultanate or Mughal.
[122:6:2] - **Vajrakarur** (Anantapur) = **diamonds** – diamonds mined in Kurnool, Gutti, Anantapur.
[122:6:3] TABLE head: Centre | Product / role
  [122:6:3.0] Tadipatri, Adoni, Gutti | Textiles, Kalamkari
  [122:6:3.1] Gutti, Rayadurg | Silk
  [122:6:3.2] Venkatagiri | Zari
  [122:6:3.3] Pulicat, Mylapore, Motupalli, Machilipatnam | East-coast ports
  [122:6:3.4] Honnavar, Bhatkal, Goa, Mangalore, Calicut | West-coast ports
  [122:6:3.5] Motupalli | Taken by Devaraya I; Motupalli Dharma Sasanam (1416)
[122:6:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen Vijayanagara Kingdom p.30 ("Imports included horses, silk, musk, pearls; exports comprised Kalankari cloths"); NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History II ch.7 (kudirai chettis); NextGen AP Geography 03 (Vajrakarur diamonds); app notes 1:122 (sub 8)
## SUB 7 | Revenue and Coinage
[122:7:0] - **Burhan-i-Maasir** (Nizam Shahi chronicle) put **Sadasiva Raya's** annual income at **12 crore huns** – not Abdur Razzaq, Futuh-us-Salatin or Sewell.
[122:7:1] - **Coins and regions (IAS 2006):** **Pagoda – Vijayanagar**, Mahmudi – Gujarat, Muzaffari – Malwa, Sikandri – North India → **2 1 4 3**.
[122:7:2] TABLE head: Coin | Metal / value
  [122:7:2.0] Varaha (Pagoda, Gadyana, Honnu) | Gold, largest
  [122:7:2.1] Pratapa (Mada) | Gold, half a varaha
  [122:7:2.2] Panam (fanam) | Gold, most used
  [122:7:2.3] Tar, Pesado | Silver
  [122:7:2.4] Jital, Kasu | Copper
  [122:7:2.5] Symbol | Hanuman – Harihara and Bukka; Venkateswara, Balakrishna – Krishnadevaraya; Garuda – Achyutaraya; Varaha – Tirumala Raya
[122:7:3] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval 04 p.75, p.141 (gold pagodas, highest denomination); app notes 1:122 (sub 7, 9)

=== NOTES 1:123 | Vijayanagara Art and Architecture - Hampi, Gopurams, Kalyana Mandapa, Vitthala Temple, Painting
## SUB 0 | Hampi – the Capital, its Ruins and its Plan
[123:0:0] - **Ruins of Vijayanagara = Hampi** (SI 2011; UPPCS 2008; ×5) – not Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmadnagar or Baroda (sultanate / other capitals).
[123:0:1] - On the **southern bank of the Tungabhadra** (Jharkhand PCS 2023) – not Narmada, Godavari or Bhima; in **Vijayanagara district, Karnataka** (SSC 2019).
[123:0:2] - "**Group of Monuments at Hampi**" = UNESCO World Heritage Site, **1986**; the **Vittala stone chariot** is on the reverse of the **₹50 note**.
[123:0:3] - **"Athens of Vijayanagara"** = the **valley area around the Virupaksha temple** (app notes; APPSC) – not Nellore-Chittoor, Bangalore-Kolar-Chittoor or the Pandya country.
[123:0:4] - **Fields inside the fortifications:** so the city would have **food supply even if invaders blockaded it for months** (NCERT; Paes) – not irrigation, revenue accounts or royal granaries.
[123:0:5] - **Why so many temples:** to **legitimise royal authority** by association with the deities – the kings ruled on behalf of **Virupaksha** (NCERT).
[123:0:6] - **Raw material:** the **Deccan plateau** gave easy local access to **stone (granite)** – that made temples like Lepakshi possible.
[123:0:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen Vijayanagara Kingdom p.1, p.8; NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History II ch.7 (fortifications enclosing fields; temples and legitimacy); app notes 1:123 (sub 1, 8)
## SUB 1 | Hampi Temples – Virupaksha, Vitthala, Hazara Rama
[123:1:0] TABLE head: Temple | Popular name / deity | Builder and facts
  [123:1:0.0] Virupaksha | Pampapati; Shiva – the kingdom's deity | First and largest temple of Hampi; 7th-century core; enlarged by Lakkana Dandesha under Devaraya II; Krishnadevaraya added the central hall and eastern gopuram (1510); ceiling paintings incl. Vidyaranya in procession
  [123:1:0.1] Vitthala (Vithalalayam) | Saptaswara Devalayam; Vishnu (Vithoba) | Begun under Devaraya II, expanded by Krishnadevaraya, continued under Achyutaraya; 56 musical ("SaReGaMa") pillars; stone chariot
  [123:1:0.2] Hazara Rama | Ramachandra temple (APPSC G2 2008) – royal chapel | Krishnadevaraya (NextGen; Rocket; MPPSC 2014) – many art histories date its core to Devaraya I/II; Ramayana friezes
  [123:1:0.3] Krishna | Bala Krishna | Krishnadevaraya – idol brought from Udayagiri
  [123:1:0.4] Achyutaraya | Tiruvengalanatha | 1534, set up by Hiriya Tirumalaraja
[123:1:1] - **Musical pillars:** **Vittala temple, Hampi** (UPSC 2007) – not Belur, Bhadrachalam or Srirangam.
[123:1:2] - **Virupaksha is at Hampi** (UPSC 2009) – "Virupaksha – Thiruvananthapuram" is the **wrong pair** (APPSC G1 2019 ×2); Kandariya Mahadeva – Khajuraho, Lingaraja – Bhubaneswar, Mahabodhi – Bodh Gaya, Dilwara – Mount Abu, Brihadeswara – Thanjavur are right.
[123:1:3] - **Kings ruled on behalf of Virupaksha** (RPSC 2012) – not Nataraja, Murugan, Venkatesa, Pampadevi or Vishnu.
[123:1:4] - **Vidyaranya's portrait:** painted on the ceiling of the **Ranga mandapa of the Virupaksha temple, Hampi** (Vidyaranya in a palanquin procession).
[123:1:5] - Krishnadevaraya's other Hampi works: **Ugra Narasimha**, Hanuman statue, monolithic Ganesha.
[123:1:6] - Distractor temples: **Kailasa, Ellora – Rashtrakuta Krishna I**; Hoysaleswara, Halebidu; Chennakesava, Belur – Vishnuvardhana.
[123:1:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen Vijayanagara Kingdom p.5 ("Built Hazara temple. Built Krishna Swamy temple and Vithoba Swamy temple at Hampi"); NextGen previous papers p.18, p.36; Rocket AP History (temples table); Wisdom Library, Vijayanagara Paintings plate 5 (Vidyaranya taken in procession); app notes 1:123 (sub 2)
## SUB 2 | The Vijayanagara Style – Raya Gopurams, Kalyana Mandapas, Secular Buildings
[123:2:0] - **Raya gopurams:** towering gateways that dwarf the central shrine – built by **Krishnadevaraya** at Hampi, Tiruvannamalai, Chidambaram, Srirangam, Tirupati (SSC 2001) – not Vidyaranya, Harihara or Rajaraja; he also built the southern Rajagopuram of the **Ekambaranatha temple, Kanchipuram (1509)**.
[123:2:1] - **Kalyana mandapas** (pillared hall for the divine marriage) = a notable feature of **Vijayanagara** temples (UPSC 2019) – not Chalukya, Chandela or Rashtrakuta.
[123:2:2] TABLE head: Feature | Meaning
  [123:2:2.0] Amman shrine | Separate goddess shrine
  [123:2:2.1] Sahasra Stambha Mandapa | Thousand-pillared hall with composite pillars
  [123:2:2.2] Ekapaadam | Hoysala-type single pillar in 3-4 sections
[123:2:3] - **Percy Brown:** the "**matured state of the Dravidian tradition**"; new: **secular buildings in temple premises**, pillared corridors added to older temples.
[123:2:4] - **Indo-Saracenic / Indo-Islamic building:** **Lotus Mahal** (Chitrangi / Padma Mahal), built by Krishnadevaraya "in Indo-Arabic style" (NextGen) – not the Vitthala or Hazara Rama temples.
[123:2:5] - Queen's Bath near the Lotus Mahal; **Mahanavami Dibba** (Krishnadevaraya); **Huzur Daftar** – Indo-Persian council chamber with **40 pillars**.
[123:2:6] - **Music:** **Sangita Suryodayam** by **Bandaru Lakshminarayana** (court musician of Krishnadevaraya) – not Krishnadevaraya, Rama Raya or Ramabhadramba; the **veena** gained prominence.
[123:2:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen Vijayanagara Kingdom p.5 (Lotus Mahal in Indo-Arabic style), p.33 (Sahasra Stambha Mandapas); Wikipedia "Ekambareswarar Temple" (southern gopuram, Krishnadevaraya 1509, inscriptions); app notes 1:123 (sub 0, 3, 9)
## SUB 3 | Lepakshi – Veerabhadra Temple, Nandi, Hanging Pillar, Paintings
[123:3:0] - **Veerabhadra (Papanaseswara) temple** on **Kurma Shailam**, near **Hindupur**, **Sri Sathya Sai district** (formerly Anantapur) – kingdom: **Vijayanagara**.
[123:3:1] - Built **c. 1530-40** by the Penukonda governors **Virupanna and Veeranna**, officers of **Achyuta Deva Raya** – "Penugonda Virupanna's Veerabhadreswara temple" = **Lepakshi** (not Tadipatri, Hampi or Kadiri).
[123:3:2] - **Three shrines:** **Shiva, Vishnu and Veerabhadra** (APPSC ASO) – not Jagannath, Kedarnath or Somnath; **Virabhadra = the fierce form of Shiva**.
[123:3:3] - **Hanging pillar** = Lepakshi (APPSC 2019).
[123:3:4] - **Huge stone bull (monolithic Nandi)** of the Vijayanagara period = **Lepakshi** – largest monolithic Nandi in India; not Tadipatri, Kadiri or Penugonda.
[123:3:5] - **Naga linga:** a linga under a **seven-hooded** serpent from a single boulder.
[123:3:6] - **Paintings:** the finest **Vijayanagara-school** murals in Andhra are at **Lepakshi** (×9) – not Srisailam, Tirupati, Tadipatri, Simhachalam, Ahobilam, Pushpagiri, Draksharama, Vontimitta, Kondapalli or Kondavidu.
[123:3:7]   - Ceilings: **Ramayana and Mahabharata**; walls: **Parvati Parinayamu**, **Tripurasura Samharam**; "pictorial inscriptions".
[123:3:8]   - Hampi Virupaksha murals: **Dashavatara**, **Girijakalyana**; style – mineral colours on lime plaster, bold outlines, **elongated, energetic figures**; survey – **Stella Kramrisch**.
[123:3:9] - **Match (APPSC JA):** largest Nandi – Lepakshi; Lord of the Seven Hills – Tirumala; saviour of Prahlada – Ahobilam; Jyotirlinga – Srisailam.
[123:3:10] - Latest: 8 Jun 2026 – state launch of **Yogandhra-2026** at Lepakshi.
[123:3:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen previous papers p.10 ("A famous huge stone bull of the Vijayanagar period is located at Lepakshi"), p.15, p.36, p.40; Rocket AP History sheets #6, #24; app notes 1:123 (sub 4, 5)
## SUB 4 | Tadipatri and Other Andhra Temples
[123:4:0] - **Tadipatri (Anantapur):** art critics rate its **gopurams above those of Hampi's Vitthala temple** (APPSC G2 2019 ×3) – not Ahobilam, Srisailam, Lepakshi or Chandragiri.
[123:4:1] - **Chintala Venkataramana** (Vishnu) and **Bugga Ramalingeswara** (Shiva) temples = **Tadipatri** (APPSC G1 1990-91, 1994) – patrons the **Pemmasani Nayakas** (Pemmasani Timmanayudu); high-relief sculpture (**Ubattu Shilpalu**) and the painting of **Vatapatra Shayi**.
[123:4:2] TABLE head: Temple | Place / note
  [123:4:2.0] Kodandarama, Ontimitta (Vontimitta) | Kadapa; AP's official Sri Rama Navami temple after Bhadrachalam went to Telangana (2014)
  [123:4:2.1] Yaganti (Uma Maheswara) | Kurnool – now Nandyal district; Agastya, Venkateswara and Veera Brahmam caves; the "growing" Nandi
  [123:4:2.2] Ahobilam / Kadiri | Narasimha
  [123:4:2.3] Srikalahasti | Vayu linga; gali gopuram collapsed 2010
  [123:4:2.4] Srisailam | Mallikarjuna; four gateways; mukha mandapam – Harihara II; sculptured prakaram – Shanti Lingayya
  [123:4:2.5] Tirumala | Kalyana mandapam and bronze statues of the king with his queens – Krishnadevaraya; steps and Govindaraja temple – Anantaraju
[123:4:3] - **Ekambaranatha, Kanchipuram:** Pallava origin, but the great southern **Rajagopuram (1509)** is **Krishnadevaraya's** – the builder the APPSC question expects.
[123:4:4] - Latest (5 Mar 2026): Achyutaraya's **1534** inscriptions on a 50-ft pillar of the **Somapalayam Chennakesava** temple, Annamayya district.
[123:4:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen previous papers p.15, p.43 ("Chintala Venkata Ramana temple is located at Thadipatri"); Rocket AP History sheet #24; nandyal.ap.gov.in (district formed 4 Apr 2022); app notes 1:123 (sub 6, 7)
## SUB 5 | Forts, Cities and Later Capitals
[123:5:0] - **Gooty (Gutti) fort:** wall inscriptions from the **7th century** (APPSC FRO 2023 ×2); a **Bukka I** record calls it the foremost of forts; Aliya Rama Raya's base.
[123:5:1] - **Penukonda fort** = **Vijayanagara** kingdom; first **Aravidu capital (1570)** → **Chandragiri** (Venkatapati Raya II; Raja Mahal) → **Vellore (1600)**.
[123:5:2] - **Nagalapura (Nagalapuram)** = city founded by **Krishnadevaraya** for his mother Nagala Devi (UPPCS 2016) – not Warangal, Udayagiri or Chandragiri.
[123:5:3] - Udayagiri (Nellore) – Panchaloha cannon; Gandikota – idols looted by **Mir Jumla** (1657).
[123:5:4] ~~ Sources: anantapur.ap.gov.in (Gooty fort); NextGen Vijayanagara Kingdom p.5; app notes 1:123 (sub 8)

=== NOTES 1:124 | Folk Culture of Andhra - Burrakatha, Harikatha, Veedhi Natakam, Oggu Katha, Tolu Bommalata
## SUB 0 | Folk Entertainment under Vijayanagara – Yakshaganam and Tolu Bommalata
[124:0:0] TABLE head: Form | Audience under Vijayanagara
  [124:0:0.0] Yakshaganam | Originated in the royal courts; entertained the court and elites
  [124:0:0.1] Tolu Bommalata (leather shadow puppets) | The chief entertainment of rural Andhra besides Yakshagana (APPSC G2 2019 ×2) – not Harikatha, dramas or Burrakatha
  [124:0:0.2] Vipra-Vinodins | Brahmin jugglers for Brahmin households
[124:0:1] - **Yakshaganam** was performed by the **Jakkula (Jakkula Varu)** community; **Jakkula Purandhri** is a character of the **Yakshaganam** (APPSC G1 2004) – not Perini, Oggu Katha or puppetry.
[124:0:2] - **Koravanji** = precursor of the Telugu Yakshagana; **Sugreeva Vijayam** by **Kandukuri Rudrakavi** = first (published) Telugu Yakshaganam; performed in Telugu with rich costumes and Puranic stories.
[124:0:3] - **Veedhi Natakam / Veedhi Bhagavatam** (street dance-drama) → forerunner of **Kuchipudi**.
[124:0:4] - Under the **Qutb Shahis** Yakshaganam became folk theatre and Kuchipudi flourished; folk forms later carried Telugu consciousness to the villages in the **Andhra Movement**.
[124:0:5] ~~ Sources: Singhania Art & Culture 03 p.84 (Yakshagana – Vijayanagar courts, Jakkula Varu), p.100 (Tholu Bommalata); NextGen previous papers; app notes 1:124 (sub 0, 1), 1:123 (sub 9)
## SUB 1 | Burrakatha
[124:1:0] - **Earlier name: Jangam Katha** (APPSC JL; Singhania) – not Kuchipudi, Bhamakalapam or Veeranatyam; in Rayalaseema called **Thandana Katha**.
[124:1:1] - Folk narrative art of **Andhra Pradesh** (and Telangana); birthplace **Guntur**.
[124:1:2] - Troupe of **three**: the main narrator (with the **burra / tambura**) and **two co-performers (Vantalu)**; instruments Gummata, Burra, Tambura, Ukki; chorus "Thandana Taana".
[124:1:3] - **Made popular by Shaik Nazar** (APPSC ×2) = **Burrakatha Pitamaha** – born 5 Feb 1920, **Pannekallu, Guntur**; **Padma Shri 1986**; works Palnati Yuddham, **Bengal Karuvu** – not Mikkilineni or Mastan Saheb.
[124:1:4] - Popularisers: Nazar, **Nittala Brothers**; used for news, reform and nationalist messages; **Praja Natya Mandali** used it for socialist ideals (**Mabhoomi** – Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao); Sunkara's Burrakathas Kashtajeevi, Raithu Vijayam, Alluri Sitaramaraju.
[124:1:5] ~~ Sources: Singhania Art & Culture 03 p.58-59 ("Burrakatha or Jangam Katha ... from Andhra Pradesh"); PMF Art & Culture 02 p.102 (one leading performer and two co-performers); app notes 1:124 (sub 3, 7)
## SUB 2 | Harikatha
[124:2:0] - **Father of Harikatha (Harikatha Pitamaha):** **Adibhatla Narayana Dasu** (1864-1945) (APPSC G2 2012 ×2) – not Kanakaiah Naidu, Shankaramanchi Ramalingaiah or Ballari Raghava.
[124:2:1] - Born at **Ajjada**, Vizianagaram district; autobiography **Na Yeruka**; Harikatha is deeply rooted in **Vizianagaram**.
[124:2:2] - A **single artist** sings, acts and dances (about 3 hours) with cymbals (**Chidatalu**) – Burrakatha is a trio.
[124:2:3] ~~ Sources: PMF Art & Culture 02 p.102 (Harikatha – story of Hari); app notes 1:124 (sub 2)
## SUB 3 | Kuchipudi – Andhra's Classical Dance
[124:3:0] - **Kuchipudi** = the classical dance of **Andhra Pradesh** (APPSC ×3) – Kathakali and **Mohiniattam** are Kerala's, Kathak North India's, Bharatanatyam Tamil Nadu's, Odissi Odisha's.
[124:3:1] - Named after **Kuchipudi village, Krishna district**; founded by **Siddhendra Yogi**; grew from the **Bhagavata Mela** of hereditary Brahmin families; village gifted by **Abul Hasan Tana Shah**.
[124:3:2] - **Statements (APPSC FRO):** Kuchipudi from Krishna district ✓; Warangal Fort – **Kakatiyas** ✓; Telugu – classical Dravidian language ✓; "**Amaravati stupa – a centre of Jainism**" ✗ (it was **Buddhist**) → **a, c and d only**.
[124:3:3] ~~ Sources: PMF Art & Culture 02 p.73; NextGen AP History (Amaravati – Buddhist stupa); app notes 1:124 (sub 6)
## SUB 4 | Tolu Bommalata – the Craft, Nimmalakunta and Surabhi
[124:4:0] - Thin, **translucent leather** figures **painted on both sides**, moved behind a **white screen** lit by a lamp; **heads of the puppets move** (unique feature); Ramayana, Mahabharata, Puranas.
[124:4:1] - **Nimmalakunta** (Sri Sathya Sai / Anantapur) – leather puppetry **GI tag 2008**; **Dalavai Chalapathi Rao** – Padma Shri 2020.
[124:4:2] - Mentioned in **Panditaradhya Charitra** (Palkuriki Somanatha), **Palnati Veeracharitra** (Srinatha), Bhaskara Satakam.
[124:4:3] - **Surabhi theatre:** **Vanarasa Govinda Rao**, from a **leather-puppet family**, replaced puppets with live actors (**Keechaka Vadham**) at **Sorugu** near Jammalamadugu (Kadapa).
[124:4:4] ~~ Sources: Singhania Art & Culture 03 p.100; app notes 1:124 (sub 4)
## SUB 5 | Oggu Katha and Community Kathas
[124:5:0] TABLE head: Form | Community | Note

[125:0:0] TABLE head: Craft | Place | Exam fact
  [125:0:0.0] Hand-knotted carpets | Eluru | Designs Farishkhani and Ashunkhani – main attraction at the London Exhibition, 1851 (APPSC 2022) – not curtains, blankets or bed sheets
  [125:0:0.1] Wooden cutlery | Udayagiri (Nellore) | GI registered 27 April 2017
  [125:0:0.2] Crochet lace | Narasapur | APPSC match: carpets–Eluru, cutlery–Udayagiri, crochet–Narasapur, lacquerware–Etikoppaka (1-2-3-4)
  [125:0:0.3] Lacquerware toys | Etikoppaka (Anakapalli district) | GI; a wooden craft (APPSC G2, 2018 Mains) – not stone carving, painting or handloom
  [125:0:0.4] Kondapalli toys | Kondapalli, NTR district | Made of wood – the light Tella Poniki
  [125:0:0.5] Kalamkari | Srikalahasti (pen / freehand); Machilipatnam-Pedana (block-printed) | "Hand-painted cotton textile of South India" (IAS 2015) – not bamboo, woollen or silk; main problem of the artisans = about 2 months per piece with poor returns (APPSC Panchayat Secretary)
  [125:0:0.6] Bobbili Veena (Saraswati Veena) | Bobbili, Vizianagaram | Carved from jackfruit wood (SSC 2019); GI
  [125:0:0.7] Budithi bell and brass | Budithi, Srikakulam | GI 2008; temple bells, Bindelu vessels
  [125:0:0.8] Dharmavaram sarees | Sri Sathya Sai district | GI

[125:0:2] - **Lepakshi** = brand of the **A.P. Handicrafts Development Corporation (APHDC)**, the state nodal agency.

## SUB 1 | Classical Dances – Kuchipudi and the Eight Forms
[125:1:0] - **Kuchipudi** = classical dance of **Andhra Pradesh** (MPPCS 1995; UKPCS 2002) – named after **Kuchipudi (Kuchelapuram) village, Krishna district**; shaped by **Siddhendra Yogi**; **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** (last Qutb Shahi) gifted the village to the performers; popular shows Bhama Kalapam, Usha Parinayam.
[125:1:1] - **Kuchipudi vs Bharatanatyam (IAS 2012):** dancers **speak dialogue** in Kuchipudi ✓; **Tarangam** – dancing on the **rim of a brass plate** – is a **Kuchipudi** feature, not Bharatanatyam ✗ → **only 1**.
[125:1:2] - Kuchipudi = **dance-drama** tradition (Bhagavata Mela, male Brahmin troupes); Bharatanatyam = solo temple-dance tradition; **Lakumadevi**, court dancer of **Kumaragiri Reddy**, was famed for Bharatanatyam.
[125:1:3] - **Solo dance (IAS 1997):** **Mohiniyattam** (Kerala; women) – Kuchipudi, Bharatanatyam and Odissi are also staged by groups.
[125:1:4] TABLE head: Classical dance | State
  [125:1:4.0] Bharatanatyam | Tamil Nadu
  [125:1:4.1] Kuchipudi | Andhra Pradesh
  [125:1:4.2] Kathak | Uttar Pradesh
  [125:1:4.3] Mohiniyattam | Kerala
  [125:1:4.4] Sattriya | Assam – introduced in the 15th century by the Vaishnava saint Sankaradeva (not Bihu, Jhumar or Bagurumba)
  [125:1:4.5] Odissi | Odisha
  [125:1:4.6] Kathakali | Kerala
  [125:1:4.7] Manipuri | Manipur
[125:1:5] - **Matches asked (UPRO 2013, 2023):** Bharatanatyam–TN, Kathak–UP, Kuchipudi–AP, Mohiniyattam–Kerala (**1-4-3-2**); Bharatanatyam–TN, Kuchipudi–AP, Sattriya–Assam, Kathak–UP (**A-1, B-3, C-4, D-2**).
[125:1:6] - **Sonal Mansingh** – **Odissi** (also Bharatanatyam); **Padma Bhushan 1992**, Padma Vibhushan 2003 – not Birju Maharaj (Kathak), Mallika Sarabhai or Yamini Krishnamurthy.
[125:1:7] - **Uday Shankar** – blended Indian classical dance with **Western ballet / European theatre** – pioneer of modern Indian dance.
[125:1:8] - **Kuravanji** – a **group dance-drama by women** on a girl's love for her beloved (Tamil; Telugu **Koravanji** = earliest type of Yakshaganam); **Rukmini Devi Arundale** staged Kuravanji (Kutrala Kuravanji) at **Kalakshetra**. APPSC asked "a famous Kuravanji performer" twice: one key **Rukmini Arundale**, the G2 2019 key **Jakka Radhika** (no source names her).
[125:1:9] ~~ Sources: PMF Art & Culture 02 p.44-70 (classical dances; Tarangam p.64; Sattriya p.70; Sonal Mansingh p.59), p.87 (Uday Shankar); NextGen Qutb Shahis p.18 (Kuchipudi, Koravanji); Telangana SCERT Social Studies VII ch.21 (Kuravanji); app notes 1:125 (sub 2, 3)
## SUB 2 | Fairs, Jataras and Temple Towns
[125:2:0] - **Kumbh Mela 2019** (Ardh Kumbh, 15 Jan–4 Mar 2019) = **Prayagraj** (Triveni Sangam) – the first after Allahabad was renamed (2018).
[125:2:1] - **Nasik** Kumbh = on the **Godavari** (UPPSC 2004) – not Tapti, Narmada or Koyna; the four Kumbh sites: Prayagraj (Ganga–Yamuna), Haridwar (Ganga), Ujjain (Shipra), Nasik (Godavari).
[125:2:2] - **Medaram Jathara (Sammakka–Saralamma)** – "largest tribal festival" (APPSC ATWO, undivided AP); Koya tribe; biennial; **Mulugu district, Telangana** since 2014 – "Asia's largest tribal congregation".
[125:2:3] - **Kurnool tourist pair:** **Mantralayam** (Raghavendra Swamy) and **Mahanandi** (Shiva; now Nandyal district) – Lepakshi is Sri Sathya Sai, Ramatheertham Vizianagaram, Mukhalingam/Srikurmam Srikakulam, Antarvedi Konaseema.

## SUB 5 | Festivals of Andhra Pradesh
[125:5:0] - **Ugadi** = **Telugu New Year** (Chaitra), in AP, Karnataka and Telangana (APPSC JL) – not Dasara, Sankranti or "Panduga".
[125:5:1] - **Sankranti** (January harvest): Bhogi → Sankranti → **Kanuma** (day of **thanksgiving to cattle and birds**, APPSC Endowment 2022); Gangireddulaata, **Kolla Pandalu** (cockfights), Pottella Pandalu (ram fights).
[125:5:2] - **Vinayaka Chavithi** – Vinayaka is worshipped with **21 kinds of leaves** (Ekavimsati Patra Puja) (APPSC Endowment 2022).
[125:5:3] - **Vasantotsavam** (spring festival) – **most popular festival under the Reddi kings** (APPSC G2 2019; AP History PYQ) – not Sankranti, Dussehra or Deepavali; **Kumaragiri Reddy** styled himself **Karpura Vasantarayalu**; merchant **Avachi Tippayashetti** headed the **Sugandhabhandagara** (perfume store) that supplied it.
[125:5:4] - **Atla Taddi** – women's festival of **Ashwayuja** (not Chaitra).
[125:5:5] - **Bathukamma, Bonalu** = Telangana identity festivals.
[125:5:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History - APPSC 12 p.10-14 (Vasantotsavam, Karpura Vasanta Rayalu); NextGen AP History - APPSC 08 p.24; PMF Art & Culture 06 p.10, p.21 (Ugadi); app notes 1:125 (sub 4)

## SUB 7 | Folk Arts, Songs and Sports of Andhra
[125:7:0] - **Folk arts (Janapada Kalalu)** = arts of the **Janapadam** (village); **Biruduraju Ramaraju** wrote the **first book on the theory of folk knowledge** in Telugu; **World Folk Day: 22 August**; **Gathasaptasati** records **couple and choir dances** of rural folk.
[125:7:1] - **Folk songs:** **Jola patalu** = lullabies; **Kolatam kirtanas** (for the stick dance) – **Annamacharya**; Sankranti songs and Gangireddulaata – January harvest.
[125:7:2] - **Traditional sports and what they taught (Sachivalayam):** **Kothikommachi** (tree climbing) – **co-habitation with nature**; **Kabaddi** – **physical fitness and fighting capacity**; **Pulijoodam** (tiger-and-goats board game) – **logical and analytical skills**; **Vaikunthapali** (snakes and ladders) – **the course of life** → **A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1**.

=== NOTES 1:126 | Battle of Talikota (1565), the Aravidu Dynasty and the Legacy of Vijayanagara
## SUB 0 | Battle of Talikota (1565) – Rakshasa Tangadi
[126:0:0] - **Date:** **23 January 1565** (some books 26 January) – year **1565** (APPSC FRO 2022, 2023; JL 2004; UPPCS 1993; MPPCS 1997) – not 1526 (Panipat I), 1545, 1555, 1560, 1564 or 1576.
[126:0:1] - **Names:** **Talikota / Tallikota** (Sewell, *A Forgotten Empire*); **Rakshasa-Tangadi / Rakshasi-Tangadi** (NextGen: Nilakanta Sastri; app notes: Fr. Heras); **Bannihatti** (H.K. Sherwani); fought near Tallikota between the **Krishna** and its tributary.
[126:0:2] - **King:** **Sadasiva Raya** (nominal, last Tuluva) – real power with regent **Aliya Rama Raya**, **son-in-law of Krishnadevaraya** (APPSC JL 2006) – not Achyuta Raya, Tirumala Raya or Venkata.
[126:0:3] - **Rama Raya's policy:** the "adventurous ruler" who **played one Sultan against another** until they united (APPSC 2019 Social & Cultural History) – not Krishnadevaraya, Harihara I/II.
[126:0:4] TABLE head: Sultanate | Ruler at Talikota
  [126:0:4.0] Bijapur (Adil Shahi) | Ali Adil Shah
  [126:0:4.1] Ahmadnagar (Nizam Shahi) | Hussain Nizam Shah – beheaded Rama Raya
  [126:0:4.2] Golconda (Qutb Shahi) | Ibrahim Qutb Shah (key organiser)
  [126:0:4.3] Bidar (Barid Shahi) | Ali Barid Shah
[126:0:5] - **Berar (Imad Shahi)** stayed out → enemy = **the Deccan Sultanates / combined forces of Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Golconda** (APPSC G1; UPPSC 2014) – **not the Bahmani kingdom** (already broken up), the Mughals or the Marathas.
[126:0:6] - **"Who fought Rakshasi-Tangadi?" (APPSC G1):** **the Adil Shahis of Bijapur and Ramaraya** (Rocket Sheet wording) – Berar's Imad Shahis stayed out; Veeranarasimha is a Tuluva of 1505; "Ramaraya and Nizam Shah" names only the sultan who killed him.
[126:0:7] - **Causes:** 1546-47 Rama Raya backed Ahmadnagar against Bijapur and Bidar and took the **Raichur doab**; 1557-63 backed Bijapur and razed Ahmadnagar; sheltered **Jagadeva Rao**, a rebel of Golconda; marriage links – **Chand Bibi–Ali Adil Shah**, Bibi Jamal–Ibrahim Qutb Shah.
[126:0:8] - **Results:** Hampi **looted for about six months**; **Sewell** called it a "graveyard" (possibly exaggerated); Sadasiva and **Tirumala** fled to **Penukonda**; the empire's centre moved to the **Telugu country**; Nayakas grew autonomous.
[126:0:9] ~~ Sources: NextGen Vijayanagara Kingdom p.5 (Tallikota/Rakshasatangadi/Bannihatti; Hussain Nizam Shah; Penukonda); NextGen AP Rocket Sheet #12 p.17 (Tallikota – between Adil Shahis of Bijapur and Ramaraya); PMF Ancient & Medieval 04 p.71 (combined forces of Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golkonda and Bidar); app notes 1:126 (sub 0)
## SUB 1 | Aravidu Dynasty (1570-1646/80) – Penukonda, Chandragiri, Vellore
[126:1:0] - **Fourth** Vijayanagara dynasty; named after **Araviti (Aravidu)** village, **Kurnool** district.
[126:1:1] - **Capital after 1565 / of the Aravidus:** **Penukonda (Penugonda)** (APPSC G1 1991; G2 2000; AP History PYQ ×3) – not Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmadnagar, Kampili, Kondavidu, Addanki, Vizianagaram, Anantapur or Chandragiri.
[126:1:2] - **Capital shifts:** Hampi → **Penukonda** (1570, Tirumala) → **Chandragiri** (Venkatapati II) → **Vellore** (c. 1600).
[126:1:3] TABLE head: Ruler | Key fact
  [126:1:3.0] Tirumala Raya (1570-72) | Founder, Rama Raya's brother; removed Sadasiva; crowned at Penukonda
  [126:1:3.1] Sriranga I (1572-85) | Lost Kondaveedu to Ibrahim Qutb Shah
  [126:1:3.2] Venkatapati Raya II (1585-1614) | Greatest and longest; "Second Krishnadevaraya", "Second Andhra Bhoja"; moved to Chandragiri; literary contests at Venkatapati Vilasam; Vilapakam (1601) and Siddhavatam (1605) inscriptions; Dutch at Pulicat; court scholar Appayya Dikshita
  [126:1:3.3] Sriranga II (1614) | Killed by Jagga Raya
  [126:1:3.4] Ramadeva (1616-30) | Battle of Toppur (1616) – "second Talikota", won by Velugoti Yachama Nayaka and Raghunatha of Tanjore
  [126:1:3.5] Venkatapati III (1630-43) | Madras granted to Francis Day (1639) by Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka (Srikalahasti)
  [126:1:3.6] Sriranga III (1643-) | Last; defeated by Bijapur and Golconda (Vandavasi; Mir Jumla)
[126:1:4] - **Jesuits:** **Venkatapati Raya II** allowed Jesuit churches at **Nellore and Chandragiri** (APPSC G1 2023; G1 PYQ) – not Krishnadevaraya, Achyuta Raya, Sadasiva, Devaraya II or Tirumala.
[126:1:5] - **Mysore:** **Raja Wodeyar** took **Srirangapatna (1610)** and founded the Mysore kingdom under **Venkata II** (IAS 2006 ×2) – not Sadasiva, Tirumala or Ranga II.
[126:1:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen Vijayanagara Kingdom p.5-6 (Tirumalaraya at Penukonda; Venkatapatiraya II – Chandragiri; Venkatapatiraya III – Madras); NextGen previous papers p.40 (capital of Vijayanagara after the Tallikota battle – Penugonda); NextGen AP Rocket Sheets (src/ap-history/rocket-ap-history.txt); app notes 1:126 (sub 1, 2, 3)
## SUB 2 | Nayaka Kingdoms, Kshetrayya and Court Literature
[126:2:0] TABLE head: Kingdom | Founder | Fact
  [126:2:0.0] Madurai | Vishwanatha Nayaka (after capturing his rebel father Nagama) | Krishnappa made it independent c. 1565; Tirumala Nayaka (1623-59) built the Tirumala Rayala Mahal
  [126:2:0.1] Tanjore | Sevappa Nayaka (under Achyutaraya) | Raghunatha; last king Vijayaraghava Nayaka
  [126:2:0.2] Gingee | Krishnappa Nayaka | –
  [126:2:0.3] Ikkeri (Keladi) | Chowdappa Nayaka | –
  [126:2:0.4] Mysore | Raja Wodeyar (1610) | under Venkata II
[126:2:1] - **Kshetrayya** (original name Varadayya; "Pada Kavita Pitamaha"): born at **Movva (Muvva), Krishna district**; padams with the mudra **Muvva Gopala**; sang for **Tirumala Nayaka of Madurai**, **Vijayaraghava Nayaka of Tanjore** and **Abdullah Qutb Shah of Golconda** (1500 padams dedicated to him) → **"All the above"** (APPSC G1 2003).
[126:2:2] - **Govinda Dikshita** – minister of the **Tanjore Nayaks** (Achyutappa, Raghunatha); wrote ***Sahitya Sudha*** – not Ayyappa Dikshita, Vedanta Desika or Vyasaraya.
[126:2:3] - **Appayya Dikshita** – *Shaivarka Mani Dipika*; **Ramaraja Bhushanudu** – *Vasucharitra*.
[126:2:4] - **Amara-nayakas** → hereditary **Palegars** → forerunners of zamindars (Kalahasti, Chittoor); **Mir Jumla** melted temple idols into cannon at **Gandikota (1657)**; Raya gopurams and kalyana mandapas spread through the Nayaka courts.
[126:2:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen Qutb Shahis p.8 (Kshetrayya – Mowva; 1500 poems to Abdullah Qutub Shah); NextGen AP History - APPSC 15 p.16 (same); app notes 1:126 (sub 4, 5)
## SUB 3 | Rediscovery of Hampi
[126:3:0] - **Colin Mackenzie** – surveyed and mapped the ruins of **Hampi in 1800**; later the **first Surveyor General of India** (NDA 2019; APPSC 2019) – not James Prinsep (Brahmi), James Rennell, Charles Metcalfe, Charles Harvey or Lord Hastings.
[126:3:1] - **Caesar Frederick** (Venetian) saw the ruined city in **1567**; **Robert Sewell** – *A Forgotten Empire* (1900).
[126:3:2] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval 04 p.66 (Colin Mackenzie); NextGen AP History - APPSC 02 p.10 (Mackenzie, first Surveyor General); app notes 1:126 (sub 5)

=== NOTES 1:127 | Mughal Empire – Babur: Panipat, Khanwa, Chanderi, Ghaghra; Tuzuk-i-baburi
## SUB 0 | Babur's Battles – Panipat I, Khanwa, Chanderi, Ghaghra
[127:0:0] TABLE head: Battle | Year | Opponent | Result
  [127:0:0.0] Panipat I | 21 April 1526 | Ibrahim Lodi (last Delhi Sultan) | Lodis shattered; Delhi and Agra + Lodi treasure
  [127:0:0.1] Khanwa | 16 March 1527 | Rana Sanga of Mewar + Mahmud Lodi + Hasan Khan Mewati | Rajput power broken; title Ghazi
  [127:0:0.2] Chanderi | 1528 | Medini Rai (Malwa, ally of Sanga) | Malwa secured; Jauhar
  [127:0:0.3] Ghaghra | 1529 | Afghans of Mahmud Lodi + Nusrat Shah of Bengal | Suzerainty over Bihar
  [127:0:0.4] Chausa | 1539 | Humayun vs Sher Shah | Sher Shah
  [127:0:0.5] Kannauj (Bilgram) | 1540 | Humayun vs Sher Shah | Sher Shah
  [127:0:0.6] Panipat II | 1556 | Akbar (Bairam Khan) vs Hemu | Akbar
  [127:0:0.7] Samugarh | 1658 | Aurangzeb vs Dara | Aurangzeb
  [127:0:0.8] Haldighati | 1576 | Akbar (Man Singh) vs Maharana Pratap | Akbar
[127:0:1] - **Chronology:** Panipat I → Khanwa → Chanderi → Ghaghra (**II, IV, III, I** – UKPCS 2024); Khanwa → Ghaghra → Chausa → Samugarh (**II, I, III, IV** – CGPSC 2008).
[127:0:2] - **Wrong pair:** "Second Battle of Panipat – Tipu Sultan and Marathas" ✗ (it was **Akbar vs Hemu**, 1556; Third Panipat 1761 = Abdali vs Marathas).
[127:0:3] - **Khanwa:** **Rana Sanga** was defeated (UPPCS 2004; Uttarakhand 2010; UDA 2010) – not Rana Pratap, Man Singh, Hemu or Uday Singh; Babur declared **jihad** here (UPPCS 2009), **renounced wine**, remitted the **tamgha** for Muslims, took the title **Ghazi**; trenches and barricades against Sanga's elephants.
[127:0:4] - **Khanwa more decisive than Panipat (UPSC 2001 ×2):** A ✓, R ✓ and **R explains A** – Rana Sanga was a more formidable foe than Ibrahim Lodi; Khanwa "broke the back of Rajput power" and **set up Mughal rule on the path of expansion** – the "real beginning" of the empire (APPSC G1 2008 key: **Kanwah**) – Panipat gave only Delhi and Agra.
[127:0:5] - **Why Babur won:** a **skilled combination of artillery and cavalry** (APPSC HWO) – **tulughma** (Uzbek flanking) + **araba / Rumi** carts shielding the guns; artillery under **Ustad Ali and Mustafa**; Babur's army ~**12,000** vs Ibrahim's ~1,00,000; **no war elephants** on Babur's side.
[127:0:6] - **Panipat I** = first large-scale use of **field artillery** in North India; but **firearms were not new** – the **Bahmanis and Vijayanagara** had used them earlier.
[127:0:7] - **Babur's arrival (UPSC 2015):** gunpowder ✗ (known before), arch and dome ✗ (Sultanate), **Timurid dynasty** ✓ → **3 only**; the State PSC variant with "introduction of **cannons** in warfare" keys **3 and 4**.
[127:0:8] - Invited by **Daulat Khan Lodi** (governor of Punjab), **Alam Khan** (Ibrahim's uncle) and **Rana Sanga**; nickname **Qalandar** for sharing the Lodi treasure.
[127:0:9] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian History - APPSC 04 p.20 (Panipat 1526; Kanwah 1527 "broke the back of the powerful Rajput power and helped Babur consolidate his rule"; Chanderi 1528; Ghaghra); PMF Ancient & Medieval 04 p.82-85 (Panipat 21 April 1526; artillery and cavalry; Bahmanis and Vijayanagara used firearms earlier; Khanwa jihad, Ghazi; Ghagra – Nusrat Shah); app notes 1:127 (sub 1-4)
## SUB 1 | Babur – Origin, Name and Titles
[127:1:0] - **Name:** **Zahir-ud-din Muhammad** (APPSC G1); "**Babur**" = **tiger** – he took the name Babur (CGPSC 2003); not Abdul Raheem, Umar Sheikh (his father) or Daulat Khan.
[127:1:1] - **Born 14 Feb 1483** at **Farghana (Ferghana)**, Central Asia (CDS 2001) – not Khiva, Khorasan or Seistan; ruler of Farghana at 12 (1494).
[127:1:2] - **Descent:** **Timur** (father's side) and **Chingiz Khan** (mother's side).
[127:1:3] - **Mughals were Turks** – **Chagatai Turks**, named after **Chagatai, second son of Chingiz Khan** (APPSC G1 2002; UDA 2010) – not Mongols, Afghans, Persians or Arabs; they called themselves **Timurids**.
[127:1:4] - **Title Padshah:** first adopted at **Kabul** (taken **1504**; title in 1507), dropping the ancestral "Mirza" (UPPCS 2015) – not Ferghana, Delhi or Samarkand (held only 8 months, 1501).
[127:1:5] - **Founder of Mughal rule in India:** **Babur** (1526) (SSC 2017).
[127:1:6] - **Contemporaries:** **Krishnadevaraya** of Vijayanagara (praised by Babur as the most powerful ruler in India), Sultan Quli of Golconda, Rana Sanga; the Mughals **did not interfere in the Deccan** in Babur's time.
[127:1:7] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval 04 p.80 (Zahiruddin Muhammad; Chagatai Turks), p.82 (Farghana 1494, Kabul 1504); NextGen Indian History - APPSC 04 p.20 (born in Farghana); app notes 1:127 (sub 0)
## SUB 2 | Babur's Empire, Coins and Buildings
[127:2:0] - **Empire at his death:** **Kabul**, **Punjab** and modern **Uttar Pradesh** (Delhi, Agra, up to Bihar's border) – **not modern Rajasthan** or Bengal → **I, II and III** (UKPSC 2003 ×2); **Badakhshan** given to **Humayun**; ruled through **jagirs** and **paraganas**; no administrative system (Mansabdari = **Akbar**).
[127:2:1] - **Death:** **Agra, December 1530**; first buried at Agra, later moved to **Bagh-e-Babur, Kabul** (SSC 2009) – Kabul is the trap.
[127:2:2] - **Coin:** silver **Shahrukhi** (Timurid style) – Babur (UPRO 2017); also copper coins.
[127:2:3] - **Babri Masjid, Ayodhya (1528)** – built by **Mir Baqi**, Babur's commander (UPPSC 1992) – not Babur himself.
[127:2:4] - **Buildings and gardens:** **Kabuli Bagh mosque** (Panipat), Sambhal mosque; **charbagh** gardens – **Ram Bagh (Aram Bagh), Agra** = first Mughal garden.
[127:2:5] ~~ Sources: PMF Ancient & Medieval 04 p.84 (died in Agra 1530, Bagh-e Babur; charbagh; Kabuli Bagh), p.85 (Babri Masjid – Mir Baqi); app notes 1:127 (sub 5, 7)
## SUB 3 | Tuzuk-i-Baburi (Baburnama)
[127:3:0] - Babur's memoirs, written in **Turki (Chagatai Turkish)** (State PSC) – not Persian, Arabic or Urdu.
[127:3:1] - **A–R (IAS 1993):** "Babur wrote his memoirs in Turki" ✓; "Turki was the official language of the Mughal court" ✗ – the court language was **Persian** → **A true, R false**.
[127:3:2] - **Translations:** Persian (1589) under Akbar by **Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan**; English first by **Leyden and Erskine** (1826; "Leyden and Ruskin" in the UPRO 2017 options), later **Annette Beveridge** (from the Turki).
[127:3:3] - **India in the Baburnama:** **five Muslim and two Hindu** powers – the Hindu ones **Vijayanagara and Mewar** (UPPCS 1995) – not Orissa, Gujarat or Kashmir.
[127:3:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian History - APPSC 04 p.20 ("Tuzuk-i-Baburi" in Turkish), APPSC 05 p.14 (Baburnama in Turkish); PMF Ancient & Medieval 04 p.84-85; app notes 1:127 (sub 6)
