## SUB 4 | Zamindaris and the Battles – Bobbili, Padmanabham
[168:4:0] TABLE head: Zamindari | Family
  [168:4:0.0] Vizianagaram | Pusapati (Kshatriya Raju) – Gajapati Vijayarama(raju) belonged to it
  [168:4:0.1] Bobbili | Velama
  [168:4:0.2] Venkatagiri | Velugoti (Velama)
  [168:4:0.3] Peddapuram | Vatsavayi (Vatsavai) dynasty
[168:4:1] - Hereditary zamindari families of the Circars: **Velamas, Reddis, Kshatriya Rajus**.
[168:4:2] - **Bobbili (24 Jan 1757):** Vijayaramaraju of Vizianagaram + the French under **Bussy** destroyed Bobbili; **Ranga Rao** died; **Tandra Papayya** killed Vijayaramaraju.
[168:4:3] - **Padmanabham (10 July 1794, asked ×2):** Vizianagaram sequestered (1793); **Chinna Vijayaramaraju** defeated and killed by the Company; son **Narayana Babu** made zamindar; **George Russell** took charge of the forts. (NextGen L2 p.14 misprints "1749".)
[168:4:4] - **Banaganapalle** – a princely state (samsthanam, Nawab's) under the Madras Presidency; Bellary, Chittoor, Madanapalle were districts/towns.
[168:4:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen modern India L2 Part 1 (src/ap-history/nextgen-modern-l2-01.txt) p.13-14; NextGen modern India L3 Part 1 (src/ap-history/nextgen-modern-l3-01.txt) p.23-25; NextGen previous papers (src/ap-history/nextgen-previous-papers.txt) p.21; old app notes row 168 (sub 4); Peddapuram and Banaganapalle: general knowledge, not checked
## SUB 5 | Thomas Munro and the Company's Officials
[168:5:0] - **Three officials revered in Andhra:** **Sir Thomas Munro, Sir Arthur Cotton and Charles Phillip Brown**.
[168:5:1] - **Munro (1761-1827):** with **Read** in the **Baramahal (1792)** – first Ryotwari; **first Principal Collector of the Ceded Districts (1800-07)**; **suppressed the palegars** (80 resisted, 18 months; with Gen. Campbell) and ended auctions; survey **1802-07**, Ryotwari (1802); spoke Telugu, needed no dubashis; President, **Judicial Commission 1814** (report April 1816); **Governor of Madras 1820-27**; died of cholera at **Pattikonda** (Kurnool), **6 July 1827**; "Mandava Rishi".
[168:5:2] - Others: **C.P. Brown** – Kadapa Collector, Vemana, Telugu-English dictionary; **Cotton** – Dowleswaram; **Charles Orr** – Krishna anicut; **Veenam Veeranna** – Cotton's assistant; **G.N. Taylor** – Anglo-vernacular schools.
[168:5:3] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 21 (src/ap-history/ap-history-appsc-21.txt) p.7-9; NextGen modern India L2 Part 1 (src/ap-history/nextgen-modern-l2-01.txt) p.18-19; NextGen modern India L3 Part 1 (src/ap-history/nextgen-modern-l3-01.txt) p.25, p.33
## SUB 6 | Judiciary, Police and Later Links
[168:6:0] TABLE head: Level | Court
  [168:6:0.0] Taluk | Munsiff court
  [168:6:0.1] District | Zilla court under a District Judge (Cornwallis Code, 1793)
  [168:6:0.2] Apex (natives) | Sadar Adalat; Sadar Faujdari Adalat (criminal), Madras
  [168:6:0.3] British subjects | Madras Supreme Court (1801); Madras High Court 1862
[168:6:1] - **Munro's Judicial Commission (1814; report April 1816):** Madras Regulations of 1816 – **Munsiff and Panchayat courts** as courts of first instance; **police supervision from judges to Collectors**; Collectors lost **judicial** powers in 1816.
[168:6:2] - **Police:** Cornwallis's **thanas under darogas**; Madras District Police Act **1859**; CPC **1859**, IPC **1860**, CrPC **1861**.
[168:6:3] - Criticism: slow, costly British procedure → more litigation and debt; judges drawn from the revenue service.
[168:6:4] - **Links (2026):** Rayalaseema sericulture traced to British promotion in the Ceded Districts – silk hubs **Dharmavaram, Madanapalle** (20 Feb 2026); Supreme Court notice (1 May 2026) on a plea under **Article 14** for a separate revenue judicial service; the Circars-Ceded gap later shaped the **Sri Bagh Pact**.
[168:6:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen modern India L3 Part 1 (src/ap-history/nextgen-modern-l3-01.txt) p.33, p.47; NextGen modern India L2 Part 1 (src/ap-history/nextgen-modern-l2-01.txt) p.16-17; old app notes row 168 (sub 9)

=== NOTES 1:169 | Establishment of British Rule in Andhra – Administrative Consolidation and Its Effects
## SUB 0 | Anicuts and Irrigation – Cotton, Veeranna, Orr and Ramapada Sagar
[169:0:0] # Dowleswaram (Godavari) anicut
[169:0:1] - 1. **Guntur famine (1832-33)** – the trigger (about 40% of Guntur's people died).
[169:0:2] - 2. **1844:** Cotton's report to the Board of Revenue for an anicut near Rajahmundry.
[169:0:3] - 3. Sanctioned late **1846**; begun **1847**; **completed April 1852** at about **Rs 1.5 lakh** (NextGen L3 p.49 says 1849 – the standard year is **1852**).
[169:0:4] - **Veenam Veeranna** – the **Andhra (Indian) official** who managed the labour; made **Rao Bahadur** and Assistant Engineer; name on the anicut wall.
[169:0:5] TABLE head: Anicut | River | Engineer | Years
  [169:0:5.0] Dowleswaram | Godavari | Sir Arthur Cotton, assisted by Veenam Veeranna | 1847-1852
  [169:0:5.1] Krishna anicut, Bezwada (now Prakasam Barrage) | Krishna | proposed by Col. Henry Atlock (Lake); executed by Captain (Charles) Orr on Cotton's plan | 1850-1855
  [169:0:5.2] Sangam anicut | Penna (Nellore) | – | 1882-86
[169:0:6] - **Captain Orr** = the **English officer** who assisted Cotton (Krishna anicut); Captain Nolt defeated Narasimha Reddy – a distractor.
[169:0:7] - **Cotton (1803-1899):** "**pioneer of irrigation in South India**"; knighted **1861**; "Apara Bhagiratha", "Cotton Dora"; on his suggestion Rajahmundry → **Godavari** and Machilipatnam → **Krishna** districts (1859); today's **Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage** replaced the old anicut.
[169:0:8] - **Ramapada Sagar(am) at Polavaram:** the "dream-child" of **S.V. (Sonti Venkata) Ramamurthi, ICS**, who named it after the backwaters reaching Lord Rama's feet at Bhadrachalam (1941-42; first survey by **L. Venkatakrishna Iyer**) = forerunner of the **Polavaram** project (APPSC G2 Prelims 2019). Not Cotton or K.L. Rao.
[169:0:9] - **Godavari and Krishna deltas** = the "**Rice Bowl of Andhra**". **Feb 2026:** crest-gate telemetry and SCADA installed at the **Prakasam Barrage**.
[169:0:10] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 21 (src/ap-history/ap-history-appsc-21.txt) p.9-10, p.16; NextGen modern India L2 Part 1 (src/ap-history/nextgen-modern-l2-01.txt) p.19; NextGen modern India L3 Part 1 (src/ap-history/nextgen-modern-l3-01.txt) p.25, p.49; https://sakti.in/classic/godavaribasin/indira-klrao.htm; old app notes row 169 (sub 2)
## SUB 1 | British Officers, Education and Telugu Journals
[169:1:0] TABLE head: Person | Contribution
  [169:1:0.0] G.N. (George Noble) Taylor | Sub-Collector of Rajahmundry; opened Anglo-vernacular schools at several places in Andhra; founded a school at Narsapur (1852), later Taylor High School
  [169:1:0.1] C.P. Brown (1798-1884) | Kadapa Collector; Vemana's verses, Telugu-English dictionary; editor, Madras Literary Journal
  [169:1:0.2] Colin Mackenzie | first Surveyor General (1815); Amaravati Stupa (1797); manuscripts
  [169:1:0.3] Thomas Munro | Ryotwari
  [169:1:0.4] M.G. Ranade | called Veeresalingam the "Vidyasagar of South India"
[169:1:1] - **Taylor (asked ×4):** Rajahmundry Sub-Collector → Anglo-vernacular schools (G2 Mains 2017, G2, AP History PYQ); his private school = **Narsapur**. Rev. Noble = Machilipatnam school (1843).
[169:1:2] - **The three revered officials:** **Munro, Arthur Cotton, C.P. Brown** (AMVI 2013).
[169:1:3] - **Telugu journals:** **Hitavadi (1862)** – first Telugu literary journal, Rev. J.E. Sharkey; Krishna Patrika, Andhra Patrika later criticised British rule ("pernicious"); hostile after **1906**.
[169:1:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen previous papers (src/ap-history/nextgen-previous-papers.txt) p.10; NextGen AP History Part 21 (src/ap-history/ap-history-appsc-21.txt) p.7; NextGen modern India L2 Part 1 (src/ap-history/nextgen-modern-l2-01.txt) p.17-19; https://taylorhighschoolnarsapur.in (web search); old app notes row 169 (sub 3, 7)
## SUB 2 | Railways and Communications
[169:2:0] - **First railway line in Andhra:** **Puttur–Renigunta**, opened **15 September 1862** (Madras Railway) – asked ×4; later Gooty–Renigunta.
[169:2:1] - Railways linked the interior with the **Madras port**; built mainly for military and commercial needs.
[169:2:2] - **Buckingham Canal:** salt-water canal through **Pulicat Lake**; extended as famine relief in **1876-78**; now part of **NW-4**.
[169:2:3] - **Fort St. George** was built at **Madrasapatnam** (1639-40).
[169:2:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen modern India L2 Part 1 (src/ap-history/nextgen-modern-l2-01.txt) p.11, p.18; NextGen AP History Part 21 (src/ap-history/ap-history-appsc-21.txt) p.17; old app notes row 169 (sub 4)
## SUB 3 | District Reorganisation and the Collector
[169:3:0] TABLE head: Year | Change
  [169:3:0.0] 1802 | Rajahmundry + Kakinada collectorates → Rajahmundry district
  [169:3:0.1] 1819 | Ganjam Collector made Agent to the Governor for the Agency tracts
  [169:3:0.2] 1859 | Rajahmundry → Godavari, Machilipatnam → Krishna districts
  [169:3:0.3] 1904 / 1925 | Guntur and East Godavari / West Godavari
[169:3:1] - The **Collector** held revenue, magisterial and police powers; revenue was collected **in cash**; hierarchy Collector → Tahsildar → village officers.
[169:3:2] - **Rajahmundry jail:** the old fort was converted into a jail in **1864** (made a Central Jail in 1870).
[169:3:3] ~~ Sources: NextGen modern India L3 Part 1 (src/ap-history/nextgen-modern-l3-01.txt) p.49; NextGen AP History Part 21 (src/ap-history/ap-history-appsc-21.txt) p.10, p.16; Rajahmundry jail: general knowledge, not checked
## SUB 4 | Economic Effects and Famines
[169:4:0] - Cash revenue demand → **commercial crops**: **tobacco in Guntur**, indigo, cotton (Ganjam 1865-66 famine followed the cotton boom of the American Civil War).
[169:4:1] - **Deindustrialisation:** duty-free British cloth ruined weavers – Visakhapatnam exports ₹7 lakh → ₹1 lakh by the 1830s; Machilipatnam dyed cloth, Eluru carpets, Kurnool blankets declined.
[169:4:2] TABLE head: Famine | Year | Note
  [169:4:2.0] Doji Bara (Skull) | 1791-92 | Madras region
  [169:4:2.1] Guntur (Nandana / Pedda Karuvu) | 1832-33 | ~1.5 lakh deaths; led to Dowleswaram
  [169:4:2.2] Ganjam (Orissa) | 1865-66 | after the cotton boom
  [169:4:2.3] Great Famine | 1876-78 | worst in the Ceded Districts
[169:4:3] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 21 (src/ap-history/ap-history-appsc-21.txt) p.5-6, p.9, p.17; NextGen modern India L2 Part 1 (src/ap-history/nextgen-modern-l2-01.txt) p.17; old app notes row 169 (sub 5, 6)
